The Wirtshaus Frau Huber is a rustic and cozy old-time inn. People go here to drink and eat. The service is very friendly, fast and attentive. It wasn't long before the glass was empty before people asked if they wanted anything else. Even when everyone was taken care of, people always asked if everything was okay. The food is adapted to the house and you get good, home-style food. The food came after a reasonable amount of time (about 10-15 minutes), was neatly prepared and tasted very good. There must be a reason why the economy was completely full on a Wednesday in January, every seat was full. You can go back here at any time, the inn is recommended.

Misaki is truly a hidden gem. The owners run this place as a family business and the service is impeccable, although it can get a bit slow at times since they put a lot of love into their food and everything is cooked to order. The variety of traditional Vietnamese dishes as well as other Asian cuisines is an interesting mix that should yield something for every taste. Even after they closed they helped us getting a taxi back to our hotel since our apps did not work, and they let us stay until the taxi arrived, even though it was getting very late. We can't thank them enough for their hospitality and will certainly return next time we're in Aachen.

The different flavors and spices presented in the starters took our taste buds on an exciting journey. Each dish was expertly prepared and had its own unique flavor. Our main course consisted of mantu, homemade dumplings, and qabuli palau, an Afghan national dish. The mantu were a real treat - the combination of tender meat and aromatic filling in the dumplings was simply delicious. The Qabuli Palau was equally impressive. The tender chicken side dish on the spicy rice was a poem for the palate. The price-performance ratio was excellent. Given the quality and generosity of the portions, you felt like you were in a real culinary paradise without putting too much of a dent in your wallet. The staff were extremely friendly and accommodating. Her enthusiasm for the kitchen and her willingness to advise us on the choice of dishes made our evening even more enjoyable. We are already looking forward to our next visit to this restaurant. If you are looking for authentic Afghan-Persian dishes in a warm atmosphere then this is definitely the place for you. Highly Recommended! We'll definitely come back.

I'll start by saying the food was absolutely beautiful, and quite tasty! We had a good meal and had some of the most creative looking dishes I've ever seen. That being said, this restaurant didn't live up to my expectations or the price point of a 2 star restaurant. My biggest complaint was probably the service. While the people who served us were very nice and I believe trying hard, I just don't think they were prepared for this serious of a meal. It made me wonder if they had new staff on the night we visited. One server broke a wine glass, another spilled a dish on someone's plate, and it felt like they were very nervous giving us our new cutlery. They would usually recite what was in the dish but we didn't get the passion or the knowledge I've come to expect from restaurants with even one star. The food tasted great, and looked really cool, but it didn't taste good enough to blow my mind and there isn't really a dish that even stands out to me now that was a clear winner. The main problem is that it's priced like a 2 star restaurant, so spending €300 euros on a meal that felt comparable to places that were €200 cheaper felt kind of bad, especially when the service felt like it did. I think the biggest tell though was that there were so many open tables in the restaurant. Every other restaurant with a star I visited has been a full dining room. Im wondering if this place has a lunch specialty and the dinner is maybe overlooked?

Great place for a relaxed lunch! The restaurant has a sort of urban oasis setting perched on an indoor garden rooftop. For lunch this allows for a very nice, airy setting. The lunch menu is a la carte, starting from two dishes at a fair 58 EUR. I took three dishes following a starter/main/dessert logic. The savoury dishes were well prepared and rock solid. Highlight was the playful dessert with the theme of mushrooms. I usually do not like gimmicky dishes, but this was really executed on a high, elaborate level. As often with entry level priced lunch menus I don't think the food fully represents the two awarded Michelin stars. Hence the full tasting menu might be the better choice to get the full picture of what the kitchen here is capable of.

I really cannot see how this place is ranked so high. While innovation in cooking is always welcome, my experience was less about culinary excellence and more about an overwhelming clash of flavors. The ambiance of the restaurant was indeed impressive, with a meticulously designed interior that promised a memorable dining experience. However, the promise of the decor was not matched by the food. The primary issue was the unbalanced and overpowering nature of the flavors. Each dish seemed to compete for attention with an excess of spices and seasoning, overshadowing the natural tastes and textures of the ingredients. It was evident that the chef was aiming for surprise and novelty, perhaps to cater to those unfamiliar with the nuances of Asian flavors. However, for someone who appreciates the subtlety and complexity of traditional Asian cuisine, the dishes felt overdone and lacking in harmony. The service was impeccable, with attentive staff who were knowledgeable about the menu. However, the focus on creating 'unexpected flavors' rather than harmonious and balanced dishes was a letdown. This restaurant might appeal to those seeking a novel culinary experience, but for connoisseurs of traditional Asian flavors, it might come across as trying too hard to impress.

I really cannot see how this place is ranked so high. While innovation in cooking is always welcome, my experience was less about culinary excellence and more about an overwhelming clash of flavors. The ambiance of the restaurant was indeed impressive, with a meticulously designed interior that promised a memorable dining experience. However, the promise of the decor was not matched by the food. The primary issue was the unbalanced and overpowering nature of the flavors. Each dish seemed to compete for attention with an excess of spices and seasoning, overshadowing the natural tastes and textures of the ingredients. It was evident that the chef was aiming for surprise and novelty, perhaps to cater to those unfamiliar with the nuances of Asian flavors. However, for someone who appreciates the subtlety and complexity of traditional Asian cuisine, the dishes felt overdone and lacking in harmony. Dear Tim Raue, Where to begin with this post? I vividly remember in 2018 sitting at the television in the living room of a home in Florida coming across your episode of Chef's Table on Netflix and upon starting it, I was instantly mesmerized with your restaurant, your food and with Berlin. I appreciated and connected with your story and felt so captivated learning about the winding road it took for you to open a 2-Star Michelin restaurant. That is all it took for me have the desire to experience Restaurant Tim Raue in person. And so, a couple of Fridays ago I finally did. It was better than anything I could have imagined. I was blown away by the service received at the restaurant from start to finish, as though everyone was moving in perfect harmony while playing a complex symphony. Upon being seated, we were tended to our every need and never felt neglected. I was looking forward to the menu being served and loved that I got a card outlining every single dish being presented that evening to me. Now, if we're taking food, I am so happy that I entrusted my palette to your kitchen. Every course was so perfectly presented and upon tasting it, I was met with a spectrum of flavors that worked so harmoniously well together. If I had to pick my favorite course, it would definitely be the Wasabi Langoustine. I had wanted to try it every since I saw it on Chef's Table and it was divine. I also tasted things I hadn't ever tried before, like imperial Caviar with sprat, which blew my mind with its umami flavor and wagyu beef cheek, which was braised to perfection. I really am so grateful to have had the privilege to dine at your restaurant. It is the single most memorable food experience I have ever had in my life and I will never forget how special I felt and how immaculate the food was. Please continue inspiring everyone at your restaurant to doing amazing work so that many more people can experience the unbridled joy I felt with every moment dining at Restaurant Tim Raue. With Gratitude, Dev.

A wonderful little place with reasonable prices and good service. Nem Ran - spring rolls Crispy spring rolls, stuffed with minced meat and vegetables. Served with mint and fish sauce. Very tasty. Ga Xien - Homemade marinated grilled chicken, served with peanut sauce. This dish was delicious too. The chicken was well made and juicy. Tom Chien Com - Fried shrimp wrapped in puffed rice. Served with homemade honey-chili mayonnaise. Today’s winning dish. The shrimp was well made (not like in many places, overcooked). The crispy puffed rice. The light and refreshing sauce. Everything was right about this dish. Pho Bo - Tasty Pho soup, with beef.. Bun Bo Nam Bo - Wonderful noodle dish with marinated beef. Light and tasty. The noodles are good, the sauce is not too strong. Great dish. Com Curry Vit - Rice dish with curry and crispy duck. It's hard to find a good curry, but it was a good one. For dessert we took Banh Chuoi Nep Nuong Fried banana, tapioca in coconut milk and peanuts. The dessert was disappointing. I have nothing bad to say about it, but neither anything good. it was ok. .The homemade lemonade is also nice Definitely recommend the place.

What a lovely evening we had! The restaurant has a beautiful modern yet relaxing interior, totally couldn’t tell when you pass by from the outside. We had the menu plus cheese plate with the wine paring, and we are glad about the choice. Chose this restaurant because of the newly Michelin star listing, and it definitely deserves the star. The flavor was overall balanced, and with some playful twists. At the amuse bouche, the freshness of cucumber with its marination made an interesting start. Then it went on with vegetables, fish and beef. And what a nice wagyu, the meat was literally melting at your tongue, and the fat was balanced with the acid from the ponzu and kimchi (although here I would say from my personal taste the kimchi could have been fermented a bit longer to lose its grassy/planty raw taste). Final dessert was not too sweet or heavy and a nice close to the main dinner. Funny that it seems Germans serve cheese plate after the dessert, but we enjoyed the choice of the cheese. Beside the food, the wine paring was phenomenal, the sommelier was nice to explain the details about the wines from their production, tasting palate and matching of the food. Most of the wines were German and we were surprised about their tastes. In summary we were satisfied with the wonderful dinner. One small suggestion, during the online booking, there was an area you could put “your reason” of the dinner reservation, and I put “birthday dinner”. Not sure if the restaurant had seen this information, and if there were a small gesture, even like a greeting of “happy birthday” would make us feel even more special.

While I'm tempted to give it a clean full score, there was one thing that put a bit of a damper on all of us (party of 5) at the very end of the dinner. First off I want to thank everyone involved for a really nice experience and excellent service. In addition I'd like to say that even as a predominantly non-wine drinker the pairings with each meal was fantastic. To the point where I outright enjoyed the combinations. The food journey from salty seafood to sweeter pastures with fruits, vegetables and gamy protein was fun and very tasty both in presentation, smell and taste. One of the highlights have to be said was the sauce we got with our main protein. It had layers of taste that just filled your mouth and kicked both the protein and wine pairing up to a wonderful wave of tastes and textures. However, the thing that brought us all down to earth rather hard after what was otherwise a fantastic discovery was the dessert (frozen, crushed brownie served in a reductionist fashion). While not bad by any means it didn't stand up to the rest. We were left with the impression that it may have been a dish made to salvage something rather than being something to finish off a thoughtful journey. At any normal dinner it would be alright, it was just such a stark contrast to everything else served this evening. Let me just finish by emphasizing that the entire experience as a whole was fantastic, especially considering the very generous pricing which should make this affordable for people to try such an experience. We may just have been a little unlucky with our dessert, so don't take it as me saying all desserts are bad; because the rest of the dishes showcases excellent craftsmanship and a passion for what they do. I would happily return and enjoy the experience again at a different visit to Berlin, so if anything I wholeheartedly recommend people to give the place a shot. Well worth the visit.

In addition I'd like to say that even as a predominantly non-wine drinker the pairings with each meal was fantastic. To the point where I outright enjoyed the combinations. The food journey from salty seafood to sweeter pastures with fruits, vegetables and gamy protein was fun and very tasty both in presentation, smell and taste. One of the highlights have to be said was the sauce we got with our main protein. It had layers of taste that just filled your mouth and kicked both the protein and wine pairing up to a wonderful wave of tastes and textures. However, the thing that brought us all down to earth rather hard after what was otherwise a fantastic discovery was the dessert (frozen, crushed brownie served in a reductionist fashion). While not bad by any means it didn't stand up to the rest. We were left with the impression that it may have been a dish made to salvage something rather than being something to finish off a thoughtful journey. At any normal dinner it would be alright, it was just such a stark contrast to everything else served this evening. Let me just finish by emphasizing that the entire experience as a whole was fantastic, especially considering the very generous pricing which should make this affordable for people to try such an experience. We may just have been a little unlucky with our dessert, so don't take it as me saying all desserts are bad; because the rest of the dishes showcases excellent craftsmanship and a passion for what they do. I would happily return and enjoy the experience again at a different visit to Berlin, so if anything I wholeheartedly recommend people to give the place a shot. Well worth the visit.

Quite a nice discovery in Schöneberg! It’s a new Michelin starred restaurant with a set 8-courses menu. The menu changes every 6 weeks and every dish is well thought, quite original and brings a lots of flavor between the spices, the bouillon, the sauces or espumas. I especially liked the cabbage which is the signature dish of the menu. Also I usually don’t like wine pairing I decided to go along this time and wasn’t disappointed. The sommelier (a she) talks with passion about her wine and I had nice surprises, from a Sauvignon blanc that had the strength of a Chardonnay aged in oak barrels to a Spanish Pinot noir that went super well with the beef dish. Totally recommend!

I highly recommend this place and would love to come back some day.

As for the meal, the food was delicious but unfortunately the portions were far too small. We were there with a larger group and almost everyone was still hungry afterwards. In my opinion, the prices here are already at a very high level: 8.50 euros for dessert and 18 euros for a gyro with fries. Unfortunately, nutritional intolerances are not addressed here, even though it is on the menu. I asked for lactose-free salad dressing and unfortunately we didn't get an answer. It's a shame that they didn't offer any vinegar oil dressing. The dishes that are supposed to be vegan are also not lactose free, so you wonder where they are vegan. The service: when we arrived we sat for a while until someone came to us and the waitress realized that we didn't have any tickets yet. They came pretty quickly. Unfortunately, it took an eternity until someone came again - in the whole time we had already picked out our food alongside the drinks. The food took so long that we had to ask in between. Then the food came and most people were disappointed by the size of the food. The mayonnaise that was ordered with the fries was also missing for 3 people. Before it came, the first ones had already eaten it. Unfortunately, there were far too few questions about drinks; we would have liked to drink more. In the end, we have always loudly drawn attention to ourselves with the glasses. Therefore the service is also poor. The ambience is cozy but if you linger long they don't close at 11.30pm. At around 10.10 we were asked to order the last round. A short time later they came and wanted to collect money. And shortly after 11:30 p.m. a gentleman came and finally asked us to leave. Sorry, gastronomy on a Saturday with a group that left several hundred euros there should be a friendlier farewell. Our conclusion: we as a group will not go here again. Dietary restrictions: Unfortunately it is not addressed at all

YamYam, a charming Korean restaurant in Berlin, offered a delightful dining experience on a busy weekday evening. Although reservations are recommended, we were lucky to get a table promptly. The service was quick and friendly, and the menu had an array of Korean delicacies. We tried the Veggie Bibimbap, a colorful rice bowl topped with sautéed veggies and a fried egg. The Nokdu Choen, a savory pancake with mung beans and vegetables, was crispy and satisfying. The Gimbap, resembling sushi rolls, pleased us with its fresh and crunchy vegetable fillings. To accompany our meal, we savored Ginger-flavored Kombucha, a refreshing fermented tea. Though slightly on the higher side, the prices were reasonable for the decent portions and quality offered. YamYam stood out for its extensive vegetarian options, making it a recommended destination for Korean cuisine lovers and vegetarians alike. Don't forget to bring your card for payment as they only accept card transactions.

One of the best veal schnitzels I've had, and not just in Berlin! The prices you pay are equivalent to those near Mitte, but the quality is tip-top and the portion size is much larger! I basically got two schnitzels for the price of one and I ate every last bite because it was fantastic. I washed it down with a Märzen (vom Fass) and even though I was stuffed, I'm a sucker for dessert and couldn't help but order the Kaiserschmarrn for two (to be fair, I had a date). And oh mein Gott was it worth needing to lie down afterward. It was one of the fluffiest, creamiest, most delicious Kaiserschmarrns I've had, and that's saying something. And they make it fresh, so do note that you need to give the server a heads up as it takes around 20m to make. Speaking of, the service is suuuper nice. They're very down-to-earth, friendly, mid-southern German-dialect-speaking ladies, including the owner Frau Nußbaumer! The only nitpick I have is that we had to sit near the bar where the service rushed in and out, but that's quite frankly my fault because I didn't make a reservation, which you'll definitely need on a Friday night. Overall, very happy with this place and it's definitely going on the list to visit again. Bis dann!

tl;dr Save your money and eat somewhere else. The worst Michelin star restaurant I've eaten at. 0. Incredibly rude waitstaff. As another reviewer mentioned they rudely called out how much we chose to tip, tell us 10% was "standard" (it's not), and then reiterate loudly the amount we were tipping. Constantly interrupted during the meal as well. 1. Poor juice pairings. Ex: A  cherry+coffee+chocolate juice was served as the pair to the main venison course. The coffee flavor was entirely overpowering instead of compliment the dish. Most juices were a similarly elaborate affair. 2. 6 course menu is more focused on being "complex" for the sake of complexity rather than flavorful. Also for leaning heavy into a Japanese 3. Hidden charges. The "welcome drink" offered is not part of the tasting menu and will cost you extra. Not to mention the gall to charge someone spending 200+ Eur/person on a meal an extra 10 Eur/person for water without listing it on the menu (or informing you). 5. Vegetarian substitutes were below par for a establishment of this caliber. 6. The views are really not as great as you might think. Only 3 of the tables have a view of the heart of the city (west) and the setting sun. All in all as someone who has eaten at many Michelin restaurants around the world I cannot reccomend this establishment. The food, drinks, and service are all lacking for the fine dining price point.

Decor and ambience reminds me of Alice in wonderland and or Peter Pan “fairy tale like.” The seating arrangement for 2 person if you like a view is against the lining of the window facing outwards (like in a cafe) as oppose to traditional two person  table top in the middle of the room. The kitchen was behind us with glass over so it was “open kitchen” concept and I love to observe the team as they were super focused. The staff does extremely well speaking in German and English. They were very personable and provided their favorite wines and were knowledgeable of their menu. Definitely Michelin worthy service. Each dish was presented with an attentive explanation. The menu i believe is fusion cuisine featuring molecular gastronomy. The “onsen egg.” was the star of the evening and also their chocolate at the end for dessert. I want to point out the wine menu is very unique and noteworthy due to the fact it features mainly wines from Germany and eastwards. We selected the Slovenian bottle that is only carried at this restaurant and it paired beautifully with the dishes. Highly recommend this bottle if you get a chance to try it.

We went here not knowing what to expect. It's far enough away from tourist areas to be legit but also right near a busy street. But the reviews looked good so we went for it. And man am I glad we did! There is wonderful seating right outside which is surprisingly peaceful for being so close to Schönhauser Allee, and the friendly service came to greet us. The menu is big with lots of temptations, but I took a gamble (because I don't normally eat fish as an entree) with the Schnitzel "Klement's" which is like a Cordon Bleu with lox, cheese, and pickles. Hooooly smokes, it was tasty! I was thoroughly impressed. While I was snarfing it down, my date also offered me some of her "normal" schnitzel, which was also delicious. Pro-tip: When you hear them *pounding* away in the kitchen after you order, you know you're getting fresh schnitzel. We were so stuffed after our schnitzels that we couldn't eat another bite. At least until the waitress informed us they had a Kaiserschmarrn-like dessert. I should note that it's not actually Kaiserschmarrn -- it's more of a powdered crepe with apple compote on the side, but it is just as delicious and I couldn't stop shoveling it into my mouth. Even though I needed to lie down afterward (or maybe because I needed to), this place is going on my list of top German spots in Berlin. Stop in and maybe you'll see me napping between meals!

I’m Going to tell you a story… in fact six stories. Meals happen every day. But an experience remains. We just had the most memorable meal of a life time. The last time my taste buds were tantalized like this, was in Venice when I was 12 years old and I enjoyed my first REAL dining experience. It began with a greeting from the kitchen consisting of an onion panna cotta. Now don’t ask me how you make onion panna cotta but it was glorious. The true essence of the onion was clear yet delicate. And the texture was mouth watering. Following this we had a smooth paprika soup. The Smokey taste of the paprika was combined excellently with the velvety soup. Next up was a crunchy fried piece of pig belly that made my mouth water. Combine with the Soya sesame reduction, I was immediately transported to cloud 9. As if things weren’t already good enough, we were then greeted by a piece of salmon with peas and asparagus. The fish melted in my mouth as it should, and the asparagus was cooked to perfection. The main course consisted of a piece of lamb back, with spinach, and potato gratin. The lamb could be cut like butter and was seasoned to perfection. The gratin was warm and soft on the inside, with a delicate crunch on the outside. By this point we were stuffed, but were greeted by the finale: a finely curated cheeseboard, along with a chocolate mousse with hard exeterior and hazelnut ice cream. They were the proverbial cherry on the cake. During our dining experience, we drank the accompaniment of wines that the team paired superbly with each course. I cannot speak highly enough of what Andre and his team are doing at Jungbluth. It is the epitome of fine dining, and they find the perfect balance between experimentation and traditional tastes: harmonious like a choir. Thank you!

The food tasted quite good, although the caprese appetizer could have been bigger, given the price. The pizza and the tagliatelle with salmon were both good. The reason for the 2 star rating is mainly the fact that both my friend and I had stomach problems for 2 days after our dinner at Il Nuovo Primo. We shared all of the dishes, so it’s hard to say exactly which dish it was. I think the food might have actually been fresh, but perhaps it was some bacteria due to lack of hygiene (the bathroom was rather filthy, for instance). In any case, I hope this was just a rare occurrence, but I would probably not risk returning to this restaurant.

Baan Sukhothai describes itself as a fine dining restaurant serving Thai cuisine. It is family run and very friendly. Unfortunately there was no service in our case, so that a completely full restaurant initially had to be served by just one person and later by two. I felt very sorry for both of them because there are a lot of tables to be served. The restaurant has a very special ambience and is furnished with great attention to detail. The menu offers many authentic Thai dishes. We chose a green curry and the fish - both dishes that were not marked as spicy. Both dishes were tasty, but so borderline spicy that you had to happily resort to the jasmine rice. So if you don't like spiciness, you should be warned to ask the waitress about it ;) We'd love to come back - maybe we'll have a bit more luck with the staff situation. Parking: There are a few parking spaces directly in front of the restaurant and a few further back. Otherwise you can park on the street in the parallel streets at the back

I was here on vacation with my fiancée to celebrate our engagement with a candelight dinner. And all I can say is that the evening was amazing and the best restaurant experience of my life so far. We received a very friendly welcome, the atmosphere in the restaurant is extremely cozy and inviting and the private room by the fireplace was very comfortable. A bouquet of our favorite flowers and a unique greeting card were prepared on the table. The menu was presented to us personally by the chef and the food itself was excellent, as was the drink accompaniment. During the course of the evening, the extremely charming Marius played the piano and entertained the guests with a little quiz if they wanted. At the end our song was played and a small sparkler was lit for dessert. I can't say anything more about it because the experience was so perfect overall that it's extremely difficult to put it into words. There was a high level of professionalism on the part of the staff and a certain professional distance on the one hand, but at the same time it felt like you were staying with friends. I can only recommend everyone to come here once and we are already looking forward to doing it again!

This small, nice restaurant run by a Vietnamese family is located in Haaren at the exit from Jülicherstrasse to Haaren. You shouldn't expect perfection in service, but you should expect cordiality. You shouldn't expect speed, but a meal with fresh ingredients and rich in taste. You shouldn't expect the perfect ambience, but naturalness and a touch of your heart. Take your time, peace and serenity and you will be in a place where time and hectic are transformed into the anticipation of enjoying a good meal. When you make a reservation, you come to a place that welcomes you, even if you have to wait a while for a drink and good food because the restaurant is full. Don't take anyone's offense, just be happy to be there! Welcome to Vietnamese Japanese fusion cuisine. Experience the freshness and stay calm. Vegetarian options: There are vegetarian dishes, but remember Asians know meatless because they can't afford it, but many Asians love meat because it's rarely on the table. Here you can experience Asia at the holiday table when there is something to celebrate. Kid-friendliness: Children are welcome, but please bring a game for the child to make the wait entertaining.

Nice and polite service. The place is a simple Indian restaurant, we tried the chicken 65, which can be really delicious, and the samosa as starters. As main dish we both took the chicken tikka masala, as the owner recommended it as very flavoured. Naan bread as well. The chicken 65 was not crunchy and tasty as it should be, it felt like it was not freshly done.It was also an extremely small portion for its price. The samosa was just one, it is usually 2 pieces. It was covered with chickpeas but not really flavoured. Finally the chicken tikka was too plain, really nothing special. The naan was just ok. Overall, all we got was just average with prices a bit above average. 1 star less for the high prices, especially for the extremely small starters, and 2 stars less for the little flavour of their meals. It's really hard to find a decent Indian restaurant in Berlin. I'd love to give them more stars but unfortunately I don't think I will consider visiting this restaurant anytime soon, considering this not-great experience and the wide selection in Berlin of other Indian places. My quest to find in Berlin decent Indian restaurants, comparable to UK standards, is still open!

Really excellent Asian inspired food in modern setting. Service a bit rushed and not the best but understandable as we booked the last spot at 2130, so it wasn't far off the kitchen closing. I would recommend maybe limiting reservations to 21:00 for people to actually get the full experience. We had a 6 course version of the 8 course tasting menu with two of the paired wines, a crémant to start and an espresso at the end of our meal. The food was all excellent. With the 6 courses the dessert we finished on was good but would have been better followed by the actual final strawberry dessert that we didn't get to chance to try. The appetisers / amuse bouche we're brilliant. There is a focus on mushrooms on the menu which we really enjoyed and is done well. Sea bass was very high quality and the dash with it had great flavour. The following courses were all excellent, although for me personally the mushroom French toast course's yuzu miso sauce was a little overpowering for the other flavours to come through. Octopus course was great, but they sent out the takoyaki very hot (and warned us) but again we were there at the end of the night so understand a bit of a rush on our food. The beef course was incredible. Perfect texture and temperature of the beef with accompanying sauces. Curd/courgette flower deep fry was nice but also a bit too hot with a rush on our meal. The dessert we had, soybean based with a meringue was nice but missing a fresh element to finish on as we had our final course dropped with the late service. They also served an umeboshi and caramel filled chocolate at the end, like petit fours. Great combo of flavours. Espresso was also great quality coffee. Decent value for money when considering fine dining in Berlin. Expensive essentially. We paid €330 between 2. Water is charged at €5 a head. €330 covered water, 5 glasses of different wine (€8-13 a glass), and two 6-course tasting menus (€118 each). The 8-course is €138 per person with €10 off for any course you don't want. I would say 6 courses is enough to be full, for balance of the menu and value all 8 courses would be the best deal. Worth it if you're able to get there for 2100 at the latest. They probably shouldn't offer a 2130 seating if they only serve a tasting menu, or should certainly have a disclaimer when booking, about the number of courses and service may be affected. Food was really well done overall. Nice modern setting, well lit by tables but still feels pretty cosy. Service is polite. Vegetarian options: There is a vegetarian tasting menu also.

I would recommend maybe limiting reservations to 21:00 for people to actually get the full experience. We had a 6 course version of the 8 course tasting menu with two of the paired wines, a crémant to start and an espresso at the end of our meal. The food was all excellent. With the 6 courses the dessert we finished on was good but would have been better followed by the actual final strawberry dessert that we didn't get to chance to try. The appetisers / amuse bouche we're brilliant. There is a focus on mushrooms on the menu which we really enjoyed and is done well. Sea bass was very high quality and the dash with it had great flavour. The following courses were all excellent, although for me personally the mushroom French toast course's yuzu miso sauce was a little overpowering for the other flavours to come through. Octopus course was great, but they sent out the takoyaki very hot (and warned us) but again we were there at the end of the night so understand a bit of a rush on our food. The beef course was incredible. Perfect texture and temperature of the beef with accompanying sauces. Curd/courgette flower deep fry was nice but also a bit too hot with a rush on our meal. The dessert we had, soybean based with a meringue was nice but missing a fresh element to finish on as we had our final course dropped with the late service. They also served an umeboshi and caramel filled chocolate at the end, like petit fours. Great combo of flavours. Espresso was also great quality coffee. Decent value for money when considering fine dining in Berlin. Expensive essentially. We paid €330 between 2. BLESS Restaurant, located at Hausvogteiplatz 10 in Berlin, has received mixed reviews. While the restaurant has a pleasant atmosphere and is aesthetically pleasing, the overall dining experience can be underwhelming. The restaurant is known for its visually appealing dishes, making it popular on Instagram. However, the reality can be a bit different. Despite the good looks, the food itself is rather mediocre and simple. Some standout dishes include their truffle dishes and seafood offerings, but generally, the menu doesn’t quite live up to the visual hype. One notable downside is the cleanliness of the restaurant. The menus are often sticky from previous customers, suggesting they haven’t been cleaned in quite some time, which is a basic yet important aspect of restaurant hygiene. The location of the restaurant is not particularly central or interesting, which might be a consideration for some diners. Moreover, the service, while generally polite, can be slow, affecting the overall dining experience. Overall, BLESS Restaurant is a decent spot if you’re looking for a nice atmosphere and good photo opportunities, but it might not satisfy those seeking exceptional food and impeccable service.

Quaint basement grill house with excellent food. Gazpacho appetizer was cool and refreshing with vibrant tomato taste, the slight crunch of the cucumber garnish was a great touch. Steak was cooked perfectly, and the accoutrements were top-notch as well. Glass of Malbec wine was complex and rich, pairing perfectly with the steak. Wonderful bar and open grill really added to the cozy vibe. A bit cramped with no outdoor seating. It's a basement with winding staircases, so low-mobility diners should look elsewhere. Service was attentive and friendly. English menu was available. Reservation recommended, as the place was mostly full at 19:30. Gazpacho was fairly priced, but wine glass and the steak dinner were a bit expensive. Worth it for a splurge meal. Highly recommend this steakhouse! Take a walk around the gorgeous Bonn Botanical Garden to work up an appetite. Bus stop to Bonn HBF is right across the street. Wheelchair accessibility: Not for wheelchair-bound diners. Very cozy and authentic place. Unfortunately in the basement without natural light, but with a nice Argentinien flair. The food is perfect. My preferred steak house in the Bonn area. The meat is grilled always to the point on an open pit with charcoals. But also the salads and the sides are really fresh and tasty. My favourite is the Chimichurri. An tomato based dip that can be served as a starter with bread, but also as a dipping sauce for meat. Please also give the green Chimichurri a try. If you don't need to drive, there also a good selection of south American red wines available. 5 stars...

As a Vietnamese person judging Vietnamese food in a foreign country, I think the dishes I had here were quite good and made right, though it is hard to demand solid authenticity in an international setting. And the presentation was nice. Bún Bò was delicious: beef was cooked right, sauce was balanced. Vermicelli was tougher than in Vietnam, but it was not a big problem. Vegetables were made a bit differently to adapt to the taste of local people, but they were in good harmony with the dish. Gà Rôti was a bit foreign to me. It was not excellent according to my taste, due to the lack of depth in flavors and aroma, but still enjoyable, with a wide range of greens. I preferred Bún Bò though. The chefs communicated in Vietnamese, I felt as if I were in Vietnam in that atmosphere. Felt so good to see Vietnamese people doing so so well in a foreign country ❤️

Unfortunately I have to give this three stars :-( the atmosphere is really nice. FYI: the sanitary facilities are currently being renovated, there is a toilet truck outside. Service was also friendly, mostly on point. Regarding the food: unfortunately it was almost a complete failure. The appetizer platter was fine. The homemade bread was really the highlight of the evening. The tomato salad was ok, oil, vinegar, pepper and salt were available separately for seasoning. The main courses did not convince us at all, on the contrary, some of them were not edible. We had pasta with beef fillet (which was super overcooked and dry) and chanterelles (you couldn't eat them because they were completely swollen with water, rubbery and tasted like nothing). The pasta was completely drowned in ok sauce. Then we had fresh filled pasta also with beef (same texture) and a tomato sauce. This was completely tasteless and not cooked properly, as it was still very sour, just like you would expect from a can of pureed tomatoes. We were really very disappointed here, as we are experienced visitors to Italian restaurants and wanted to make the trip to Beuel. When making the selection in Bonn, we don't know whether we will manage to give a second chance, so the first impression actually has to be right...

The best Indian restaurant in Cologne? No! It’s the best Indian restaurant in my life! Since I’m a vegetarian and a spicy food lover, I eat Indian food often. But this place is the very best food so far in my life!! We first went to this place in February or March this year, and now almost have their food every 2 weeks - 1 month. They deliver without any extra cost within 4 km, so if you live not so far, you can call and order by phone. Their Mango sauce is fantastic so as their Mango lassi. The Art India antipasti set is also nice if you are a fan of fried stuffs. Their soup and rice never fail, overall, everything they make is extremely nice and heavenly!! My recommendation (what I always order) is menu “31” with extra spicy.... muah, it’s out of this world.. What’s menu 31? Check by yourself in their menu😉 ... Forgot to write about the staff!! Very nice and friendly! Once I even forgot my phone at the place (food was too tasty and I was almost dead) and the guy came to the street and handed it to me.

Really very good Indian restaurant for the people staying near to Merheim. The taste I found here seems more authentic than other restaurants that are in Neumarkt. Chicken biryani, Chicken Tikka and Lamb Tikka masala is a must try from this restaurant. The speciality of this restaurant is that the spiciness is added based on what you ask for. Unlike other restaurants adding chilli powder for the dishes to make it more spicy... These people definitely add a few authentic spices to make it spicy as we do in India. Overall it was a nice experience! Kindly note that sometimes the restaurant will be crowded and it's expected to book you table and visit it!

Lovey food and ambience at this slightly out-of-centre take on an Austrian hilltop brasserie in a leafy suburban setting. A 15-minute walk from central station you enter a different vibe - more residential, perhaps a uni quarter, and quieter than the city centre hubbub. The leafy terraces surrounding the restaurant add to the oasis-in-a-city vibe while the interior is a modern take on alpine hotel meets hotel library. Food was hands-down excellent. It was a light and refined take on classic dishes, with a real pride in the ingredients - all showing up in the taste. We had the 6 course tasting menu and it was a mix of surprises and pleasure at the interpretation of things we thought we knew. The service was fantastic with the waiter covering wine, food history and any else with a real humour. Prices surprised us as being on the cheaper side of expectation give the quality. Worth a detour from the city centre for.

Greatly enjoyed my dining experience at CARUSO Pastabar during a recent visit to Germany. As an English-speaker, I was able to dine without any major issues which is always welcoming to see. I was treated a little differently but it was acceptable. The food was delicious and I am glad I selected the 3-course meal option. The only minor issue I encountered was with the water situation, as I was surprised to see myself being charged for water that was presented as being from tap (not sparkling or still). When ordering I requested tap and it arrived in a jug that I assumed would be tap. Nonetheless, I would certainly recommend a visit to CARUSO as either a local or visitor to Cologne.

restaurant_name: Govardhan- Pure Vegetarian and Vegan Restaurant
description: Favorite Vegetarian/Vegan Restaurant!! If you are looking for authentic homestyle Indian food then this is the right place! Nostalgia hit hard the moment I took the first bite of Dal and Rice. I have eaten at various places in NRW region but have never come across such a nice nice and warm "homestyle" Indian restaurant. If you're reading this, please visit this place and try the "all you can eat" buffet priced at 14€ (weekends). The owner is a very friendly person and serves food as if he's doing a "service to the society". This Indian gesture is reminiscent of my home. Regarding the food, it is a great bargain to eat such healthy and nutritious food as much as you want for 14€ (on weekdays, it is around 10€). All of it is very delicious! I took 3 servings of almost everything and ate to my heart's delight. They accept EC cards ONLY along with cash (bargeld). Shower some love to this place coz I feel it is very underrated. As an Indian, I feel this is a hidden gem. P.S - If you're a vegan or vegetarian, this place is truly a blessing. Vegetarian options: Everything is Vegetarian and stuff that is vegan is clearly mentioned.

restaurant_name: Govardhan- Pure Vegetarian and Vegan Restaurant
description: Good food, the only problem I have is with the authenticity. Very, very homely taste, reminded me a bit of home. Ordered a Day menu, which came with a dal makhni, which wasn't truly a dal makhni, rather mixture of other lentils, the second dish was a subzi, which would still pass as a subzi, the raita was alright, roti authentic, very very home-like, and the kheer was also good but too sweet for my liking. The pricing overall was pretty good. All of this was 8,90€. If you want to eat something which is close to what people cook in India, this place is recommended. Not a place for authenticity purists though.

So worth it IMO

The food is amazing.  Creative dishes and really an experience. However, I would NOT recomment this restaurant because of various reasons. First, the wine pairing €120,- for 7 wines and a small glass of Kölsch beer is ridiculous. They don't even serve whole glasses, more like half gasses/tasting glasses. This isn't the ** Michelin star experience you'd expect. Yes the wines came from different regions in the world, but if you can't pour a normal glass, then go for cheaper wines that would also go with the dishes. Don't skimp on wine. Or, don't aks a ridiculous price for the pairing. Second, the 15 courses aren't really 15 courses. Some were one biters and in my opinion don't count as a course. And as a Michelin star restaurant, you can't not have a winepairing with some of the dishes. We thought we would get 8 wines with 15 dishes and that some dishes would be accompanied by the same wine. It's not. There are a few courses where they don't serve anything. Like what? Third, it was a loooooooong night. We sat for 5,5 hours for 15 dishes. That is way to long and there were times we had to wait a very long time for the next course to come. At a ** star restaurant I expect the kitchen to be fully choreographed and smooth running from beginning till the end with little waiting time in betweeb courses. Also the chairs are not too comfortable, so 5,5 hours is a loooong time. Lastly the price for a bottle of water, €13,- per bottle of San Pelegrino. Like, are the insane?! They keep on pooring, not asking if you want another bottle. In the end we had to pay €39 for 3 bottles of San Pelegrino. I have no words.. We left the restaurant feeling very disappointed and robbed of our money. I don't mind paying for food and drinks, but we had better at soo many * star restaurants and even non star restaurants. So Ox & Klee is a big no no for me.

This was our 3rd time at Ox&Klee, every time we go we think we know what to expect. But it really is an „experience tasting“, every time is so different, each course is mind blowingly tasty and surprising. What we love most about this place is that you can let them know up front what foods you don’t like, they accommodate any wishes without being annoyed about it. I opted for first time for fully vegeterian to be on the safe side and I do not miss out on the different tastes and textures that are designed for everyone else. The wine accompanied has been chosen carefully and works perfectly. Last but not least, the staff is delightful and this place is just so open minded for being so „posh“. Simply can only love.

I'm sharing two different experiences, one before the ownership changed and one after. June 2022- we hosted our wedding dinner here with about 35 guests. The booking process was very good. We called and then made an appointment to come in to discuss the menu. We were given wine to taste and were told of the different menu options. We went for a 4 course meal, only 49€ per guest! It was a ton of food. Tolle Preis-Leistungsverhältnis 😉 Food and drink: Antipasti plate for EACH guest, two tastings of pasta, one main course (fish or beef), and one dessert (choice of tiramisu, chocolate mousse, or Panna Cotta). I can't remember if wine and beer was included in the price or not or an add on to our package. Anything that wasn't wine, beer, or a soft drink was the guests responsibility. I think we had two different wine options, one red and one white. At some point they started serving a sweet wine which was not what we chose, that was a little disappointing. Otherwise the food and drinks were phenomenal! Service/ambiance: it was a Saturday at 18;30 and the place was PACKED. I was honestly disappointed that they took so many reservations when they knew there was a wedding. We could barely hear each other and it was the end of June and it got uncomfortably hot inside the restaurant with it completely full. We finally asked them to turn on the air conditioner after we realized we couldn't open all the windows. It took a long time to cool down so most people were outside in between courses. It was THAT hot inside. Also we had to wait an hour before getting ANY food. Even bread. That was not acceptable. Probably because they were so full. Otherwise the service was friendly, when they came around. June 2023- I was surprised to learn that they changed ownership, but the quality of the food has luckily stayed the same. It was absolutely delicious! Service was very friendly and attentive and we had a nice seat outside. I also had some nice prosecco and wine. They unfortunately did not have or know what port wine was, even though it was on the menu. Regardless, it was a lovely time. Bottom line, I can recommend visiting this place. We had a wonderful wedding celebration here! Definitely try the Antipasto Della Casa and I can very much recommend their fresh grilled fish.

The first time I tried Setzkasten was during lockdown for their takeaway menu. It was spectacular and so much fun, but going in person was truly an experience. The service is fantastic, not pretentious at all like many Michelin star restaurants, friendly, warm, welcoming and informative. The chef's table was wonderful, watching the detail going into prep was fantastic, such a calm organised environment. The food was beautiful. The attention to detail, texture and taste was second to none. What really stood out were the additional touches. The smoked creme fraiche with choux pastry with craquelin was absolutely spectacular and the butters were sublime. Every course was exceptional and the accompanying wine paired perfectly with each one. Personally I found dessert a little disappointing, as if they don't have a pastry chef and a regular chef made dessert. It was fine, just didn't have the same flair as the other courses and I remember thinking the same when we got the takeaway menu. Overall an incredible experience, we will definitely be back.

Overall, it was a great experience from the time I entered the restaurant until I left.  I started with a nice glass of Tattinger Champaign and had the opportunity to chat with "the Duchy," who is the well styled hostess.  She explained the ideas and history behind the restaurant theme. It was a nice conversation, and as I was dining alone, welcomed.  They start the service by bringing out two types of bread with salted butter.  Both breads were nice - potato bread and bread with apple and black pudding (sausage).  I selected the steak tartar as my  starter. The meat was very good quality, and the mix of ingredients was tasty. For the main course, I chose the beef rib, which was accompanied by a tomato salad. The steak was very well cooked and  seasoned - which was a first for me in Germany.  For the desert,  it was black cherries with a warm chocolate cake and sunflower ice cream. All was good, especially the ice cream.  This restaurant is expensive and a bit of an indulgence,  but it used local top quality ingredients and was exceptional. I would certainly recommend it.

Fine dining at its best! A reason to visit Dusseldorf again. We made an online reservation in advance, where we mentioned our dietary restrictions & food allergies. The moment we entered the restaurant, we were welcomed by Mr. Urs, who knew our exact preferences as if we had been friends for life. It's plausible that the Duchy follows the farm-to-table concept focusing on sustainability. Like Jamie Oliver says: "Real food doesn't have ingredients. Real food is ingredients." Mr. Urs helped us choose the best courses and drinks. I'm on medication (nothing serious) and should avoid alcohol for some time, therefore I had to abstain from having a glass of wine. It wasn't a problem for Mr. Urs. He offered a lovely alternative to wine: some fancy ice tea that looked like wine and had a very delicate taste. The Homegrown Potato Soup, as well as Handmade Tagliarini and Regional Salmon Trout are what we enjoyed the most. Refreshing sorbet was the final act of the evening. All we can say is Thank You and we'll be back again.

First of all: it is absolutely important to book a table. We read about it on the internet, but thought that if we got there at 6 p.m. it would work. "Pustekuchen" At 6 p.m. there were no tables left for us. Since many restaurants here are only open on weekends in the low season, but we wanted to eat pizza, we decided to order a pizza to take away. This place reminds me of my friend's Korean grandmother's home cooking.  Since I've moved away from them, I've had Korean food many times, but there was always something missing, like it was "restaurantified." This is the first time in 20 years that I had food that reminded me of those good times.  This is Korean home cooking at its finest.  It really is like having your buddy's oma cook you a meal, and in that sense I think it's one of a kind here in Düsseldorf. To all those are Gusan:  thank you for the amazing meal and the trip down memory lane.  This is one I will remember. PS.  I had the kimchi and pork belly spicy stir fry, and my wife had the japchae.  They were both amazing, so amazing that we forgot to take pictures and dug in.

I was here a long time ago. Somehow I forgot this little gem. Fortunately, my friend wished to have Korean food and I didn't want to bore her with the same restaurants again. There came Gusan back to my mind. Gusan stands on the quieter side of the Stresemann Straße. The sign is written in classic korean calligraphy, which gives a hint of authenticity. The layout inside the restaurant is simple and clean. Some may not like the lightly clustered feeling, but it is what makes it Korean. The restaurant offers home-style Korean food. The menu is brief but sufficient. You won't be trapped in decision-making. At the same time, you choices are not compromised. You can choose from different meat, seafood and vegetables in forms of soup and stir-fry in different levels of spiciness. The service is spotless. A waitress stopped us from ordering a side dish that we would get from a main dish combo anyways. The lady cook consulted us if the main dishes should be served before she did it. By leaving, the lady even held the door open for us. If you crave for some authentic hearty Korean food, Gusan is the place to go. I can only recommend it. P.S. we've ordered too much food than we could eat. Eyes are always bigger than stomach. I have to apologize for the food waste. I'd be more considerate  next time.

It's a bit loud and warm. The decoration is a bit kitschy. (Candles still wrapped on the shelf) But super nice, huge aquarium and great (very large) cherry blossom decorations. Super nice tables. Unfortunately there is no decent cloakroom (although there is room in the small anteroom) and one corner looks a bit wild. Not particularly nice. There are all sorts of things lying around there, menus, cutlery, etc. Many restaurants have corners like this, but you could put a table or a standing desk with a telephone and drawers at the bottom - then the paying customer won't see it that way... Service is extremely good, very courteous and attentive. The older lady alone is a bit taciturn, which seems unfriendly. She hardly reacts to what is said, everyone else is very nice. The food, especially the noodles and sushi, are delicious. The coriander wasn't too much. Very pleasant. But the most delicious thing were the wontons. (Minced meat) Nice and crispy and spicy. We go out to eat a lot and we already know something and these wontons were the best so far! Drinks: Mango lassi and lychee juice are highly recommended! The food is plentiful and beautifully presented. The drinks come very quickly. Under 2 minutes, even if the restaurant is crazy full. We recommend Sakana! Parking: It's in the city center! But there are paid parking spaces a few meters away. Come on foot, by bike or by public transport! Kid-friendliness: There is hardly any space for strollers and I didn't see any high chairs.

🍣 Food good, ambience ok, service needs improvement! The food was really tasty, the price was like that of all the other adjacent sushi bars. The service wasn't the best. We were asked too often if everything was okay and if we wanted to order anything else. Either you really wanted to sell me something or get rid of us. We then urgently discussed that we didn't want to order anything else and just have a quiet chat. It should be noted that we still had something to drink. So we didn't block the space for other guests. There were also several free places left. The ambience is good, the aquarium is an eye-catcher and you can also sit outside. There are two floors with enough space. Unfortunately, next to the entrance was the cash register and a storage area for chairs and the menu. It was total chaos! The chairs just stood there with no structure and there were a few menus here and there. Regarding the menu, I would like to mention that it was very simple. The pages were not laminated and already felt very dirty. Some images were inserted with very poor image editing skills. Prices were simply written over with ballpoint pen. It's a shame I didn't take any pictures of them, you'll have to see with your own eyes, so unprofessional! Important note: No card payment possible! As with most Asian restaurants, card payment is not possible here, which is annoying for customers but an advocate for possible tax evasion. Would I recommend the restaurant to you? NO My advice: Opposite, less than 30 meters, is Bay's - Asianfood & Sushi, you can also get sushi there, the service and the ambience are much better.

restaurant_name: Da Michele Dresden Ristorante · Pizzeria · Osteria
description: My favorite restaurant in Dresden. The food is always tasty and delicious. The service is great, they are friendly, polite and they always have good suggestions about wine. We take all our friends who are visiting Dresden there. And all of them are amazed with the food! By the way, don’t forget to taste their marinated olives! I suggest reserving a table as well if you wanna have dinner between 6-8 p.m. If you are going later than 8 p.m., you don’t have to worry about finding a spot. If you are vegetarian and you are looking for a light tasty pasta, my suggestion would be Ali Ortolana. I have to stop writing at some point otherwise I would have listed the rest of the menu too! Oooo, try the Pomodoro soup too!!!

Absolutely exquisite meal. Everything was perfect. The service was friendly, finely coordinated and professional. The communication and precision was an absolute pleasure to experience and observe. The food was sublime. From the amuse bouche to dessert, everything was perfectly seasoned and an exceptional blend of taste and texture. The 4 course tasting menu was excellent value at 99 euro and the wine pairing was a very reasonable 25 euro and paired expertly. A rich Malbec to go with the lamb, a flinty Grüner Veltliner to go with the Arctic Char, a delightful Italian dessert wine and a beautiful Grau Begründer that perfectly cut the richness of the quail breast. One of the best meals we've had in Germany. The restaurant was so impressive. Lots of large parties in, yet it ran such a tight coordinated ship an embodiment of the German efficiency we were promised when moving here, but had yet to find. A truly exceptional experience, we will definitely be back.

I had the opportunity to share a wonderful dinner with a few colleagues at Ferrucci's. What made the night worth remembering wasn't only the delicious food and excellent wine, but Luca, the waiter and his fantastic way of describing the food and constantly referencing Piemonte. "In Piemonte, where I come from..." This was my first encounter with Pheasant tartar; if I didn't know, I would say it was beef. I liked the Tuna tataki, with black pepper from South America and excellent wasabi. The Tomahawk steak was lovely, but even better was the side dish, truffle-filled Agnolotti ("Piemonte style mini ravioli"). The Cassata wasn't the best, and I probably could have done without the banana chips decoration on the starter. On the other hand, the Marolo Grappa, made from Barolo grapes, was memorable. If I get a chance, I will visit Ferrucci's again!

But they never even apologised for the long wait. They didn’t even smile. when I arrived, the front man just looked at me… stone face… so i smiled and said i’m here 10mins early for our table reservation. he looked at his book… couldn’t find us. then i decided to show him the screen shot of our booking confirmation. he then asked if i had booked online… then he just walked away and started to prepare an empty table for us. i waited at the table for my friends to arrive. during this time… no menu not even asking me if I’d like a drink. interior is clean. Bathroom floor is very sticky. But they packed too many tables in the dining space which results in you invading everyone’s personal space if you want to stand up and head to the bathroom or bar. While we waited for 2 hours for our food, they didn’t even tend our table. Just left the starter dishes piled in the centre of the table. I would have given a positive review, if it wasn’t for their lack of friendliness. and unapologetic attitude. My advise for other potential customers… avoid saturday nights… they can’t handle it. or if that’s when you want to go, then expect a long wait and to be ignored by staff that have forgotten how to be smiling humans. When a new arrival is waiting for the rest of the group (we were 4ppl) to arrive, ask them if they’d like a drink while they wait. Maybe get some more staff… ? If this feels too much to ask… try placing the tables a bit more spread out so that guests don’t have to feel like they have to invade neighbouring tables when standing up. And no I’m not overweight. I’m 186cm and 86kg. I’d come again if I knew these improvements have been applied.

Traditionally furnished Greek restaurant with typical Greek meat dishes and friendly, attentive staff. The four prepared dishes and three starters were of a fair size and at a fair price. Unfortunately, my moussaka and the garlic bread (similar to bruschetta) were not typically spicy and there was a bit too little eggplant for my taste, but the fried anchovies (see photo) were great and the other two grill plates are also a great portion. Unfortunately, it was a bit noisy due to a larger company and it was no longer possible to refill drinks at an advanced hour. Since I didn't visit the toilets or the beer garden, I'm reserving one star for that.

1. The food is good enough for me to have a business dinner. It is not a wow but Frankfurt is not the peak of gourmet, literally everyone can start a restaurant on the level of Asian street food. 2. I asked my client to go to this restaurant for dinner on Sunday. It was crowded in the end of this L shape restaurant. A group of 20 people soaked the oxygen out of the end of the L thus it was hot and sticky air. We moved to opposite of the bar - with time it became better and I suspect the air conditioning does not work properly, in May it is still acceptable. 3. The petite service girl was attentive, and maybe a bit too attentive - we were there about 1.5 hours and she came four times to ask whether we need more, whether we finished our plates, etc. This is a sign for restaurants to shush away customers. 4. we paid for sea weed and a bowl and a curry plus a 1-litre water plus a limo and Coke Zero for 61 euro roughly. For business meals on Kaiserstr. it was fine - yet I would not go there for hungry tummy. Overall, it was a decent dinning experience though due to the annoying over-friendly asking, I would honesty 3 stars. Service at restaurants may want to go for a patience, and manner training, because these confusing service practices are getting common I guess due to lack of trained staff.

I would not recommend the course menu but sticking to the sushi.

A recent dining experience at Ariston Restaurant left me with mixed feelings, as the establishment presented a striking contrast between its remarkable culinary offerings and its woefully inadequate service. Allow me to share my thoughts on this intriguing dining experience. Ambiance (4/5): The restaurant's ambiance was pleasant, with tasteful décor, dim lighting, and a cozy atmosphere that exuded a sense of sophistication. It set the stage for what promised to be a memorable meal. Service (2/5): Unfortunately, where Ariston Restaurant fell drastically short was in the service department. Our initial impression was not promising, as it took an uncomfortably long time for a server to acknowledge our food was ready, it took over 1 hour for the mains. Throughout the evening, the waitstaff seemed overburdened and disorganized, leading to lengthy delays in taking orders, food, and providing basic attentiveness. Multiple requests for refills and condiments were forgotten or ignored, and the overall service experience left much to be desired. Food (5/5): On a brighter note, the food at Ariston Restaurant was undeniably exceptional. It's evident that the kitchen is staffed by talented chefs who take great pride in their craft. Beverages (3/5): The beverage selection at Ariston Restaurant was adequate, but not particularly noteworthy. The wine list was decent, offering a range of options to complement the meal, but it didn't stand out as extraordinary. Price (3/5): While the food quality warranted the price range, it's hard to justify the cost when the service experience was so lacking. Dining at Ariston Restaurant is an investment, and it's disappointing that the service did not match the prices. In summary, Ariston Restaurant is a place of culinary excellence with a glaring Achilles' heel - its service. The remarkable food alone may be enough to draw patrons back, but the frustrating and disjointed service experience undoubtedly taints the overall dining journey. If the restaurant can address its service issues, it has the potential to become a true dining destination for those seeking gourmet cuisine. Until then, diners should be prepared for a culinary rollercoaster of delights and disappointments.

Cozy restaurant with tasty traditional Ethiopian food. We had a mixed Demera platter and Ye Doro Wet (Alicha) with injera (it was an all gluten free choice). The food is eaten by hand and can be served seperately or as a shared platter. We choose the latter. The food is freshly prepared. Our server was a very kind and happy woman who left no questions or requests unanswered. The coffee was excellent as well, I absolutely recommend to try some! Also, the prices were very fair and the hygienic facilities were clean. We are looking forward to our next visit there! Vegetarian options: There is a range of vegetarian dishes, most are cale and/or lentil based. As we had some to try on the mixed platter, we can definitely say that they're tasty! Also, I normally dislike cale but here I liked it a lot.

The food is very delicious, the service is top friendly, and the price is cheaper than the others. I also like it that we can be quite flexible with the menu and have certain requests that are happily fulfilled by the kitchen. If you come here, go at lunch time during the weekdays, they have cheap lunch options. Vegetarian options: They are quite flexible with vegetarian options. For example I wanted a korma dish with paneer but it was not on the menu and they happily made it for me. I find this great! I can completely recommend Shalimar as your go-to Indian restaurant in Flensburg as vegetarian :)

We were satisfied so far. The food was delicious, there is still room for improvement! However, I don't expect it to be any different here. Since the plates are relatively small, the chef has little opportunity to serve properly. Service was attentive and there was also a saying that lightened everything up. We will definitely come back. We didn't have dessert but I have to say that I found the prices for the sundaes very high and I don't need a huge sundae after the meal. After dinner we had a cappuccino, my husband liked it, but it was too thin for me. However, I also prefer strong ones that still taste like coffee. Barrista Cappuccino from the Italian. Wheelchair accessibility: We got into the restaurant and to the table without any problems. Toilets are in the basement, therefore not accessible to wheelchair users. We made a reservation online, but were called immediately after making the reservation and advised of this. So everything is great

Definitely worth mentioning and visiting, that's how I would like to start my review. We have been somewhat reluctant to visit this excellent restaurant in the past. Also because we had the erroneous belief that the food there was “old-fashioned”, “drug-like” or “boring in terms of cuisine”. But life always shows you how wrong you can be, as this restaurant offers dishes that are at a very high level in terms of composition, quality and quantity (not just the remarkably large and delicious schnitzel menu). Yes, the focus of the menu is somewhat on home-style gastronomy, but it is so imaginative and diverse and interestingly designed, so that everyone is sure to find something to suit their taste. The service, in the form of the owner and his wife, is very charming and attentive, but never intrusive. That's exactly how it should be. The prices are absolutely reasonable and quite cheap for the quantities offered. The selection of dishes is extensive, with constantly changing daily and seasonal menus and high-quality ingredients. Since this restaurant has developed into an absolute insider tip, it is advisable to pre-order here, also because the dining rooms are not waiting rooms but rather cozy rooms. By the way, there is also a bowling alley here, but it is well booked. All in all, a restaurant with a family atmosphere and wonderful cuisine that is definitely worth visiting. We are now regular guests there.

Good restaurant, but bad value for money. Don’t forget to book you table in advance.

Kampai Sushi Bar is Quality. When we were visiting Hamburg, we wanted to get sushi and Kampai was the TOP peoples’ choice. Everyone’s review about the sushi is great. This place serves the BEST sushi in the city or even country. I am a sushi fan and I’ve eaten it in so many places(countries), but nothing like this. Here is what you need to know about Kampai Sushi Bar: 1. Location may not be attractive, but trust me it’s worth the visit! There is a metro nearby. 2. Do email them before going. Make your reservation a day or so ahead, otherwise you may not get a seat, because there are only 6 seats inside which are available upon reservation only. 3. Prices are affordable and worth every penny 4. Friendliest Chef ever, ask him about “Okinawa Island songs” 😊 5. Friendliest staff ever. We talked to all of them 6. Make sure to order Nigiri Salmon Flambe. Omg..I still can’t get over the taste. We liked it so much we went for another round. Kampai Sushi Bar is a very small place, but the atmosphere, the service, the taste of sushi is worth it. Trust me you will want to go back (because we do and we will definitely go there again). Best sushi experience I’ve ever had!

We have been regular guests in Corfu for many years and that is why I would like to share my experiences. Corfu is a wonderful Greek restaurant with fine cuisine. Opening times are currently from 1:30 p.m. to 10:00 p.m., with Tuesdays being closed. I can only recommend everyone to reserve a table, as sometimes it can happen that you don't get a seat without a reservation. The interior is simply designed, but the Greek influence is clearly visible. The dark tables and chairs in the room can be pushed together for larger groups as needed. There is also a simple terrace with wicker chairs, which are unfortunately a little too low for the table and are not particularly comfortable. Large umbrellas are stretched over almost every area of ​​the terrace. The staff is very friendly, even if they sometimes forget something. However, these are just small details that could be a little annoying. The boss is very communicative and also takes the time to ask how you are doing. Unfortunately, you can't find that kind of personal attention everywhere. The food is typically Greek and simply delicious. Of course, every now and then something may have been left on the grill for too long and slightly burnt, but overall it's delicious. Over the years we have noticed that prices have increased significantly (which I completely understand). Unfortunately, the warming device for the meat was also removed, so the meat ends up being rather cold. The delicious coleslaw was sacrificed to a mixed salad. Unfortunately, card payments are no longer accepted, so you should remember to have enough cash with you beforehand. In summary, we always enjoy coming here. Nothing is perfect, but the owner makes up for a lot with his charming manner that I haven't often experienced in a restaurant. Thank you for the many years in which we have been your guests.

Went here for the lunch menu and we ordered Kräuter Pfannkuchen and Labskaus (one of my fav food in Hamburg). The Labskaus was tasty, and somehow felt a bit different from what I've tasted before. Like instead of canned meat, they used something like pulled meat. But this is just my hunch. I was pleasantly surprised with the Pfannkuchen though. It's like an omellete that has Mushroom sauce and pork wrapped inside it. And it tastes amazing. A German version of umami bomb, coupled with the delicious mushroom taste of the sauce. Coupled with a really vintage, Stube (Bar) like interior; the Restaurant im Sprinkenhof nestled in the recesses of the city center  is a real hidden gem!

I finally made it to the Wolfshöle again in January. Unfortunately, I can only go there to eat on my vacation, as the Wolfshöle is closed on Sundays and Mondays and I also have those days off. I was there last summer and was thrilled. And this time, in my opinion, Mr. Fauster has gone one better. Every course was perfectly seasoned and a delight.  The restaurant is decorated in dark wood and has beautiful black and white photos on the wall, and some of the pictures were even painted by a young lady from the service, as I found out at the end (see my photos at the end... the lobster and others) The staff, that evening 4 nice young ladies and a man in service.... and everyone was so incredibly nice and always had a smile on their faces... only every restaurant had a staff like that... and even Mr. Fauster himself has them Food served with... What I personally don't like are the table runners. I'm just a fan of classic white tablecloths. But of course that's a matter of opinion... because when it comes to the monthly costs for table linen and napkins... you can now pay an employee for that. So either table linen or one more employee... of course everyone should decide for themselves. and another small suggestion for improvement .... for someone who likes to eat alone like me... I would like to see a larger selection of small bottles of wine. But of course that doesn't detract from a wonderful evening in the Wolfshöle.... and I'm already looking forward to my next vacation so I can enjoy this delicious meal again.

The restaurant is decorated in dark wood and has beautiful black and white photos on the wall, and some of the pictures were even painted by a young lady from the service, as I found out at the end (see my photos at the end... the lobster and others) The staff, that evening 4 nice young ladies and a man in service.... and everyone was so incredibly nice and always had a smile on their faces... only every restaurant had a staff like that... and even Mr. Fauster himself has them Food served with... What I personally don't like are the table runners. I'm just a fan of classic white tablecloths. But of course that's a matter of opinion... because when it comes to the monthly costs for table linen and napkins... you can now pay an employee for that. So either table linen or one more employee... of course everyone should decide for themselves. and another small suggestion for improvement .... for someone who likes to eat alone like me... I would like to see a larger selection of small bottles of wine. But of course that doesn't detract from a wonderful evening in the Wolfshöle.... and I'm already looking forward to my next vacation so I can enjoy this delicious meal again.
