Aretea is a great restaurant. There are the typical Greek dishes and Italian food, which I haven't tried but which is also said to be very tasty. We had reserved a table (they should do better) and were welcomed very nicely. In addition to the normal menu, there was also a blackboard with a specialty, the daily rabbit. We quickly got our drinks and an ouzo. We shared the appetizer platter as a starter. Very rich and diverse. Vegetables, fish, mushrooms, tarama, broad beans etc. All very tasty. There was also fresh bread with a super delicious cream. Then came the main course. Large portions, with salad, crunchy vegetables and, for me, fries. And tsaitsiki. I ate lamb. It was very tender and flavorful. In between and with the bill, another ouzo was offered. I couldn't eat any more dessert, I was too full. Overall, a great evening with attentive but not intrusive staff. I deducted the ambience because it was sometimes very loud due to a larger group. But everyone feels that differently. In between, a rose seller came into the restaurant, his rose is still looking good in the vase after a week. Feel free to buy one for your friend, wife/husband - it's a nice memory of a great evening. Thank you M. for the rose and you both for a very nice evening.

Calisperassas. A real honest and delicious Greek restaurant in the east of Hamburg. And the store is often packed. Quality paired with a big gastronomic heart. The service staff have fun, just like the family. This is noticeable. The ice-cold ouzo as an aperitif warms everyone up, even more so in summer. I would walk 100 km for a very good Mediterranean salad, it is really very good here. Fresh, hand-picked, house dressing or oil with balsamic vinegar. Why go to Greece, you can get everything here too. Without a long flight. OK, the topic of sun, let’s leave that…. The bifteki was also very good, solid and tasty, vegetables and rice on point. And thank you, dogs are cared for and treated immediately. And they can also pour beer. The foam crown is made of concrete and stands like a 1st Yammas. It's really fun to come here from time to time. The ice-cold ouzo afterwards cools you down. Calinichta.

I highly recommend Estancia Steaks for anyone craving a top-notch steak and great service.

Ponzu is always a nice experience and a restaurant to recommend. There is something for everyone, whether small, large, vegetarian, with meat or fish, spicy or not spicy. :) Ambience: The restaurant is beautifully decorated inside, and you can also sit very well outside. Most of the time we didn't have to reserve a table when we went there to eat, but I would still recommend just to be safe. Unfortunately, the main street outside was a little noisy at times, which the restaurant can't do anything about, but I would still deduct one star. 4/5🌟 Food: the food was super delicious! The portions were large enough to fill you up but without making you feel overfilled or stuffed. If you reordered, the food always came very quickly. The menu is very varied and there is something for everyone. Be it vegetarian, with meat or fish, spicy or not spicy. 5/5🌟 Service: the service was really great. Maybe it was because it wasn't that busy, but we received very quick and very friendly service. The food was always there very quickly and warm and even when ordering, everything was great. 5/5 🌟 Conclusion: it may not be an eye-catching or positively shocking restaurant, but I would definitely recommend it to everyone, especially since you can go out to eat very well, be it a celebratory occasion or just a non-binding meal with friends. :) Vegetarian options: Vegetarian dishes are marked, and very tasty. Kid-friendliness: The restaurant is child-friendly. The children can play and run around outside. Wheelchair accessibility: It's very easy to sit outside, and the area is definitely accessible with a wheelchair. As far as I know, you can only access the indoor area by climbing stairs, which could be a problem for a wheelchair user. I would just call the restaurant and ask because I'm unsure.

We have been planning to go here from long time so we decided to go on a weekday. It was not overly crowded and the staff was very very friendly , helped us with our coats and all at the entry. We all could speak enough German but probably seeing us make mistake, they offered to help in English. There was a tiny snack to begin the dinner with, it was something I can’t describe in words. Later on we got the wine and they helped in choosing a good one for our requirements. We decided to go with classic Lebanese starters, all vegetarian and we got taste of a lot of food. All of it was such a treat to our senses. Then instead of going for one main course for each one of us, we got bigger portions of some of the most liked vegetarian starters and filled ourselves more with those. No wonder given the location and the reviews. But none of the guests will definitely come back.

We can only recommend it and look forward to the next culinary trip.

We have been happy regular guests here since it opened in 2016. The Goa is by far the best Indian restaurant in Hamburg and is simply in a league of its own compared to the competition. The large and varied menu offers something for every taste and also boasts an excellent selection of vegetarian and vegan dishes. My absolute favorite is the Palak Paneer. For the run-of-the-mill Indian, this dish often tastes like meaningless spinach porridge; in Goa, one of these classics of North Indian cuisine is a true taste revelation: hearty, spicy, umami and simply one of the most rounded flavor compositions that I have ever had the pleasure of tasting. Also highly recommended are Paneer Pasanda, Shahi Paneer and Malai Kofta. The service is professional, warm, unobtrusive and attentive. One would like to shout to a few reviewers who claim the opposite here: "As it echoes into the forest, so it echoes out again." The ambience is authentically Indian and modern at the same time. The interior of many other Indian restaurants often appears extremely kitschy. That's not the case here. Large-format wedding photos of the owner and his wife hang on the walls and give the room a very nice, personal atmosphere. Sometimes chefs are extremely careful with spiciness (if you really want it really spicy, you should emphasize this very clearly) and are even more generous with sugar. Without a doubt, this is a concession to the effeminate North German palate. But the good thing is that the friendly and helpful waiters are happy to respond to the guest's individual wishes. When we order, we now always say “extra spicy and not so sweet, please”. Since everything is freshly prepared, the kitchen can always react flexibly. The portions are large and plentiful, filling even grown men. The pricing policy cannot necessarily be called defensive. However, anyone who delivers such quality also has the right to demand corresponding prices. We will certainly remain happy regular guests for a long time. The Goa now belongs to Blankenese like the Linde or the Dal Fabbro. Thank you and see you next time!

We have been happy regular guests here since it opened in 2016. The Goa is by far the best Indian restaurant in Hamburg and is simply in a league of its own compared to the competition. The large and varied menu offers something for every taste and also boasts an excellent selection of vegetarian and vegan dishes. My absolute favorite is the Palak Paneer. For the run-of-the-mill Indian, this dish often tastes like meaningless spinach porridge; in Goa, one of these classics of North Indian cuisine is a true taste revelation: hearty, spicy, umami and simply one of the most rounded flavor compositions that I have ever had the pleasure of tasting. Also highly recommended are Paneer Pasanda, Shahi Paneer and Malai Kofta. The service is professional, warm, unobtrusive and attentive. One would like to shout to a few reviewers who claim the opposite here: "As it echoes into the forest, so it echoes out again." The ambience is authentically Indian and modern at the same time. The interior of many other Indian restaurants often appears extremely kitschy. That's not the case here. Large-format wedding photos of the owner and his wife hang on the walls and give the room a very nice, personal atmosphere. Sometimes chefs are extremely careful with spiciness (if you really want it really spicy, you should emphasize this very clearly) and are even more generous with sugar. Without a doubt, this is a concession to the effeminate North German palate. But the good thing is that the friendly and helpful waiters are happy to respond to the guest's individual wishes. When we order, we now always say “extra spicy and not so sweet, please”. Since everything is freshly prepared, the kitchen can always react flexibly. We felt absolutely comfortable and will definitely come back.

Restaurant Zorbas - Friedenauer Str 45 This is a Greek that you have to experience once. Always the best quality combined with over forty years of restaurant tradition. My absolute insider tip is a combination of my tastiest favorites, which you definitely have to try: “Saganaki & Ouzo plate gratinated”!! That’s right: “baked” is the “magic word” here for even more enjoyment! Juicy meat in different variations with this unique Metaxa sauce - I love it! I would also like to call this plate “Andreas plate” or “fire department plate”, because this combination will fill up the strongest among us with enjoyment. The location of the restaurant not far from the Mittelland Canal also invites all cyclists to take an enjoyable stopover. The interior has been subtly modernized and adapted to the times over the decades, but has always remained true to itself and the concept. There are small works of art to discover and the picture gallery always makes me dream of Greece. Visit the Sterkas family, come to Greece... Many thanks to the Sterkas family for this wonderful place of Greek hospitality

If you are looking for a restaurant with friendly service, delicious food, large portions and a great ambience, you have come to the right place! We have been here several times and again today. Service: The boss still takes personal care of his guests here and not too little. As soon as you arrive you are greeted warmly and you immediately feel welcome. You don't have to wait long for food and drinks, even if the restaurant is full. Eat: We already have many dishes (about starters, main courses and dessert) Tried them and were always impressed by the good taste and richly filled plates. If you leave here hungry, you have to have more than one stomach. Even the food for “small hunger” is plentiful. Even if you don't make it all the way through, the leftovers will be happy to be packed up. The menu also offers a wide selection, so there should be something for everyone. Price: Anyone expecting a €10 burger menu is wrong here. But for the quantity and quality, the prices are really great. Ambiance: A very nice restaurant with the typical Greek flair and facilities. There is also a very nice outdoor area for warm days. The Greek background music is a matter of taste, but it's part of it for me. Conclusion: If you love extremely friendly service and good, plentiful food, this is the place for you. Parking: Right next to the restaurant Kid-friendliness: The waitresses and the boss are extremely friendly and work hard with children. Wheelchair accessibility: Easily accessible

I never tried desi restaurants that much, because when I did the food was never authentic. However, I read reviews for Maharaja, and then we happened to have a stop in Karlsruhe so we decided to try it out. We were surprised by how well decorated the restaurant is. On top, the staff was really really nice, they took our luggage and placed it safely. The person waiting on us spoke Hindi with us, even though we're urdu speakers but we felt right at home. Now coming to the food, it was amazing. We tried the makni chicken and roghan josh and it was amazing. The garlic naal, drinks everything. Would love to stop by again whenever we're in Karsruhe. We were in a hurry to catch the next train, if not we would've loved to try the wide variety of desi desserts. And one plus point, their food is halal. Vegetarian options: As with any desi restaurant, they have options of vegetables too.

Visited Karlsruhe for business visit and was amazed to see numbers of Indian restaurants in the city. Maharaja is located near Karlsruhe Central Station and is quite popular one. When I visited the place on Sunday, it was quite busy. The staff was amazing and serving everyone promptly. Shout out to Prince for his excellent service. There are plenty of food options. I love the way food is served. The staff put small fire oven on table so that food can remain hot. I never seem this before. Here is my list of favorite food options: Lentsil soup 🍲 ***** Garlic naan    ***** Paneer Masala 🥘 ***** Green Tea 🍵 ***** I loved garlic naan and masala paneer. It was really good. The sitting area is not very large. However if you are really big group than it may not able to fit. The place is fully accessible for old people and people with special needs. Further, it is pet friendly facility and you can take them.

I was there at Easter with my girlfriend and I was very impressed by the food and the atmosphere, the shop was well attended. In addition to the fixed menu, there is a changing weekly menu, which is definitely worth taking a look at. Although we only had pasta, other guests' pizza also looked extremely appealing. In addition to the delicious wine, I definitely recommend choosing homemade desserts (these are specially marked). In the end the price was ~100€ for 2 starters/main courses/desserts, a bottle of water, 2 glasses of red wine and a coffee, which was reasonable in my opinion. All in all we had a wonderful evening there. Vegetarian options: Various pizza and pasta variations. Kid-friendliness: There were families sitting in the shop and also a family with a dog, which wasn't a problem, they even brought a bowl of water.

Indian restaurant that has a lounge and a pleasant patio at the back of the premises. Very extensive menu and fantastic service. I went for dinner, opting for mutton korma, a dish consisting of chopped lamb in sauce, seasoned with various spices, accompanied by flavored basmati rice. To drink I had a half-liter beer, and for dessert I had mango cream, for a bill of €24. The dish was spectacular, intense flavor, delicious, and abundant, in fact I couldn't finish all the sauce, which was delicious. They were nice enough to give me a pen.

Today we visited Gatto Nero for the first time. We were there at 12 p.m. and were warmly welcomed. The range of food on offer is wide-ranging. There are starters such as caprese, bruschetta and anti pasti plates. Various salads, meat dishes such as schnitzel, rump steak, grilled dishes. Burgers, pizza, fish dishes. Also classic pasta dishes, such as Rigatoni Pomodoro, and delicious tagliatelli with smoked salmon. Also dishes for the little ones, such as chicken nuggets, children's schnitzel and spaghetti with tomato sauce / Bolognese. There is also something for vegetarians, such as grilled vegetable pan and potato pan with avocado. Some desserts are also waiting for you. We had the Chrunchy Chicken Burger twice, the Pizza Tartufo and I think the fourth was the veal liver with fried potatoes. Everything was delicious and the portions were very large. It doesn't compare to my own food, but it's not that easy to top either 😉 The prices are a little higher compared to other restaurants I usually visit, but completely ok for the portion size and the taste. The staff and the chef were very nice and happy to join in the fun. We asked 2-3 times if everything was ok. Very attentive, very commendable. The restaurant is somewhat remote, at a sports field and is quite quiet. Which I personally like. I don't like it when it's too loud. It is easily accessible by car and there are parking spaces in front of it. You can also hold a celebration there with up to 100 people. Delivery area is the mountain villages of Hohenwettersbach, Grünwettersbach and Palmbach from 15€ no delivery fee. Wolfartsweier, Durlauch Aue and Stupferich From 25€ + 2€ delivery fee Waldbronn, Karlsbad, Durlach From 50€ + 2€ delivery fee Definitely worth a visit 😊

Jaroon's is a typical American diner. From the interior design to the menu, everything is super harmonious and you feel like you've been catapulted straight to the States. I saw a group of five who hadn't made a reservation being seated at a tiny bar table. The served dishes were pushed back and forth in good old Tetris style. Unfortunately it didn't look comfortable. I've eaten here many times, but to be honest I've never been interested in the burgers. Right from the start I didn't find them visually or qualitatively appealing. If I want to eat a (very) good burger, I go downtown, where there are better, and sometimes even cheaper, alternatives. In the past, when I want to snack before a movie, my choice has always been an appetizer and the taco salad. Here you get a fresh, crunchy lettuce, ground beef, sour cream and cheese, served in an edible taco shell. Once the salad is eaten, you can eat the taco shell with the dip that was served with it. Cool! You really can't get that anywhere else in Karlsruhe. And nothing feels heavy in the stomach during the movie. The drinks prices, however, are a little harder to stomach. This is certainly due to the location within the cinema. But what I would really like to emphasize is the super-friendly service. No matter how stressful things got because of the crowds, she always had a few kind words and a smile on her face.

Uli Ui Ui….. how the restaurant “San Michele” with Antonio has slacked off - for me it always had a special feeling to eat there because you felt welcome as a guest + friend…. but unfortunately that was once... Unfortunately it was extremely relaxed. Apart from the extremely expensive prices for drinks and expensive prices for the food, the quality left a lot to be desired in relation to the expensive price. Today we had dinner again - and probably for the last time - with Antonio and his wife in the “San Michele” restaurant in Lübeck. Not only the waiting time of 1:45 hours, which is just tolerable, but also the time delay when serving the food for 4 people on the table with approx. 10-15 minutes per meal is not nice and everyone then fends for themselves to eat. If a bottle of cheap Lambrusco with 0.70l (purchase: approx. 5 - 6.- EUR) costs a whole 29.50 EUR and therefore more than a bottle of wine, then that's really special. Beer + water had normal prices. The dish of the day for a proud EUR 35.50 is a simple veal cutlet fried in the pan - without any sauce - only served with about 2 tablespoons of “arrabiata pasta”, which in reality was unfortunately just simple pasta Napolitana (with tomato sauce)... The whole thing for just EUR 35.50... doesn't fit at all - sorry. My wife's small portion of octopus with a “mirco salad bowl” tasted delicious - but it was for the quantity and the minimalist side dishes... completely miscalculated + overpriced. Our friends, who also dined with us and also shared the price/performance experience with us, quickly agreed with us: The rack of lamb was tasty and at least somewhat adequate - the small portion of noodles was not that good. “...we won't eat here anymore” that was the consensus of “UniSono” -. It's a shame but that's the way it is!! I really like “Antonio” - the boss - as a person and have known him for over 20 years... but what his guests are offered for this high-priced restaurant is unfortunately not worth the money. I don't want to blame the service at the table at all; they were friendly, courteous and attentive... that was a positive thing. P.S. When we finally spend > 250.- EUR with 2 pairs... I have the expectation that with a good Italian restaurant I will at least be offered a small nightcap / grappa "unsolicited" with the bill - but unfortunately nothing... nothing like that!! We experience this with all the other good Italians in Lübeck (with Gino in the San Marco, San Remo, with Salvatore on the ship, with Dirk in the VAI and with Vito in the tower and also a few others) ... At “San Michele” the question didn’t even come up… and when I asked the boss and the boss’s wife as they were leaving, the only answer was: “You could have let me know.” Conclusion: That doesn't fit here at all - far too overpriced food of unfortunately not high quality with sometimes small quantities (including side dishes) and long waiting times of 1:45 hours (even though the restaurant was not fully occupied)... Unfortunately there is a “NO GO”. A pity…. We regret this... but would like to at least give all other future guests some advance information. Ciao and arriverderci…

We were looking for a special restaurant on the last day of our vacation and discovered Foster's Garden through the Australian offerings. That evening we were greeted very friendly by the boss (there weren't many left) and served. Despite the increased price, we opted for the Australian grill plate for 2 people with an additional crocodile (which costs extra). Since we know that good Australian quality has its price, we expected one piece of meat per person and we got a platter that would certainly have been enough for 4 people. Ev. You could do something else here in terms of price/quantity ratio (less, but cheaper). The meat was perfectly prepared and very tasty, and the side dishes also tasted excellent. The ambience was more than suitable for our last evening. The lighting in the glass room together with the subtle music created a very romantic atmosphere. The boss had a very nice chat with us at the end and the employees were always friendly throughout the evening. We would like to see a restaurant like Foster's Garden in our area. If we are in the area again we will definitely come back :-) Thank you for the wonderful final evening of our vacation :-) Parking: No special parking spaces available. You have to look for a parking space in the side streets on the edge.

The highlight of the day for us, absolute recommendation. The price for the grill plate, which comes with various side dishes and sauces, an extra side dish and 3 large cola, was €105. Absolutely appropriate for the performance.

description: Inconspicuous from the outside. I've walked past many times and never thought there would be a great restaurant hidden here. The food and service were extremely good, very accommodating and pleasant. The bread that was served at the beginning is homemade and incredibly good, as is the greeting from the kitchen. Fantastic food with personal service in a cozy small room! We enjoyed a 5 course dinner for 2 people on a weekday night and it was a splendid experience. The food is extra-ordinary (the literal sense of the word), very interesting and different ingredients and overall well balanced tastes. The highlight definitely is the current extra starter they have (scallops on a buckwheat crêpe with kimchi mayo, sesame and basil - absolutely breathtaking). What I really liked was their flexibility, we could have 2 different starters and 2 different desserts! The service is supercute and personal, giving flexibility and pacing the meal nicely. They create a relaxed atmosphere but also lets the time fly by with their entertainment. Also the chef is so nice and approachable. The ambiance is the biggest area of opportunity, though it’s still very cosy, definitely professional and inviting: lots of tables for two and an overall small space make it intimate. However, it could use some more soft and warm lights and some color. The decoration on the tables is cute though, with different small fresh flowers on every table. Overall very recommendable and definitely a great price for what you get!

tl;dr: good (but not excellent) food; they kept us there for way too long. This isn’t an easy review to write. ESSENCE is an upscale restaurant (they might even be hoping for a Michelin star at some point) and that comes with certain expectations, which (might I add, on that specific day; your experience may vary) were not entirely met. They offer a tasting style menu which comes with multiple courses, and that’s what we went for. The food is very nicely prepared and presented, and there is an interesting variety of options. It didn’t blow my mind, but I objectively cannot say it was bad. The biggest problem for us was the service. None of the servers were rude or unhelpful, quite the opposite, they just kept us there way too long. The whole menu took over four hours to be served, with gaps of sometimes almost half an hour between courses. I don’t know whether that was intentional or not (it’s entirely possible they were short staffed, it’s COVID times after all), but we felt it was too much and it’s the first time it took us this long to get our food, even in comparison with similar restaurants with even more courses. Overall an enjoyable dining experience, blemished by weirdly slow service.

tl;dr: good (but not excellent) food; they kept us there for way too long. This isn’t an easy review to write. ESSENCE is an upscale restaurant (they might even be hoping for a Michelin star at some point) and that comes with certain expectations, which (might I add, on that specific day; your experience may vary) were not entirely met. They offer a tasting style menu which comes with multiple courses, and that’s what we went for. The food is very nicely prepared and presented, and there is an interesting variety of options. It didn’t blow my mind, but I objectively cannot say it was bad. The biggest problem for us was the service. None of the servers were rude or unhelpful, quite the opposite, they just kept us there way too long. The whole menu took over four hours to be served, with gaps of sometimes almost half an hour between courses. I don’t know whether that was intentional or not (it’s entirely possible they were short staffed, it’s COVID times after all), but we felt it was too much and it’s the first time it took us this long to get our food, even in comparison with similar restaurants with even more courses. Overall an enjoyable dining experience, blemished by weirdly slow service.

This place was a big disappointment, I'm honestly very surprised it's so highly rated. First off, the service is excellent, multiple waitresses came over to check on me and bring me what I ordered and refill my wine glass, you really can't ask for better service. The food, on the other hand, is really not very good. I had this seafood bisque that had a fishy taste, then a pork entree with potato cakes and a sauce with herbs. The meat was dry and the herbs didn't quite go with the sauce, everything was overall very bland and the sauce watery. The dessert was a white chocolate cake that mainly tasted like raw dough, and the homemade ice cream was actually the star of the show. It's a shame that a restaurant with service this good had food that was so incredibly mediocre.

We went to this place for dinner. It started lovely with the short-haired server suggesting we get the sharing platter as starters. It arrived promptly, consisting of savoury bread, truffle mayo, dips, cheeses, cured meat— it was really good. Then the mains took 1.5 hour to arrive. The tempura zucchini flowers had too much batter, soggy, the veal cutlet wasn't to our liking but the mini cleaver was a cute touch, the veal cheeks was soft but not worth the 1.5 hour wait and they are not cheap. The 2nd blonde server was rude and didn't  show us a receipt for the bill, she told us to pay this amount and we didn't know if there was service charge or not. But when we left whatever spare change we had—she told us that this wasn't even enough for the kitchen alone.

Today I had the pleasure of dining at this restaurant, and I must say, it was an awesome experience. From the moment we stepped inside, we were captivated by the chic and cozy decoration. The ambiance was just perfect for a romantic evening. The staff at the restaurant were incredibly friendly and can speak english, german and of course persian. They were attentive and made us feel welcome throughout our visit. Their warm hospitality added to the overall enjoyment of the evening. As an appetizer, we ordered the "tahdig gheimeh," and it was absolutely delicious. The crispy rice paired with the flavorful stew was a delightful combination. It set the tone for what was to come. For our main course, we opted for the classic kebab with rice and two small portions of "khoresht." The flavors were rich and authentic, truly capturing the essence of Iranian cuisine. However, while the kebab was good, I felt it could have been even better. Nonetheless, the overall meal was satisfying and left us craving more. To end our meal on a sweet note, we indulged in the ice cream, a pistatio flavor I had never tasted before. It was a delightful surprise, and I appreciated the restaurant's willingness to offer unique and intriguing selections. The restaurant had both indoor and outdoor seating options. we preferred to dine outdoore. But if you like to eat indoor, the air conditioner keeps the temperature pleasant, allowing you to relax and enjoy your meal without any discomfort. The choice of Iranian music playing in the background was a lovely touch. It wasn't loud, which enhanced our overall enjoyment of the evening. The soothing melodies transported us to Iran and added to the romantic ambiance of the restaurant. To complement our meal, we ordered a gin with pomegranate. The drink had a distinct flavor that reminded me of home in Iran. It was a delightful pairing with the food and added a touch of authenticity to the experience. I must mention that the price of the dishes was slightly on the higher side. However, considering the lovely ambiance, attentive service, and the overall romantic experience, I believe it was worth it. The restaurant provided an unforgettable evening that left us with wonderful memories. In conclusion, I highly recommend this Iranian restaurant for its chic and cozy atmosphere, friendly staff, and delicious cuisine. While the kebab and rice could have been improved, the overall experience was delightful and romantic. It's a perfect place to indulge in Iranian flavors and create beautiful memories.

As an appetizer, we ordered the "tahdig gheimeh," and it was absolutely delicious. The crispy rice paired with the flavorful stew was a delightful combination. It set the tone for what was to come. For our main course, we opted for the classic kebab with rice and two small portions of "khoresht." The flavors were rich and authentic, truly capturing the essence of Iranian cuisine. However, while the kebab was good, I felt it could have been even better. Nonetheless, the overall meal was satisfying and left us craving more. To end our meal on a sweet note, we indulged in the ice cream, a pistatio flavor I had never tasted before. It was a delightful surprise, and I appreciated the restaurant's willingness to offer unique and intriguing selections. The restaurant had both indoor and outdoor seating options. we preferred to dine outdoore. But if you like to eat indoor, the air conditioner keeps the temperature pleasant, allowing you to relax and enjoy your meal without any discomfort. The choice of Iranian music playing in the background was a lovely touch. It wasn't loud, which enhanced our overall enjoyment of the evening. The soothing melodies transported us to Iran and added to the romantic ambiance of the restaurant. To complement our meal, we ordered a gin with pomegranate. The drink had a distinct flavor that reminded me of home in Iran. It was a delightful pairing with the food and added a touch of authenticity to the experience. I must mention that the price of the dishes was slightly on the higher side. However, considering the lovely ambiance, attentive service, and the overall romantic experience, I believe it was worth it. The restaurant provided an unforgettable evening that left us with wonderful memories. In conclusion, I highly recommend this Iranian restaurant for its chic and cozy atmosphere, friendly staff, and delicious cuisine. While the kebab and rice could have been improved, the overall experience was delightful and romantic. It's a perfect place to indulge in Iranian flavors and create beautiful memories.

It is a small restaurant with seating for about 20-22 people. The chef and the wait staff are very friendly. I ordered their 300 g ribeye steak rare. It was cooked to perfection and delicious! No fussy sauces or other additions to hide any imperfections. Seasoned with simple salt and pepper. Just want the doctor ordered. I accompanied the steak with a house salad which was also really good. I also like my beers dark and alcoholic and they had the perfect one for me. The chef prepared the steak and followed up with me to check that everything was okay. It was excellent! The beer, the steak, the salad everything was on the money! They were getting ready to close by the time I was done with my dinner. I stepped out for a smoke and realized I was out. Tried to buy a pack from the vending machine right outside but it wouldn't accept my card and I couldn't understand the language on the display. So I asked the waitress for help but instead the chef came out to help me. We figured out pretty soon that the machine was not accepting international cards. So he offered me one of his cigarettes. Hehe! Best service I've had in Europe!

A Peruvian friend recommended this restaurant to us, since we wanted to eat some good ceviche and lomo saltado. The food was great, very good presentation and delicious. The atmosphere and the restaurant was super nice, the person that took our orders was really friendly, and overall we had a great time. We were two couples and had a reservation at 6pm, since our friend has told us that the ceviche might sell out if we reserved later. I had ceviche as a starter (you can also order it as a main), and it was delicious, I do not like very much fish, but ceviche was always the exception. I was a little bit scared since the fish might not have been as fresh as when living in a coastal city, but it tasted as good as the one I had in my home country. As a main dish I had the lomo saltado, which is always super nice, the quality of the meat was perfect. And for dessert I had the cheesecake. If you want a good taste of what Peruvian food is, I recommend to go here

Just to summarize- with a very small issues I have to say this is a very good place and I will be back sometime for sure.

reviewer: Daniela Ullmann / Healthy Lifestyle by Design
description: Ordered take away many times but never actually ate inside. Had a lovely dinner on Friday night with my friend before watching a movie. Restaurant was 80% Full when we arrived at 18.30. (I reserved 1hr earlier online) I ordered the veggie inside out roll (vegan option was possible by removing cream cheese - 12€), which was delicious!! and got some water with lemon and mint. (ice cold water is not my favorite). My friend got the coconut curry (21€) and she was also very happy. Service was very attentive (as always) and the food was delivered fast. I can also recommend the veggie tempura. For me it’s one of the best places for sushi in the neighborhood. Price wise on the higher end but amazing quality and presentation of food. Their outdoor terrace makes you feel like you sit in a wine garden. More vegan options on the menu would be fantastic.

Just ate there this evening. I ordered the 300g Filet cooked to medium as recommended by our server when I described how I wanted it. It was cooked as a true medium rare is in the United States - a thick stripe of red through the center.  This piece of meat was the size of a baseball and tasted amazing. In my 61 years of life, I will say that this was in the top 2% of all steaks I’ve ever had.   My wife, who likes the occasional steak, who, over the last 25 years I have coached down from hard medium well (ruined) steaks to medium-medium rare steaks ordered a 200g filet cooked medium well upon the servers advice.  She described it as unbelievable and it was cooked to a perfect juicy pink. The salad that comes with the steak is offered with a yogurt or other type of dressing… I don’t eat dressing so I chose neither and they brought out a vial of olive oil and another of balsamic vinegar in case I wanted something different.  I didn’t but my wife wished she could have had that.  We ordered a baked potato to share… it was cooked just right.  Each meal also came with two slices of garlic toast.  The service was exceptional and the price was incredibly low.  I had tap water to drink, my wife had sparkling water and a glass of wine - the tab was 78 Euros I believe.  This photo is of my 300g steak.  Magnificent experience.

I had heard about the restaurant several times, but had never eaten here before. We had reserved, I would recommend it to everyone. Especially on weekends. Our table was in one of the back corners. There were 4 of us. A friend is more or less a regular and knows the local area and menu very well. There is a good selection of starters, salads, meat, a few fish and children's dishes and some side dishes. The latter can be varied. I had souvlaki with tzatziki and gigantes (beans) instead of fries. The quality was excellent, the portion was really good. For me, after the starters, too much. But absolutely perfect with a good appetite. We shared appetizers at the table. The garlic bread that goes with the tzatziki is truly incredible. The tzatzi is also delicious. We also had the shrimp sganaki. For €8.40, 4 shrimps weren't really that much. But also absolutely delicious in terms of taste. Only the service with the drinks was a bit slow. Which was certainly due to the fact that the restaurant was absolutely full. Of course, this was extremely stressful. Because of the space in the corner, we might have gotten a little lost at times. Therefore not 5/5 everywhere - but an absolute recommendation! Price/performance top!

Highly Recommended! We order here often and also enjoy eating locally. Attentive and friendly service. Special requests when ordering over the phone work easily here! If you want to eat on site, you need to make a reservation in advance. The restaurant is always well filled. The ambience is classic Chinese, a bit old but not something that really matters here. The food is placed on warming plates or hot pans in front of you on the table. It can quickly become a bit crowded on the table, but that is quickly forgotten with the extremely tasty curry. The crispy fried duck is also very tasty and stands out in terms of quality from fast food snacks. All dishes come with rice unless you order it differently. As the icing on the cake, you get an aperitif and nightcap on the house. In terms of price, the cheap drinks stand out and combined with the food, the result is a fair price-performance ratio. The two of us paid just under €60 for drinks, main course and dessert. Conclusion: great restaurant, we would love to come back!

restaurant_name: NAMASTE - Indisches Traditionelles Restaurant in Nürnberg Rathenauplatz
description: My 16 year old daughter and I picked this place based on good reviews on several different platforms.  We were not disappointed. The one thing that this restaurant had which most Indian restaurants seem not to have is tasteful decoration.  That has been my experience over the last 3 decades of trying different Indian food all over the world.  The ambience was really nice and tastefully decorated. The service was good and friendly enough.  I come from North America were it is sometimes over-the-top friendly but there was nothing here I would complain about. The food was really good.  I took off one star from my rating  for the relatively small amount of chicken in the dish.  It could have been a little bit more. Otherwise it was quite tasty.  The raita was exceptional. Bottom line:  I would recommend this restaurant and will definitely go back again. Kid-friendliness: I have older kids but I did see 4 high chairs for toddlers. Wheelchair accessibility: The restaurant is on one level with the street with no steps.  The bathroom I can‘t speak to.  It probably does not meet the official requirements to be wheelchair accessible.

restaurant_name: NAMASTE - Indisches Traditionelles Restaurant in Nürnberg Rathenauplatz
description: I recently dined at this Indian restaurant, and I had a wonderful experience. The interior decor was beautiful. The staff was attentive and friendly. When it came to the food, two dishes stood out for me - the paneer tandoori tikka and the Palak paneer with naan. The tandoori tikka had a flavorful, smoky taste that I thoroughly enjoyed, and the Palak paneer was a highlight of the meal. In fact, I'd go as far as to say it's the best Palak paneer I've had in Germany. .What's impressive is their diverse menu, catering to both vegetarians and non-vegetarians. They offer a wide range of choices, ensuring there's something for everyone. Additionally, the option for indoor and outdoor seating adds flexibility to the dining experience. Overall, I highly recommend this restaurant for its fantastic ambiance, great staff, and must-try Indian dishes. Just be prepared for slightly higher prices compared to some other options but it’s worth it. It's a gem for Indian cuisine enthusiasts in Germany.

When it came to the food, two dishes stood out for me - the paneer tandoori tikka and the Palak paneer with naan. The tandoori tikka had a flavorful, smoky taste that I thoroughly enjoyed, and the Palak paneer was a highlight of the meal. In fact, I'd go as far as to say it's the best Palak paneer I've had in Germany. .What's impressive is their diverse menu, catering to both vegetarians and non-vegetarians. They offer a wide range of choices, ensuring there's something for everyone. Additionally, the option for indoor and outdoor seating adds flexibility to the dining experience. Overall, I highly recommend this restaurant for its fantastic ambiance, great staff, and must-try Indian dishes. Just be prepared for slightly higher prices compared to some other options but it’s worth it. It's a gem for Indian cuisine enthusiasts in Germany.

We recently spent a few nights in Nuremburg and enjoyed a very good meal at Mesob Restaurant on this trip. This is a casual Ethiopian restaurant on Pillenreuther Straße that makes for good alternative if you are looking for something different to German and Franconian food. Not particularly familiar with Ethiopian food, we found the waitress particularly friendly and able to make good meal suggestions. Menu is in German only but she was able to explain things quite easily in English. During our meal we had a mixed platter for 2 persons that included a mix of stewed meats and vegetables served with injera, a sour dough bread. Some of the items we enjoyed more than others but on the whole, everything was flavourful and enjoyed. In the end, this was a quality meal that we enjoyed very much, would gladly return for another dinner here during future visits to Nuremburg.

As a fan of Sichuan style food, I was excited to try this restaurant's "insider menu" featuring less mainstream dishes. However, I was disappointed by the lack of specialness in the dishes, especially given the high prices. The ribs, in particular, were unacceptable - they appeared to be microwaved and had an overpoweringly sweet marmalade sauce that was unpleasant. Unfortunately, the lack of attention from the staff was also disappointing. Even minor details like clearing the table were not handled with much hospitality, as they simply dumped all the leftovers onto one plate and stacked it up without much care. However, I have to admit, watching this spectacle for 4 minutes was somewhat humorous. I hope this feedback helps the restaurant improve their dishes and customer service, as I believe there is potential for them to stand out in the competitive Sichuan cuisine scene.

Amazing experience! Stopped by for lunch with my classmates on a Friday, the restaurant was nearly empty probably due to the late lunch hours and covid situation. All the necessary precautions were taken- tables were disinfected before we sat down and our waiter had a mask on. All the plates and dishes were very clean and hygienic, incredibly appreciated during the ongoing pandemic. The restaurant is located on Winzinger Straße, private enough to avoid the hassle of the main street but also open enough so it’s easy to spot when passing by- best of both worlds. Beautiful greenery around the entrance gate provides a welcoming and warming first impression. Maharaja accepts reservations, we were shown to our table and given the menus at the drop of the hat. I’d describe the general atmosphere as very peaceful, easy to relax and let go of your day to day worries. The tables were set apart with enough space to sit comfortably, also definitely classifies as child friendly. The indian style menu had an incredible range of choice including an option to customize your own curry dish which I thought was very unique. Me and my classmates decided to go for different variations of the classic chicken curry along with salad and pita bread. The food took about 15-20 minutes to come and was worth every minute! Everything was fresh and tasted delicious, the chicken was cooked to perfection and combined excellently with the mildly spicy sauce.What I find in Indian restaurants is that sometimes the spiciness is slightly overwhelming for my taste, even in the theoretically not spicy dishes. However, this chicken curry provided an exquisite blend of spice which was greatly enjoyable. The pricing was even above my expectations, for the curry, pita bread and drink I paid just under 10​Є. This is an excellent price to quality ratio, and you 100% get your money’s worth. This place is perfect for any type of occasion whether it’s a family outing, brunch with coworkers or a dinner for two! I would definitely recommend Maharaja to anyone looking to spice up their culinary experience.

We called for reservation a few hours before visiting on a Saturday. Although we got there late there were still available seats (so not as busy as we thought). We ordered the tom yang gung, papaya salad and green curry. The dishes were quite salty (but in general I find food in Germany quite salty), especially the tom yang gung (very flavorful). Lastly, just a side note — the food left us quite thirsty! The restaurant itself has nice interior design with a relaxing ambience.

These reviews include previous visits, this restaurant was around long before Google reviews! Locally in downtown Neumünster, right on Großflecken. Easy to reach on foot. They don't have customer parking spaces. The entrance area is quite inconspicuous, peeking out a little from the front of the house. I've walked past there so many times when I wasn't paying attention. The restaurant is on the first floor and can be reached via stairs. There is an elevator further back. [Due to the current CoVid-19 restrictions, I didn't wander around and take photos.] Right in front there is a small pond with fish, a change from the large aquariums. Makes an impression like: "Now I'm stepping onto the terrace." Normally you are greeted with a friendly look and shown to a table, but you can't see it because of the prevailing hygiene regulations. We sat at a table of six with three people. But you needed the space on the table when ordering from the menu. The drink selection is normal. I think it's nice that various Asian drinks can be ordered, for example there is also Japanese sake. In addition, the usual selection of non-alcoholic and alcoholic drinks. Due to the CoVid-19 hygiene regulations, there are currently: no buffet. But when it still existed, you could find a wide selection. Photos are still available. I had dish 208 from the seafood department, spicy shrimp in a delicious sauce. It was simply delicious as they met my taste exactly. The rest of the dishes we ordered were also good. The portion size also matched the price. As always, rice is served in a large pot for everyone. The food was served on hot metal boards or with a candle underneath and the food plate was preheated. So great service. You can also order coffee or something similar at the end of the meal. The premises allow you to celebrate birthdays or similar things there. That's why I've been there several times and have always been satisfied. Special requests are not only accepted, but also implemented. The toilet facilities (at least on the men's side) are spacious. This is an important point, especially in these times. Especially if you want to get away from the large "Bahnhofswartehalle" restaurants, this family-run, smaller restaurant is worth a visit (or several visits). This applies to the extended family as well as to the newly in love couple. Just try it out. 😊 Addendum: I can't understand the strange *negative* one-review-one-star descriptions. One person finds it too hot, another too cold, another doesn't like the dish. Apparently it stinks or something similar. The wrong type of beer... A little tip, then stay at home! No restaurant in the world can satisfy *every* person. That doesn't work either because every person is different. The restaurant is also not allowed to simply turn away customers because they have the wrong hairstyle, someone had bad breath or the women freshen up their 8x4 shortly before the entrance [even worse in front of discos!]. But what you can and can do: A direct discussion on site; This is the only way to bring about a positive change immediately. If necessary, write a polite letter with exact details of the visit and the table, give pictures of the "infraction", etc. A "That was cold there." is difficult to understand later. Just think for yourself, what was there for your 18th birthday or on which wedding days did it rain? These short reviews are intended for foreign guests who prefer a certain type of restaurant or certain dishes. No forum for complainers! If you liked my short review, please leave a 👍 under this review. Thanks in advance.

We went to Uluru Restaurant yesterday for a Valentine's Day meal. A 4-course menu was offered, with a choice of fish or meat. The quality of the food was really good in all four courses. The plates were also presented in an attractive way. Price-performance is therefore consistent. The menu cost €49 per person. The starter was a parsnip soup, which taste-wise was a 10/10. Unfortunately the soup was only lukewarm, which was a real shame! This was followed by two tortillas, which were really delicious - nothing to add! The main course was a great tasteful combination. Unfortunately, this course was quite "manageable" in terms of quantity; one could have possibly asked for a few euros more to fill the plate better. We both decided on the meat option, so we had saddle of lamb, which was really well fried and seasoned - really tasty! For example, a scoop of vanilla ice cream or another component would have gone well with the dessert, a (warm) blueberry muffin with chocolate cream. Because the dessert was quite 'dry'. All in one, a really great menu with tasty experiences. Personally, the menu just left us feeling full. The ambience was deducted one star because we were unfortunately sitting in the farthest corner of the restaurant (which felt like it was in an adjoining room). The restaurant offers a really nice ambience in the main room, unfortunately we only saw this when we went in and out, because the room we were sitting in had a rather less nice ambience. The sum of these smaller criticisms led to a star deduction. We would still visit this restaurant again at any time!

Reservations by telephone are friendly and recommended, as Hoppe's fills up quickly on this Wednesday evening. The service on site is also friendly and attentive, throughout the evening. The atmosphere is cozy, but it quickly gets loud. The menu offers Baden and Alsatian dishes, main courses range between 16 and 26 euros. The cuisine lives up to its reputation. Everything is beautifully served and tastes excellent. Only the Pinot Noir failed to convince me this evening, which the Primitivo more than compensated for. Conclusion: Regional delicacies and excellent service in a central location.

Right now I am in a delightful food coma after visiting this gem of an Italian restaurant in the heart of Ashton Under Lyne. Tonight 10 of us dined here. From the moment I made the booking for my family till we ate our absolute fill & left the restaurant- the staff have been nothing short of wonderful. Upon entering, we were shown to our table by friendly & courteous staff. We ordered drinks & our starters and mains. I had the chicken liver pate for my starter ( much to my family’s dismay as they aren’t fond of it). Though it looked like chocolate mousse & jam to everyone else, I happily tucked into my delicious starter which was followed by a scrumptious flat pasta main with goats cheese & mushrooms in a creamy sauce. Everyone at my tabled loved their food. The pace was perfect, every dish was hot not to mention tasty & everyone’s food arrived together. The staff were super attentive & gave us halal options - the chicken is halal. They also made sure there was no alcohol in any of our orders. What I absolutely loved was that each of our requests were accommodated in a professional & efficient manner - even when we asked if there was somewhere to pray after our meal. We were given a designated space which was hugely appreciated by us. Desserts & hot drinks followed. Again the staff members let us know which ones might contain alcohol. By the time we finished we were very happy & content. It is definitely a restaurant we will be returning to & though my waist line might not thank me for it, I will happily eat my carbs here on a treat day knowing each mouthful is worth the wait! A really lovely experience ~ thank you to all your brilliant staff especially the ones working tonight & hats off to the chef! Dietary restrictions: We asked for halal options ( the chicken is halal ) & for our food to be made without alcohol. The restaurant was super accommodating! Parking: After 6pm its free in the side streets around the restaurant.

In days of yore, it used to be a hallmark of sophistication that one’s village boasted a Thai restaurant in addition to a chippie, Indian and Chinese restaurant. While that position has now been usurped by the Vietnamese restaurant (or Japanese sushi bar if a nouveau hamlet and Cambodian if hipster commune) there’s no denying that it remains the destination of choice for coconut themed spicy hits of flavour. Being on my door step, Phanthong was a place that I often passed en route to somewhere else, so after a night carousing with my Malay and Singaporean (yes, there is a difference!) friends reminiscing about that usual topic - food and where to eat it, the abject lack of Nasi goreng in Hale came up. Thai was considered to be the next best thing now that Angor Soul has departed. Therefore when I drove past today, I seized the day and popped in for lunch. To be fair my bench mark for a decent Thai lunch has to be the nondescript stalls in Chatuchak market rather than the rarefied offerings at 80/20 on Charoenkrung road. In this regard Phanthong scored full marks. The Moo Ping took a few seconds to impress me with subtlety of the marinade. I must decipher it’s secrets to up my summer BBQ game. The Pad Thai was umami and scrumptious mess all rolled into one. The tamarind was not overwhelming as can occur with an inexperienced chef. I chickened out with dessert opting for the safe option. Now I regret not sampling the banana coconut option. While I could be accused of throwing shade here, the folks at Chilli Banana could certainly learn a thing or two from Phanthong.

The food is colourful, interesting and very different. They don't rely on meat substitutes, instead they craft each plant based dish with care and attention to make the veggies shine! My wife really enjoyed the artichoke ceviche whilst I demolished the carrot saltadito and asparagus causa. We also really enjoyed the dragon fruit Tiradito! The drinks are prepared with as much love as the food. Their pisco sours can be made vegan- delicious. I had a nikkei time which was honestly amazing. Can't recommend Chakana enough! Very nice restaurant serving upscale British cuisine. We went there during the week so it was rather quiet, which we actually prefer. The restaurant has a nice bar in the front of the house, where you can enjoy a range of interesting and imaginative cocktails, but they serve classics too. The restaurant part is at the back and you pass an open plan kitchen with bar seats as well, where you can see all the master preparation, it's really interesting! There are normal tables as well obviously, further back. We had a tasting menu with wine pairing. I really enjoyed the finger food that comes before the main menu, but all dishes were great. Some interesting matches, but also some surprisingly simple dishes like a pasta with butter, truffle and cheese, were absolutely delicious, and nicely paired with the wine. You can taste the quality of ingredients, and masterful preparation just completes the dish. The service is impeccable, friendly and knowledgeable. The sommelier was particularly good, clearly knowing his trade, but also very approachable and nice to talk to. The whole menu comes to about 8 or 9 dishes, so it's a lot, and we struggled a bit to finish it all! The experience was very good and I can definitely recommend it.

I cannot recommend Adam's restaurant highly enough! It wasn't our first time in Adam's, but it was the first time in years, after we moved out of Birmingham six years ago and came back recently. We had fond memories from our previous visits, and we were happy to see that nothing has changed in terms of quality of food, service and overall experience. We had the tasting menu with wine pairing, obviously it's not cheap, but the experience is worth the price! Everything was excellent, I cannot think of a dish that I liked the most because each one of them was special - wild bass, scallops, quail with prawns, halibut, beef, were all amazing, with interesting and surprising side pairings that added to the complexity of each dish, and wonderfully paired wine that complimented the food. The service is impeccable, very professional but friendly and approachable, so you can feel being cared for on every step. We are going back, and I would recommend to anyone to do the same! Wheelchair accessibility: There are two steps from the sidewalk leading into the restaurant, but the staff has a ramp and will be happy to assist you. After that it's all on one level, including toilet access. I am not sure about the chef's table experience, I think it's downstairs, and I am not sure if there is a lift - I would recommend checking with the restaurant, their service is impeccable and I am sure they will be able to provide any information you need.

Having dined here on two occasions quite a while ago, my experiences at Adam’s Michelin starred restaurant were quite mixed. The service was impeccable, setting a high standard from the moment I walked in. The food itself was a creative masterpiece, and looked beautiful on the plate, especially the desserts, which were both delicious and decadent. However, the restaurant fell short in a few areas. Firstly, in my opinion it wasn’t very accommodating for vegetarians or vegans and I wouldn’t recommend it if you are, as the menu options may be limited for those dietary preferences. Secondly, the decor lacked the modern or classic elegance expected of such an establishment, feeling more office like. Lastly, the portion sizes left something to be desired, as I left feeling less than fully satisfied on both occassions. Overall, while the quality and creativity were commendable, I'm not personally in a rush to return anytime soon. Parking: I believe the Street parking is free after 7pm. However be sure to confirm at ticket dispenser.

The food itself was a creative masterpiece, and looked beautiful on the plate, especially the desserts, which were both delicious and decadent. However, the restaurant fell short in a few areas. Firstly, in my opinion it wasn’t very accommodating for vegetarians or vegans and I wouldn’t recommend it if you are, as the menu options may be limited for those dietary preferences. Secondly, the decor lacked the modern or classic elegance expected of such an establishment, feeling more office like. Lastly, the portion sizes left something to be desired, as I left feeling less than fully satisfied on both occassions. Overall, while the quality and creativity were commendable, I'm not personally in a rush to return anytime soon. Parking: I believe the Street parking is free after 7pm. However be sure to confirm at ticket dispenser.

So, we craved Middle Eastern magic, and Palmyra's "Special Offer for 3" seemed to cast a spell of deliciousness. Unfortunately, the only magic trick they pulled was vanishing any trace of flavor or freshness. Let's start with the "red meat." Imagine a sunburnt brick that still shivers – that's the level of doneness we're talking about. The chicken shawarma, meanwhile, resembled a mummified parrot, whisper-dry and ancient. And the kofta kebabs? More mystery meat than Middle Eastern delight – I'm pretty sure I saw tumbleweeds rolling out of one. The salad? It was there. That's about all I can say. And the rice, the precious, promised rice for three? Enough for a peckish hamster, maybe. We begged for more, but even Aladdin's lamp wouldn't have conjured another grain. But wait, there's more! Palmyra, in their infinite generosity, threw in two expired beers. Like a bad punchline to a terrible meal. Thankfully, we dodged that bullet faster than Indiana Jones in a tomb – those suds weren't touching our lips. Now, here's the kicker: I have a sneaking suspicion this feast wasn't fresh. It had that "leftover from another table, reheated one too many times" vibe. The dryness, the reheated sighs of spices – everything screamed "secondhand meal." Delivery was fast, though. That's... something. Look, Palmyra, your "special offer" was anything but. It was a culinary crime scene masquerading as a meal. For the love of hummus, save your hard-earned pita and avoid this place like the plague (or any other unappetizing metaphor that comes to mind). Unless, of course, you're a culinary daredevil with a cast-iron stomach and a taste for the questionable. Then buckle up, grab your antacids, and bon appétit! Just don't say I didn't warn you. (P.S. Deliveroo, you rock! Thanks for the refund and the emotional first aid.)

The Vendor name that will show on your credit card statement after visiting The Wilderness is ANOTHER BAD IDEA. Whilst you might think that when you get your next statement and have to pay for it, hopefully the memory of the food and the experience overrides that. Down an alleyway in the JQ, The Wilderness wants to be different to the other Michelin/tasting menu gaffs in Birmingham. And I think they get it spot on. The pop up that they had years ago near New Street was, from memory, a bit more ingredients focused (there was a pudding with ants on it) and had a tree in it. This place is dark walls, dark furniture, guitar music, but I think the food is even better. Every dish on Tasting Menu 2 (there are three in total) was incredible including beetroot ice cream, pig cheeks, mackerel, pigeon. Service was great, wine was a mix of stuff from £40 to a thousand (luckily I didn't succumb to that bad idea), and the whole night was fabulous for our 10th wedding anniversary. Loved it.

We had a high expectations in regards to the food, as to be expected from the Michellin's star restaurant. Food was good, but not excellent, with an exception of the desert (Burnt English egg surprise 10 10 10) - 10 out of 10 for us. We were very surprised to see the bread and butter, that was literally just 4 slices of bread served with two types of butter (one of them was not to our taste). I would say, it would have been OK as a side, but not as a course. We also did not like the snack, that was brought to us while waiting for the table. The staff were friendly, we found the stories interesting and each dish was described, however some of them spoke very quietly so we didn't get the full details with all the courses. They were however very polite and made us feel welcome. We were asked if we wish to have a still or sparking water at the table and we were given the wrong one for the entire 3 hours. It was my birthday and it was noted, I have received a complementary dessert that was nice but not amazing, but definitely a nice touch - thank you. Wine was very good, although pricey (we went for by the glass option). Overall it was a nice experience, but we won't be tempted to come back, unless for the desert only. Our bill for the tasting menu, two bottles of water and 3 glasses of wine was over £370.

We enjoyed an exquisite tasting menu for lunch which didn’t disappoint. As you’d expect the service was on point from the moment you enter and we really felt like we were being looked after in a friendly, efficient way and not overbearing or contrived. As we were driving we can’t comment on the wine pairing… not this time anyway. Definitely thought the menu was priced appropriately and thoroughly enjoyed every mouthful. Highly recommend treating yourself.

Stunning venue in JQ with an assuming front but a grand beautiful inside! As soon as you walk in you’re met with a dark bar but as you go through to the back there’s a bright and airy well designed industrial style restaurant. Food was great but quite expensive although very taste and large portions, well seasoned and a fairly good menu to choose from. We went for a Sunday toast but also look out for the deals they do during the week. Definitely more of a venue where you plan to visit in advance rather than just show up due to how busy it gets and the price. Spent a similar amount as a fine dining restaurant in the area. Would be great for big groups however. Service was friendly and attentive although we had three different servers in the short space of time we were there. Looking forward to my next visit, it’s just the price is more for an occasion rather than a casual visit

Last year, we discovered The Rolling Mill in Birmingham’s Jewellery Quarter and found it to be delicious, so we finally made the decision to return. This time we went for… 🌮 Beef Rib Taco’s 🐑 Marinated Grilled Lamb Cutlets 🍆 Baked Aubergine filled with Ratatouille The beef tacos were absolutely delicious! The flavor was enhanced by the lime mayo, and we can’t express how delicious they were. We regret not ordering more, as one each was definitely not enough. The Lamb Cutlets came with dauphinoise potato, carrot, leeks, mint salsa verde and gravy. Although the lamb was very tasty, we found it to be quite tough and had quite a lot of fat on it, meaning parts were not edible. I did ask for this to be cooked pink and it did come out the way I asked, but unfortunately was still tough. The dauphinoise potato was incredible and full of flavour, we really enjoyed them. The baked aubergine was a new experience for us, and it was gorgeous. The variety of flavors that were present certainly stimulated your taste buds. Although The Rolling Mill’s menu is not extensive, we always find something we want to try and it never fails us. We consistently recommend this restaurant to all and will carry on doing so.

The service was amazing and the place was well decorated and cozy. We started off with Moroccan tea which was delicious then with our starters, we got a small mixed mezza platter and harira soup, I have no words to describe how delicious it was and how eager I am to return. I live in a completely different city and yet I whole heartedly plan to return with my friends to share the experience. Unfortunately, the main dishes were disappointing compared to the appetizers. The fact that I am middle eastern and am used to eating these mains as home cooked meals may make me too judgmental over the food. We got a tahini kofte and mixed shawarma, I found both to be dry though the spicing was not bad. Overall, I will 100% return for the appetizers, tea and a lot more of that harira soup. Ps ( they served 4 grape leaves, but we started off with it before taking the picture) Edit: sure enough, i bought my friends and came back for the appetisers. Safe to say, everyone was very happy and we managed to finish the food plus more soup, some dessert and tea. I truly would recommend going, and the service truly is superb

This was an outstanding find and I really enjoyed the ramen and starters we enjoyed as part of our meal. The ramen really was outstanding - very richly flavoured and filling. We also had the crumbed oyster mushrooms and chicken and actually it was a bit hard to finish it all with the rich ramen as well. The atmosphere is busy but has a nice bustle about it. The staff were helpful and friendly and were able to explain everything on the menu very well. I liked that they had a kombucha as a drink option since I don't really drink alcohol. One thing to note is that the dinner reservations are turned around very promptly and your table is booked for only 1 hour. It is advisable not to turn up too early for your table or expect to lounge around after your allotted booking time. Given that its a ramen place, I think this is entirely appropriate but it is something to consider when booking to eat, especially if its for an occasion. I am still dreaming about the pork ramen I had and fully intend to go again soon. For us, who don't live in central Bristol, we found parking in Cabot Circus convenient since its a 10 minute walk away (and it was easier for us to get out of Bristol after the meal so was convenient for us). Vegetarian options: All the ramens come as either a veggie option or as the meat equivalent. What was not clear to me is whether they offer a veggie option that does not include tofu, as I don't really eat it because it interferes with a medication I take. They were very good with including options that suit most vegetarians and vegans on the regular menu. Dietary restrictions: Ask in advance because the broth has quite a lot of elements in it and they may need to confirm if they can accommodate. I found it a bit strange that they don't offer a chicken ramen option as I would have tended towards that were it offered instead of pork.

When we walked in it was busier which is a good sign. We ordered their platter in starter which consisted of 5 different items. The portion size was huge and delicious. Food was tasty but chicken Thai green curry could have been better. Green curry paste was really thick which downgraded the taste a bit. It's not a place for romantic or fine dining because you won't get such a vibe here. The interior deco is messy and bit weird. They have a different range of light in a different style then different range of wall pictures. It would have been better to have consistency and better decorations throughout.

I'm not too familiar with Hungarian food, probably 'Goulash' is the only dish I'd recognise so I was interested to see what the menu looked like at The Deck. We stood outside and read the Breakfast Menu taped to the window and we were happy with the options available, so we decided to go in. Inside it was warm and slightly damp, the windows were steamed up and covered in condensation. The Cafe isn't huge, but they had a selection of rustic wooden tables and chairs that allowed couples or larger crowds of maybe 6-8 to  eat together but it was a bit tight and not the place for secret or intimate conversations. There were some high stools in the window where (on another day) a lone customers could sit and watch the pedestrian traffic on the pavement outside. We sat at a table just inside the door and were soon given a menu which offered some interesting options to the Full English and I decided on the Meaty Burrito (£7.75) with a Hot Chocolate (£2.55) whilst my wife went for the Hungarian Omelette (£6.95) and a Flat White Coffee (£2.75). The Meat Burrito was a little disappointing. It had very little meat in it. It was advertised as Scrambled egg with Bacon, Chorizo, red Onion and Spinach in a wrap with Cheese and Avocado. I imagined a wrap full of Bacon and Spicy Sausage but It was in fact a 'Scrambled Egg Wrap,' there was very little meat included. It's a pity really as this could have been a great option. If it had been served with a few slices of Bacon or a couple of Sausages, maybe some Hash Browns and a few baked beans it would have been a great breakfast but it was a bit frugal. I enjoyed it but it was nowhere near substantial enough to satisfy the appetite of the Fat-boys breakfast club. My wife enjoyed her choice but again it was 'Scrambled Egg' rather than an Omelette as we know it. Service was friendly and efficient though we weren't very demanding. There were some rather nice looking cakes and pastries available but we decided to resist the temptation and head out into the bitter cold wind of storm Arwen.

The menu showcased a delightful array of traditional Indian dishes, each prepared with a commitment to authenticity and innovation. In every aspect that place stood out as a beacon of excellence, offering an unforgettable dining experience. I wholeheartedly recommend this establishment to anyone seeking a taste of India's rich culinary heritage, where the Prawn Moilee reigns supreme.

Beautiful bright interior with large windows. Open planned kitchen at the ground level with a mezzanine level over it. Lunch menu -2/3 courses. Had the additional course of the spring bites which was really amouse bouch but paid for , 2 items for £6- cheese profiteroles and the foie grae tartlet- latter was amazing , the former average. Bread was average with butter: standard pre-starter item. The starter of Crapaudine which was pulled meat of a Guinea fowl with a layer of rose film/layer over it with two amazing sauces- Apple green colour- beautiful tasting and looking  dish. Mains of lamb was tiny- was on The gamey side with accompanied of two asparagus with a half boiled potatoes and couple of strands of grilled spring onion- good tasting dish but portion size too small. Desert of the honey cake with clove had a honey ice cream and some mead sauce- beautiful dish with a crispy disk. The petit four  of fennel snap and pastle was average. Service was good other than when the menu arrived and it was only the long tasting menu! They should offer the lunch menu when. Providing the menu rather than diners having to ask for it. Please be more generous with main portioning.

We made a reservation for the first day we arrived in Belfast and went to this place, We encountered an excellent quality of service from the moment we entered the restaurant to the moment we left. We tried the tasting menu and encountered multiple factors to influence each course. We really had a very different tasting experience in terms of food. We felt the taste of the dessert we ate change in our mouth even as we ate it, and the way these two tastes went together was wonderful. We had equally great experiences with cocktails and were definitely not disappointed in almost anything we tried. It was a very nice experience in terms of service, each course that arrived was explained in detail and great attention was paid to each one, including special cutlery. Everyone showed incredible interest, especially Isabelle, who helped us have a really good time and increased the quality of our experience with the attention she showed us. Despite certain sensitivities and allergies we showed regarding the food, they adapted the menu accordingly and presented it to us. There was a really elite and retro atmosphere about the atmosphere, this interior design created a very sweet contrast with the light music coming from the background. It was a quality place that met the expectations expected from a Michelin star place. Even though the prices are high due to its quality, we definitely recommend it as a place to try when you come to Belfast.

The Muddlers Club is a Michelin star restaurant in the heart of the Cathedral Quarter in Belfast. We have been wanting to go here for so long and finally had a good excuse to visit! The wait was definitely worth it 😁 The Muddlers Club impressively have a full vegan tasting menu. This was a spread of multiple dishes, with each one being as delicious as the next. We spoke to the servers and found that all the ingredients are sourced locally from an organic farm in NI. This farm only supplies the high end restaurants in Belfast and having tasted the produce I can see why. Each dish was based heavily around local ingredients which was even more impressive as their chefs weren't hiding behind fake meats or protein sources like Tofu, Tempeh or Seitan. This really meant the vegetables could be the star of each dish and with the marinades and perfect preparation, they really did steal the show. The service was excellent, getting a perfect blend between professionalism but also adding a human touch. I will absolute come back here as soon as I possibly can. Well worth the money and an absolute must for foodies in Belfast 😋

The wait was definitely worth it 😁 The Muddlers Club impressively have a full vegan tasting menu. This was a spread of multiple dishes, with each one being as delicious as the next. We spoke to the servers and found that all the ingredients are sourced locally from an organic farm in NI. This farm only supplies the high end restaurants in Belfast and having tasted the produce I can see why. Each dish was based heavily around local ingredients which was even more impressive as their chefs weren't hiding behind fake meats or protein sources like Tofu, Tempeh or Seitan. This really meant the vegetables could be the star of each dish and with the marinades and perfect preparation, they really did steal the show. The service was excellent, getting a perfect blend between professionalism but also adding a human touch. I will absolute come back here as soon as I possibly can. Well worth the money and an absolute must for foodies in Belfast 😋
