Dined here solo On a Saturday night. There were all two other solo tables and with views of the kitchen, can be quite entertaining. Long room with little interior deco- industrial style With an open kitchen and low Lighting The noise levels can get quite high with the lack of soft furnishings Wood tables and wood chairs. Tables are generally low with bronze light lamp on the table Great cocktail- coconut margaritas were excellent as was the chilli caiparinia. Bread In two form: slides sour dough and a ball  was Ok. The pork butter was interesting as was the good oil for dip The trio of amouse bouche was goods and the best was the like the sea trout tartlet The first starters: Torched scallops with broth and half peas with  pea shoots- broth was too sweet made from the pure onion consommé. If it had an extra sugar would suggest reduction. Second starter: Creamed burrata with a pesto sweet sauce with nuts and crispy bread and heritage tomatoes, really worked well as it was creamy, sweet and sour from the tomatoes and a really delight of a dish. First main: Halibut with horse radish and beu blanc, fish wa dry Courgette buttons and asparagus heads Second mains: Salted beef about 30g with a leaf of wild garlic over , a new potato which was boiled and a stalk of asparagus and a small beet root. The beef looked pink but was overdone to be medium tare. The whole dish looked great but was a let down by taste as When all components came to gather it didn’t wow. Pre desert: Rhubarb with peppercorn and Curd With Drink of rhubarb juice and cream On the top was Excellent. Rhubarb was rather fibrous but sweetened. The desert of Coconut cracker , Chocolate cracker , Chocolate mud  and Hazelnut cream was good was both a save dish and did not wow. Niall who provided the service was excellent. Best meal I had in Belfast.

My friend and I were looking for a place to have seafood chowder and found this place on Google map which is luckily located right in front of the hotel we stayed. The seafood chowder was really tasty! I would’ve liked it more if the soup was more creamy but that’s just my preference. The taste was amazing! This place was the first place outside of Japan where I genuinely thought they did an amazing job at making the tempura coating so light and crispy! Hats off to the chefs!! I wish I lived in Belfast, I would’ve gone to this restaurant regularly.

The restaurant had open tables on a Saturday night for a reason. Requested to sit at the kitchen counter, however the lack of magic to witness was uninspiring. The kitchen was cluttered, and the chefs even more so. Dirty shirts, dirty aprons, and pants barely staying up high enough. Disheveled best describes. The kitchen porters appeared better kept. My dining companion is a vegetarian and though we appreciate they recognized the dietary restriction, the options are as underwhelming as the rest of the food to come. We ordered sourdough and olive oil as well as Pan con Tomate. Our mistake for ordering basically the same thing, however it would have been a nice gesture from the waitress to have double checked and asked when we placed our order. Potato Gnocchi - don’t call it gnocchi if it’s going to be potato fondant. Really disappointing, though appreciation to the effort taken to plate it nicely. Pil Pil spice prawns and a the Bertha smoker hanger steak were both ok. Nothing bad, nothing to write home about. Chips however, those were not cooked well. Soggy to the point of unenjoyable. The Pastry Chef and the dessert might be the one saving grace. He was clean and well kept. The Churros followed suit. The appearance of the Chefs is an appropriate reflection to the quality of food.

First of all, we went with high expectations because it was a restaurant on the Michelin list. However, we found the taste of the food, the atmosphere of the place and the attitudes of the employees to be average or below average. Besides the criticisms, we loved the truffle potato croquettes and dessert. We definitely recommend those who visit to try these two but we think the price is not good in terms of performance. For those who are interested, we have listed detailed comments about the food, atmosphere and other topics below. Atmosphere: Considering the capacity of the place, there were more tables than there should have been. This caused us to become very close to the people at the next table. In addition, for this reason, the waiters had difficulty in serving and they frequently hit our chairs, causing discomfort. The place was very noisy in general. Food: There was generally a lack of taste in the food, for example, when eating paella, there was no desired taste. The mussels were very small. We loved the Potato & Truffle Croquettes and ordered them twice. The desserts were also very nice. We also loved the orange, almond & Olive Oil Sponge & Cinnamon Ice Cream and Chilled Chocolate Fondant & Salted Caramel and think they should be tried when you visit. Tortilla de Patatas, pommes pont neuf, truffle & parmesan were not very good. It can be said that there is an average taste range on average. Service: The employees tried to show as much attention as they could. But in our opinion, we sometimes had difficulty expressing some of our requests because they were insufficient in number. Other than that, we agree that they do their best in everything they care about.

Immerse yourself in exquisite experience of flavours, unusual Halloween/dark decor and the friendliest of waiting staff. I've wanted to come back to the 'new' location for a while and booked a table for my birthday. We had a lovely table with very attentive male waiter who didn't shy away to speak Polish with us. Had been given the yummiest drinks. My Apple Pie was so delicious and the glassware just stunning. Nothing was too much trouble. My sister is a very demanding customer and there had been occasions where restaurants found her challenging. However The WitchEZ had made her every quirky request met with a smile and spring in their feet. Definitely the highlight of our visit is the food. We had The Sea for starters, served with a shot of Mad Dog which is my absolute favourite and was made to perfection, sauerkraut and mushroom Pierogi served with rich and flavoursome beetroot borscht and Quarantuna for mains, never skip a dessert! My husband had a crumble which he described as the best he ever had. My little hooves were just as wonderful,  sweet and fluffy as I remembered. It's a hidden gem and hopefully stays hidden as I'd love to come back very soon.

Located in the heart of Cardiff city centre, near the iconic Cardiff Castle, Pasture Cardiff offers a remarkable dining experience. We recently visited to celebrate a birthday with a party of three, and it was a memorable evening from start to finish. The ambience of the restaurant is inviting, with a warm and sophisticated atmosphere that complements its prime location. Our evening began with the attentive and knowledgeable service from our waitress, originally from Palestine. Her expertise in the menu was impressive, providing detailed descriptions and recommendations that enriched our dining experience. Her customer-focused approach was evident, a quality that isn't always found in many restaurants. Our meal started with an array of delicious starters: trout, squid, and crab. Each dish was exquisitely prepared and full of flavour, setting high expectations for the main course. For the mains, we indulged in a 1.2kg Tomahawk steak and a steak and ale pie. Both dishes were exceptional. The Tomahawk steak was cooked to perfection, succulent, and bursting with flavour. The steak and ale pie were hearty and satisfying, with a rich filling that was both comforting and delectable. Unfortunately, despite our desire to try the desserts, the generous portions of the starters and mains left us completely full. Overall, Pasture Cardiff is a top-notch dining establishment that I would highly recommend. From the knowledgeable and attentive staff to the exceptional quality of the food, it is a perfect place for special occasions or a memorable meal in Cardiff.

Went here on 16/02/2024. Made a reservation, it's a small restaurant, popular so best to book. Lovely place, nicely decorated. The 2 members of staff were very sweet and helpful but we felt a bit rushed when we finished especially from the male server.. So, to the food and drinks. All was explained, some items were unavailable but that did not detract. Drinks arrived promptly as did the Thai shrimp crackers, shortly followed by our other 3 starters, Wings, Calamari and Prawns, all delicious, crispy and extremely fresh. Be warned the food has a good chilli kick. We ordered the Chicken Masaman, Prawn Pad Thai, Gai Med Mamuang, and some jasmine rice. All were divine, and the aromatics and flavours were spectacular however, there was one issue. While the prawns were succulent and tender, we all 3 agreed on the 2 dishes with chicken, the texture was overcooked, chewy and dry. I assume they cook the protein separately beforehand and combine with the sauces and coatings, rather than cook it fresh which would make these dishes sensational. It is a pity. I also note that some beef, pork or lamb options would be helpful. Now this is the only negative, we would return but not choose chicken mains unless they change. We came from London for the weekend. They would get five stars across the board except for the rushing at the end and the way the chicken was prepared. Oh! One other thing, the fries are yummy, but the seasoning is definitely not.

Absolutely love coming to The Crown and Pepper, food is so cheap and cheery , especially when you get the 2 meals for £10. Staff are friendly and it’s been refurbished with a lovely Buddha bar and incredible bathrooms . Food has always been to a good standard, the portion sizes are great and service is so fast. I always order the Singapore noodles and salt and pepper tilapia , however the lamb curry and black bean crispy noodles are also delicious . Seen a few complaints about how the food is too spicy now… how about asking the chef for no chilli ? Perhaps that will solve that dilemma . Overall, thoroughly enjoy coming here , I’ve been over 10 times and will continue coming .

restaurant_name: Teriyaki- Japanese restaurant & Bubble tea bar in Coventry
description: Teriyaki, the Japanese restaurant and bubble tea bar in Coventry, is an absolute hidden gem in the city center. I've had the pleasure of dining here several times, and I can confidently say it's one of the best Japanese food experiences I've had in the United Kingdom. My favorite dishes are the Katsu Chicken Curry and Chicken & Shrimp Udon Noodles. The flavors are authentic, and the portions are generous. The owner is super sweet, welcoming, and has a really good attitude, making each visit feel special. The atmosphere is cozy and inviting, which adds to the overall wonderful dining experience. I can't recommend Teriyaki enough. If you're in Coventry, make sure to visit this place for an unforgettable meal! 😍

description: Amazing experience in the newly updated teriyaki (www.loveteriyaki.co.uk) restaurant. Amazing to be able to meet up with ex software engineer Mohamed, who runs this with amazing passion and gumption and has got his priorities absolutely correct! Building from best value wonderfully tasting food, and serving with a great attitude and story. Truly inspirational! If you have a chance , stop by and say Hi and Well Done Mohamed for creating a wonderful dining (and takeaway ) experience ! Go ahead and order ! (Especially to chicken karage! We had 2 more portions after having one for starters at the end of our main meal! That’s how good this was. Well done Mohamed and I wish you and your 2 sons and wife every success in this new business venture and refurbishment to come. Can’t wait to come by when popping back from London! This is better than Karage from some new Malden korean restaurants! Spicy coconatsu chicken was also large and full of vegetables and so tasty with lovely sauce which was just the right spice .

Amazing to be able to meet up with ex software engineer Mohamed, who runs this with amazing passion and gumption and has got his priorities absolutely correct! Building from best value wonderfully tasting food, and serving with a great attitude and story. Truly inspirational! If you have a chance , stop by and say Hi and Well Done Mohamed for creating a wonderful dining (and takeaway ) experience ! Go ahead and order ! (Especially to chicken karage! We had 2 more portions after having one for starters at the end of our main meal! That’s how good this was. Well done Mohamed and I wish you and your 2 sons and wife every success in this new business venture and refurbishment to come. Can’t wait to come by when popping back from London! This is better than Karage from some new Malden korean restaurants! Spicy coconatsu chicken was also large and full of vegetables and so tasty with lovely sauce which was just the right spice .

I had a full course dinner menu at the Cambridge Michelin restaurant, which was quite impressive. I did not expect to be stuffed at a Michelin restaurant given my large appetite… We started off the taste journey with a bite size warm cheese tart, topped with shredded Parmesan. Among the three snacks, my favorite was the rabbit course, which was exquisitely prepared with complex flavors. Featuring a thin, crispy coating with the wild taste of rabbit meat preserved just right. The pre-meal bread was a pleasant surprise and one of the reasons my friend revisited. I'm not usually interested in flaky bread, but the bread itself was moist but not greasy, and I was surprised by its warm feel, easily crumbled crust, and perfectly structured air pockets. Among the three kinds of butter, my favorite was the fermented yeast, which had an unexpected taste of miso. Followed by a custard mushroom soup, the custard was different from the Asian style, resembling cream added, with a garnish of black truffle aroma, overall not bad. The three main courses were pork belly, codfish, and beef. The pork belly was fatty but balanced well with an aggressive sauce similar to "scallion oil"; the final steak was thoughtful, with butter used in a layered potato, the beef tongue and steak were slow-fried, and the bone marrow was stewed into a sauce. However, the codfish was a bit disappointing, although the fish was tender from low-temperature slow cooking, the sauce lacked surprise. The transition before the dessert was clever, with a grapefruit sorbet parfait and lemon jelly making a refreshing, grease-cutting ice cream sandwich. However, the actual dessert was somewhat too heavy, with the caramel almost reaching the viscosity of toffee, overpowering the bitterness of the chocolate itself, which, as a chocolate lover, I only managed to finish with difficulty. Overall, it was delicious, but I feel this menu was not well-balanced between dishes, starting from the very first appetizer, giving a strong sensory impact and easily becoming too rich.

However, the codfish was a bit disappointing, although the fish was tender from low-temperature slow cooking, the sauce lacked surprise. The transition before the dessert was clever, with a grapefruit sorbet parfait and lemon jelly making a refreshing, grease-cutting ice cream sandwich. However, the actual dessert was somewhat too heavy, with the caramel almost reaching the viscosity of toffee, overpowering the bitterness of the chocolate itself, which, as a chocolate lover, I only managed to finish with difficulty. Overall, it was delicious, but I feel this menu was not well-balanced between dishes, starting from the very first appetizer, giving a strong sensory impact and easily becoming too rich.

I had a full course dinner menu at the Cambridge Michelin restaurant, which was quite impressive. I did not expect to be stuffed at a Michelin restaurant given my large appetite… We started off the taste journey with a bite size warm cheese tart, topped with shredded Parmesan. Among the three snacks, my favorite was the rabbit course, which was exquisitely prepared with complex flavors. Featuring a thin, crispy coating with the wild taste of rabbit meat preserved just right. The pre-meal bread was a pleasant surprise and one of the reasons my friend revisited. I'm not usually interested in flaky bread, but the bread itself was moist but not greasy, and I was surprised by its warm feel, easily crumbled crust, and perfectly structured air pockets. Among the three kinds of butter, my favorite was the fermented yeast, which had an unexpected taste of miso. Followed by a custard mushroom soup, the custard was different from the Asian style, resembling cream added, with a garnish of black truffle aroma, overall not bad. What a great experience. The service was really spot on. Greeted at the door by the waitress and got a nice table. Seating was comfortable and the overall environment inside was really nice. Not overboard but really well done. The music was on light enough to hear and not be overwhelmingly loud. Ordered drinks right away and an appetizer that came out quickly and was quite enjoyable. The meals themselves came out in a timely manner. We never felt rushed or anxious about getting our food, or being rushed to eat. We got two different chicken meals and both were moist and delicious and really didn’t need any sauces although I did use some of the garlic and chili sauce, quite sparingly because the taste was really on point. Got an order of sutlac for desert and it was plentiful to split between two of us. Closed the meal off with some Turkish tea that was quite delightful. I have two days left in London and you can count on my last meal being here.

Manager needs to work on his demeanour, set an incredibly poor tone from the offset. As someone who’s dined very often and trained in south Asian cuisine, this was unfortunately something that fell short of the mark. Service was cold with no warm spirit, when enquiring on recommendations or house favourites we were met with a ‘read the menu’, the establishment was empty but the waiters had to let us know how busy it normally is. Butter chicken was made overly sweet with a pre-made sauce, saag paneer whilst the paneer was cooked well was presented in an overly oily spinach base and the naan’s were overdone in the tandoor coming out hard. Chicken tikka masala previously recommended by a colleague was something he did not enjoy on this visit, noting how dousing it with red food colouring/ratanjot doesn’t detract from the lack of authentic masala. For the area, the restaurant is an option with limited choices to enjoy this cuisine, the food is okay but comparative to many others in other cities nearby, this falls far short of the mark on service and quality.

description: Frankly, this eatery deserves the overwhelming amount of 5-star reviews that it's received! The value is unbelievable and the portions are very generous. The food is also flavoursome and beautifully presented. I cannot recommend this venue enough; my parents and I were all extremely satisfied with the whole experience. Additionally, if you choose to eat in and you visit the furthest dining space from the stairs there's a hidden surprise... Namely, a remnant of the city's former walls! History and noodles!? What more could a guest want? Well, a drink would be nice but the venue informed is they're getting an alcohol license issued soon which I'm sure will complete the package!

If you are in search of a delightful dining experience, look no further than the Bridgeview Station Restaurant. A charming haven that has consistently served up excellent cuisine, it has stolen my heart and won my palate on multiple visits. The food at Bridgeview Station Restaurant is nothing short of spectacular. Each dish is a testament to the meticulous attention to detail and the pursuit of culinary perfection. The club sandwich, an often-underrated staple, is elevated to a gastronomic delight here. Layered with the freshest ingredients and bursting with a symphony of flavours, it leaves you craving more. The soup is yet another standout dish. Rich, warming and wonderfully balanced, it's the kind of comfort food that soothes your soul on a chilly day. The chefs at Bridgeview Station Restaurant have truly mastered the art of crafting a memorable soup, and it's a must-try on every visit. As for beverages, the lager is light, refreshing, and the perfect companion to the delightful dishes. It's the kind of beer that you can savour on a sunny day on the patio, enjoying the beautiful views as you sip. What makes this restaurant even more special for me, is the memories it has helped create. My mother and I have been frequent patrons, and each visit to Bridgeview Station Restaurant is a cherished experience. From the warm welcome we receive, to the last satisfying bite, it's a restaurant that has earned a special place in our hearts. The ambience, the views, the friendly staff, the impeccable service, and most importantly, the exquisite food - all come together to create a dining experience that's truly unparalleled. Whether you're a local or just passing through, Bridgeview Station Restaurant is a destination not to be missed. In conclusion, if you're looking for a restaurant that combines an inviting atmosphere with delicious food and drink, then Bridgeview Station Restaurant should be your top choice. From personal experience, I wholeheartedly recommend this restaurant - it's a culinary journey that you won't regret embarking on.

We got hallumi fries and nachos to start, they brought the kids pizza and chips with our starters which was a good call as they were boiling hot. Mains we got the chicken surf and turf and the chicken stir fry. Hubby enjoyed his surf and turf, my stir fry was a little lack lustre, it was more like par boiled  veg and a tiny bit of chicken in an average tomato sauce (that tasted like hubby's prawns had been in the same pan). It was OK but boiling hot and took ages to cool to a decent temperature due to being in the skillet. The chips were the best bit. £32.50 (eat out to help out) for 4 mains, 2 starters, 2 soft drinks,1.5 pints of lager and 2 cocktails. 8/10 only because my meal was just OK, will return but will choose something else off the menu.

Since the restaurant was open, I have been coming to the Indian Palace. On each occasion, I was pleasantly surprised with the freshly, homemade quality of genuine south Indian cuisine. I always start with poppadoms and dips (most of them are home made, and utterly tasty), than I go for kerala paratha (as a starter, I discovered this type of bread for the first time in this restaurant), as a main, molly made with the prawns (the best every, mild, made with coconut milk) combined with the pashwari naan and plain rice, presents the perfect meal! Sometimes, I drop by for a lunch, there is a buffet just for 8.99 on workdays. There are always (among other dishes) lamb and chicken curry, the lamb curry is spice but perfect taste! The other day, the restaurant wasn't that busy during the lunch time, and the waiter (all members of staff are always really pleasant and welcoming), Siv introduced me to the chef, really humble, still amazing talent! The prices are more than reasonable, hence if you want Indian food check out this place!

restaurant_name: Ty'r Winch pub- restaurant and guest house
description: The ambiance was amazing. 17th century buildings gives a cosy vibe. The service was 10/10 I would give 5/5 stars but only if the beef was freshly ground and not a pre-made patty. The lack of seasoning was a letdown. But the fish and chips was well worth the visit. I will return and try more items from the menu. Food & drinks: This was my first time visiting the restaurant so I haven’t had many items from the menu. I tried the fish and chips, it was excellent the cod was cooked perfectly the batter was light and crispy the chips were crispy and delicious. The homemade tartare was perfect. The beef burger was not amazing. If a restaurant of this calibre doesn’t ask you how well would you like the burger cooked just know it’s not going to be fresh ground beef. It will most likely be a pre-made patty.

We recently had a meal for 14 for our wedding here at Rocco's, and it was worth the wait and the 25minute drive! Some guests had starters some didn't, but all our food came out piping hot and all dishes were absolutely beautiful to look at, and definitely gorgeous to eat!   We could not fault anything, the service was fantastic, all the servers were very attentive, and very quick with everyone's meals, and drinks. I myself had mussles in the garlic and white whine, followed by black artisan pasta with king scallops,  king prawns, mussles with a prawn butter sauce,...I've never tasted anything like it! Both courses were beautiful! And I ended my meal with the sublime Torta Della Nonna, a lemon and pine nut tart, a must have slice of naughtiness! Please go, you won't be disappointed.... its a little piece of Italian HEAVEN in St.Mary's Court, Tickhill. We will definitely be back....Thankyou! X

Been wanting to come here for a very long time after driving/walking past it, and my partner has wanted to come here since she’s moved here. Hand sanitizer upon arrival with track & trace check in code. All the staff are very welcoming, friendly, helpful and all very masks. The lady we had who served us throughout our time (apologise I forgot her name began with A I think), she couldn’t have been anymore helpful. With a very wide range of food, she told us everything on the menu was very nice as she has tried everything! The decor of the restaurant is what I’d expect in a typical Italian restaurant, very rustic and has a feel of being in Italy. To start I had the belly pork with Jack Daniels sauce, I’ve never tried belly pork and it was so tasty and very tender. My other half had the goats cheese in filo pastry which was also very nice. For mains, I had the Risotto con salsiccia (spicy sausage, peppers, onions, garlic, tomato and chilli). It was so nice I’m glad it was a big portion as I wanted more! I don’t think the sausage was spicy but overall I was very impressed. Other half had a cheese chicken & mushroom calzone which was also nice. We had a nice bottle of white wine which absolutely complimented the whole meal. For dessert I had sorbet and other half had a deep fried cannoli once again both really nice. Reasonable priced meal for two people, and very highly recommended. Plenty parking and we will be back soon with our family. Very authentic home cooked Italian food and Cafe Casita is way better than some of these chain restaurants!!

I have visited Kanpai Sushi twice for lunch in the summer of 2021 in a small group and a dinner in a larger group recently. Really nice: - extensive menu, large restaurant that is relatively calm and quiet with the sushi chefs working at a visible counter. - the ice creams are delicious - some of the sushi dishes are creative and delicious too (liked the maki wrapped in buckwheat) Room for improvement: - the service can get rather slow in the busy times and we got some of our orders confused while acting annoyed :( - the sizes of the dishes are difficult to predict, some nigiri sushi and sashimi can be very small. Make sure to confirm. I would probably try it again when it's calmer for lunch.

It was quite surprised while I saw this restaurant with the same company name I work for in 2019. But I was traveled alone so didn’t have a chance to try, after 2 years finally got an opportunity to enjoy the dinner with my friend and K here in Edinburgh. The menu isn’t only opinion for sushi, but also has some Japanese fusion dishes. Fresh, authentic, and overall a great vibe. 🍃Environment: Modernly decoration, medium containing space, and here has a heightened sense lively atmosphere in bar for grabbing a drink. 🛎️Service: We had reservation at 8:30pm, but waited for about 15-30 mins to get our seat. As we all work for food & beverage, we think it’s acceptable. But the waiters were obviously not enough for service so we had waited for a bit longer to get our drinks in the waiting area. So I deducted a star for the service. 🍽「Crowned Tuna Tartare」 Fresh tuna is served with vinegar rice and refreshing sauce, a delicious appetiser can perfectly pair with Japanese sake. 🍽「Sashimi Combo」 I was very surprised that seafoods here in Edinburgh can be so good and fresh, tasted even better with a little bit wasabi and soy sauce. 🍽「Teppan Scotch Beef Sirloin 8oz」 Highly recommended NOT to order beef when you’re having meal in a sushi restaurant. I asked for medium-rare, but it came with iron plate so obviously overcooked. What a pity! It seems very popular and you have to make a reservation for sure.

Simply overrated.  Not an authentic Japanese restaurant.  The food alone was not so bad and could still easily secure 3 or marginally 4 stars.  However, this poor review was about how they chose to run a restaurant and the way they treated their customers. In terms of food, the biggest miss was messing up the supposedly light and airy Japanese tempura batter.  If you enjoy Japanese food, you would probably admire the careful juxtaposition of ingredients altogether, of which the skills were lacking in this restaurant.  Sashimi was of a small portion but being plated in an oversized bowl for presentation, etc. In terms of services, unreasonably rude!  30 min after I was seated and had just started eating, I was told to leave in another 30 min's time.  I was not told about the time restriction at the beginning.  Besides, from my observation of the table next to me (also a solo diner), she was given 90 min to eat and the message was communicated at the beginning when she was seated. I had to admit that I did have some expectation for a £60 meal per person (food only, no wine).  Even a fast-food type sushi store would not kick me out of the premises when my mouth was full.  By the time I left the restaurant as they wanted, the restaurant was not even 20% full. It gave me the impression that they only cared about making money, put the food on your table and urged you to leave.  They did not care whether you needed time to eat them!  They had no passion to take Japanese food as an art form.  No respect to diners whatsoever.  They did not even know how to run a regular restaurant with their bookings and front-of-house work.

Probably one of the most enjoyable Michelin Star restaurants we have experienced. It started with incredible service. I was extremely impressed by the ownership every single person in the restaurant had. Every organization has a hierarchy… it was not clear what it was here as every person was responsible for any and every last detail of providing excellent service (even ones that were not part of the team taking care of our table). At one point, my wife dropped her napkin and within seconds a random person showed up and handed her a clean one. Now we can talk about the delicious food. Every dish had sauces that had us wanting to lick the plate. Each and every dish was expertly crafted creating a beautiful multi sensory experience. We will be back the next time we’re in Edinburgh. A truly completely marvelous evening!!

This place offers reasonably priced but delicious tasting menu. The small bites and first two courses on the menu did not do much for me, but things picked up quite well after the turbot. The turbot and the game birds were handled expertly. As a matter of fact, this place offer some of the best food that I have had. Service was okay. It felt that they paid more attention to certain customers than others. Compared to the other one-Michelin-star places in town, Timberyard had the least impressionable service. The selection for wine by glass is quite limited as well. The ambiance is modern and cool. It looks like they repurposed a factory or warehouse into a restaurant. The restroom has this cool sound in the hand washing area. Overall, this would have been a perfect dinner if the service were better.

We had the best South Indian (Kerala) food experience after a very long time here. Will definitely be back for yet another variety of meals. Talking about the food: Their Porotta beef varattiyathu combo was top notch with authentic flavours and very good amount of gravy and meat. The Alfahm Mandi was another dish we enjoyed. And we had their Malabar Dum Biriyani and Porotta Chicken combo which was really good too. Coming from India being able to enjoy the native dishes right here near to the heart of Edinburgh city makes us less homesick and it is really budget friendly comparing to the other so called Indian restaurants which serves below average meals with a very expensive menu. Overall, the food, atmosphere, customer service and the time we had there really made us worth the visit.

As first-time visitors to Scotland, we approached our dining experience with curiosity. The cuisine generally impressed us with its preparation and appealing flavors. However, two dishes fell short of expectations. The Bone Marrow pie, while visually enticing and aromatic, lacked the robust taste we anticipated. The Crispy lamb shoulder, though enjoyable, left us wanting in terms of portion size and could have benefited from additional vegetable accompaniments. Despite these minor setbacks, our overall culinary journey was satisfactory. It's worth mentioning that the bartender was exceptionally helpful in explaining the whisky flight options. For whisky enthusiasts, Scran would be a good choice.

This was our first Michelin experience for our first wedding anniversary. Been looking forward to it for months. The food was exceptional as expected. So were cocktails and wine paring. The staff were lovely and attentive and we had and amazing time while there. Value for money too. However, I have to give only 4 out of 5 stars. This is because we were charged £90 for not turning up. My wife noticed this in the taxi after we left. She called the restaurant to make sure this wasn’t the case and only a mistake as we were clearly there. But, the money came out the account. My wife emailed them. They acknowledged there was another table booked in a different name but with our contact details etc and we would get our money back in 5-10 days as a “Gesture of goodwill on this occasion”. That statement seemed a bit snippy to me like it was our fault. Took a bit of the shine off the whole experience to be honest. I would still recommend as everything except this was great and hopefully this was just a one off error.

The Kitchin, nestled in the heart of Edinburgh, offers a dining experience that truly captures the essence of Scottish cuisine. On my first visit, I was immediately struck by the warm, welcoming atmosphere. The staff's friendliness made me feel like a long-time regular, setting the tone for an exceptional afternoon. Opting for the prestigious tasting menu with an additional cheese course, I embarked on a three-hour culinary journey. The kitchen's commitment to sourcing produce from various regions of the UK was evident in every dish. Each plate showcased the top-quality ingredients, skillfully prepared to highlight their natural flavors. While the presentation may lack the ornate aesthetics often associated with French cuisine, the flavors more than compensated. The chefs' expertise shone through in their ability to coax out the best from each ingredient, proving that substance can indeed triumph over style. The tasting menu was a well-orchestrated symphony of tastes, demonstrating both the diversity of British produce and the kitchen's technical prowess. From start to finish, each course reaffirmed The Kitchin's reputation as a standard-bearer for modern Scottish cuisine. Though my first visit, it certainly won't be my last. The Kitchin has earned its place on my must-visit list for future trips to Edinburgh. For those seeking a true taste of Scotland, expertly prepared and served with genuine hospitality, The Kitchin is an experience not to be missed.

Currently the best Indian restaurant I've found in Exeter.  Fabulous food with lots of different tastes and flavours away from the usual list of'standards' that most restaurants serve. Booking is essential as the previous time we tried to visit, people were queueing out the door waiting for tables. My starter was the Mushroom Manchurian which was absolutely delicious. In fact 3 of us had  different Manchurian starters and they were all equally good, with one of us having the Chicken 65 which almost had an Indochine flavour to it and was also very good. My main was the Chettinadu Chicken Curry which was also just as food as the starter. There was an interesting array of breaks available too which I've never seen before in any other restaurant including Poori and Baturas that puff up when fried and looked amazing. The range of Dosas looked very interesting too so I think I need to revisit again to try these different dishes. Needless to say I shall definitely be returning! Kid-friendliness: Very kid friendly with a kids menu and  there were a number of families dining when we were there.

There’s hardly anything I could fault on my experience dining at Fhior. The experience has been amazing throughout and deserving of a Michelin star. First of all, the food was amazing, the very essence of fine dining to the core. Each portion was tiny, designed to introduce new excitements on the palate. My partner and had a really fun time joking about it, that it was a very delicious potato fry, or that the resto only need to order a whole duck for the whole restaurant’s dining operation that evening, and more giggling moments about each dish story. In truth, we enjoyed every moment, each dish was really delicious and by course number 7, we were happily full. The service was lovely, attentive, and very courteous, the type of service we haven’t experience in a western restaurant in a long time (exceed London level). We saw that each server had to lead on introducing certain dish, abd they did really well for such complex descriptions! We received really nice courteous goodbye at the end of our meal which really finished the experience with a great big smile. I felt proud for booking Fhior for my partner’s 40th birthday. Atmosphere lastly was next to none. Again, very strong attention to detail. Tables were nicely spaced away from each other, giving a nice sense of privacy. The music was turned at the right volume and was really complementary to the food and to being in Scotland. Very simple decor but very high quality, we loved the little touch to having special knife for chopping few bits of duck (another chuckle for us). Another big plus was that unlike london restaurants, we were not hurried out after 2 hours allotment. Overall really a michelin star experience and zi would love to come back again!!!

I recently had the pleasure of enjoying lunch at Hook Fish & Chips, and it’s safe to say it was an unforgettable experience. From the incredible food to the warm service and inviting atmosphere, this place is a seafood lover’s paradise. I started with their classic fish and chips, and it was a revelation. The fish was unbelievably fresh, coated in a perfectly light and crispy batter that wasn’t greasy at all. The chips were equally fantastic—crispy on the outside and soft on the inside, seasoned just right. A standout addition to the meal was the curry sauce. This rich, savory sauce added an amazing depth of flavor to the fish and chips, with just the right amount of spice to elevate the dish without overpowering it. It was a delightful twist that made each bite even more enjoyable. To complement the main dish, I also tried their onion rings, and they were a highlight in their own right. These golden rings were crispy and flavorful, with a perfect balance between the crunchy exterior and the tender onion inside. Paired with the curry sauce, they were an absolute treat.

Fine dining but not much else. As the first in the restaurant, it was nice having the place to myself in the corner for the first several minutes enjoying the quiet. Quickly the entire room filled up with reservations and the normal chatter of a restaurant filled the air. Ordering the tasting menu I expected to be given a rundown of ingredients and locations with each dish but sadly was not. A simple repeat of the ingredients in each dish as it was set down and that was it. The dishes were delicious, make no mistake. I left satisfied but not full, the tasting menu included dessert and a cheese plate was added in as well. Two glasses of wine to pair with the dishes. The staff were quick about and courteous, clearing plates, placing new cutlery, filling water glasses and cleaning wine glasses. Again, I did expect more description and sourcing of the dishes. Seated at noon I left by 2:30, a solid lunch. Overall it was a nice experience but left me wanting more. Sadly didn't have the same impact as a similar restaurant down the street did upon first visit. This place is a gem with outstanding quality and an unbelievably low price. There were quite a few worrying things about coming here - Google says only 4.1*, clunky website and entire place empty at lunchtime. But wow, steaks were fantastic, on par with the best steakhouse in London. Chips were also really good - in that rare category of on another level compared to most. My little boy had a mango and ice cream smoothie which he announced as the best drink he'd ever had - and it was delicious. Decor is also very nice, a good mix of wood and white leather. Pricing is the lowest I've ever seen in a steakhouse, which is amazing given the quality. Only thing that let it down is the 'white chocolate and raspberry cheesecake' had no raspberry at all. I also couldnt tsste any white chocolate. And apparently they were missing the 'dressing sauce' which they didn't mention until serving it. This definitely should have been mentioned sooner, and combined with providing a different cheesecake to that on the menu let the place down quite a lot. Hopefully this place is busier in the evenings, it absolutely deserves to be, at least if they sort their deserts out. If it was in Brighton or London it would be constantly packed. Given the high-end quality and the extremely reasonable price, this is almost certainly the best value steakhouse in the UK. Absolutely recommended.

Amazing 🤩 literally stumbled across this place as the place we were going to eat was closed. It did not disappoint, we decided to go for the 40oz rump as it worked out not that much more than 2 normal sized steaks and what a decision. The waiter was super friendly and my wife and him bonded over music taste, I wasn’t so keen on Michael Bolton, but they were enjoying it. The restaurant was nicely kitted out and they had a great selection of steaks. When the steak came out it was perfectly cooked and the sauces and chips and onion rings were incredible too. I had a virgin mojito as I was driving and that was really nice, had I had more space I would have liked to try the milkshakes, but the meal was enough to feed us twice over, that didn’t upset me as I now have some cracking meat to cook a meal at home with. We will definitely be returning in the near future, I don’t usually have steak out as I can cook it home, but this was definitely worth it. Parking: There’s a parking lot round the corner on the industrial estate.

Wow!! Absolutely amazing experience from start to finish. The only downside was the lack of parking but the extra effort was totally worth it. As a non meat eater there were several options and I went for seabass that was cooked to perfection on a bed of the most decadent and delicious mash I have ever tasted. The arancini starter was delightful with wonderful texture and the fresh ingredients just sang.. My meat eating boyfriend was utterly in his element, salivating over the entire menu and eventually opted for the lunchtime combo of steak and ribs with chicken wings for starters. We were slightly beaten by the generous portions but 100% recommend..if you go.. go hungry and go again and again! Has easily slipped in to the top spot of best Farnham eatery for us..in no small part down to the amazing service we received from Daniel who was warm, welcoming and knowledgeable.. discreetly keeping us topped up and well cared for without at all hovering. Cannot wait to come back.. thank you for making this a special birthday experience for us!!

A much smaller restaurant than I expected after looking at the website and menu online but it's cute and very Italian. My daughter said she felt like she was in the Disney movie Luca. The service is extremely friendly and the food quality is good buy overall there are some problems I would fix before I could recommend or return. With so many restaurant options available and many Italians to choose from, you have to stand out and I think Marcus falls short on a couple of things. Firstly the menu is somewhat limited and uninspiring given the costs of some of the options. It's a little pricey and the portions are not big. The second issue is that the mains come with nothing but the meat or fish described. I really find it hard to rate a restaurant high, who charge a high price for the dish but can't put a few chips/salad or veg on the plate. By the time you add them on it becomes a very expensive meal in quite a simple looking restaurant. With this in mind there are far better options locally that don't fail on the two things mentioned, so unless they are remedied, I will not be returning or recommending

Mind-blowing food at Madras Cafe. Went it on a Saturday afternoon. The restaurant was quiet. I’m a fuzzy eater. Was looking for something lite for lunch. The menu looked appealing and was in a dilemma about which dish to take. Thanks to the waiter who helped me when I told him to pick something lite for me. Had a South Indian mixed vegetables dish with lentils and the classic chicken tikka. Both of them were outstanding. Could taste the freshness of vegetables. The chicken had a smokey flavour of coal which I guess was cooked in a clay oven run by coal. The meat here was surprisingly not dry like other places I ate in. Thanks to Madras Cafe for their incredible food and service. Will return and definitely recommend it to my friends.

What a lovely warm reception we were given at Amanzi tonight. We were looking forward to trying the restaurant after reading great reviews and we were not disappointed. It was difficult to choose - but we eventually settled on ribs and the ostrich sosatie. We'd recommend both! Our compliments to the chef, because the ostrich, which is a lean meat, wasn't overcooked or dry. The meat chunks were a good size and had been seared well on the braai, with apricot and bacon between. The pork ribs fell off the bone and had a delicious sweet, smokey sauce. Remember it's South African portions, so maybe arrive half starved. And don't forget to book. We're so glad to have found Amanzi and it will definitely be an essential part of our Cornish holidays.

All in all a great family friendly restaurant with very authentic Indian food.

Me and my partner went to the Blue Sky Lounge for our dinner after the stadium tour and had a lovely meal. Top points - Card only payments - Is Wheelchair Accessible We went on a Sunday and the carvery was on, the food was fantastic and staff were excellent. We had a clean booth with comfortable seats and strong tables overlooking the stunning Ibrox pitch. It was a starter, carvery and dessert for £37. The starters, a choice of pâté or lentil soup were served quickly and were absolutely delicious, at the carvery you can get 4 different kind of meats we had a bit of everything (Turkey, beef, chicken and pork), lots of different side dishes including massive Yorkshire puddings, mac n cheese, cauliflower cheese, roast and mashed potatoes, roasted veg and mixed veg, with an option of 4 desserts (Chocolate Mousse, Vanilla Cheesecake, Chocolate fudge cake and apple crumble. My partner and I were very happy with the food and really feel like we got our moneys worth. Would recommend to rangers supporters of any vintage and tourists who are in the area and looking for a great meal. Wheelchair accessibility: Ramp accessible with lift

Short version – 10/10 Food was wonderful, blown away. Staff were so friendly and offered great service, top notch. Long version: My daughter started working there a few weeks ago. She impressed upon us how good the food was and how they made it all from scratch. She also told us how welcoming and knowledgable all the staff were and how excited she was to work there. My daughter told us about the menu and sounded right up our street. So we booked a table for a Saturday afternoon, to try it out. We don’t really visit Uddingston too often, we live about 10 miles away and have good eateries close by. So hadn’t even seen the restaurant. Easy to get to on the main street and we got parked just round the corner. We got greeted straight away and were seated in a nice table for two at the window. The décor and ambience of the place was very nice. The staff were smily and open which is always a good sign. For starters there was a special of King Scallops, with Asparagus, chorizo and bacon, which I went for and the good lady wife choosing the Chicken and Duck liver parfait with caramelized onion  with toasted brioche. The Scallop dish was amazing. I’m going to make the first of 2 comparisons to the ‘Come dine with me’ series. I have had Scallops only twice before and a long time ago, they were nice but that's all I can remember. In ‘Come dine with me’ hosts were forever getting slaughtered for cooking them too long, making them tough. At Smiths I reckon I got them exactly how they were supposed to be cooked. They were tender and succulent, slightly seared and tasty as you would like. Went so swell with the rest of the dish, absolute dynamite. I didn’t get a taste of the wifes parfait (its not my cup of tea) but the good lady scoffed it all with not a crumb left on the dish. She really enjoyed it. My daughter had put forward a recommendation to us to try the blade of beef in particular as that came with the mashed potato that she stated was outstanding.  The good lady went for this, I was humming over getting the steak, but hey I have had steak plenty of places and its very specific and cooked on the spot, but wanted to to try something from the main menu. I went for chicken breast which was lightly smoked and roasted, with glazed carrot, roast Thyme gravy and Arran mustard crushed potatoes. Second reference to come dine with me. They always slam the host for the chicken don’t they? Too tough, dried out, or even worse, the dreaded pink. Oh not at Smiths. Wow, eye opener, this is how chicken is supposed to be cooked. Hands down in 52 years on this planet eating solid food, that chicken on Saturday was the best I have ever tasted. It honestly was something else. I need to look at how I cook chicken because it aint like this. The delicate smoky taste through the succulent breast. It was a wonderful sized portion and the potatoes, my ow my, these were outstanding. The mash which I sampled from my Mrs plate was very good, but the Arran mustard crushed variant with spring onions mixed through it – wowee, absolutely splendid. I had a go at the good ladies dish. It was a slow braised feather blade of Scotch beef in a rich red wine jus. Tender as a kiss from an angel, beautiful. Plates scoffed, almost licked clean. For desert the waitress recommended the Vanilla Rice pudding with Rhubarb, apple and ginger crumble topping, as it was her favourite and described it as a ‘warm hug’ and who doesn’t like a warm hug?  We were tempted to get two of these, but I fancied trying something else out on the menu, knowing fine well I would be stealing a bit of my ladies ‘warm hug’, so went for the nutella cheesecake with Pistachio ice cream with a raspberry coulis. Wonderful combination it was as well. Fabulous and so delicious. I did have a couple of spoonfuls of the rice crumble dish, this was superb as well. The rice, so creamy, the crumble so tasty. Not a scrap left on any of hour plates on any of the courses. Magical experience and would thoroughly recommend.

In ‘Come dine with me’ hosts were forever getting slaughtered for cooking them too long, making them tough. At Smiths I reckon I got them exactly how they were supposed to be cooked. They were tender and succulent, slightly seared and tasty as you would like. Went so swell with the rest of the dish, absolute dynamite. I didn’t get a taste of the wifes parfait (its not my cup of tea) but the good lady scoffed it all with not a crumb left on the dish. She really enjoyed it. My daughter had put forward a recommendation to us to try the blade of beef in particular as that came with the mashed potato that she stated was outstanding.  The good lady went for this, I was humming over getting the steak, but hey I have had steak plenty of places and its very specific and cooked on the spot, but wanted to to try something from the main menu. I went for chicken breast which was lightly smoked and roasted, with glazed carrot, roast Thyme gravy and Arran mustard crushed potatoes. Second reference to come dine with me. They always slam the host for the chicken don’t they? Too tough, dried out, or even worse, the dreaded pink. Oh not at Smiths. Wow, eye opener, this is how chicken is supposed to be cooked. Hands down in 52 years on this planet eating solid food, that chicken on Saturday was the best I have ever tasted. It honestly was something else. I need to look at how I cook chicken because it aint like this. The delicate smoky taste through the succulent breast. It was a wonderful sized portion and the potatoes, my ow my, these were outstanding. The mash which I sampled from my Mrs plate was very good, but the Arran mustard crushed variant with spring onions mixed through it – wowee, absolutely splendid. I had a go at the good ladies dish. It was a slow braised feather blade of Scotch beef in a rich red wine jus. Tender as a kiss from an angel, beautiful. Plates scoffed, almost licked clean. For desert the waitress recommended the Vanilla Rice pudding with Rhubarb, apple and ginger crumble topping, as it was her favourite and described it as a ‘warm hug’ and who doesn’t like a warm hug?  We were tempted to get two of these, but I fancied trying something else out on the menu, knowing fine well I would be stealing a bit of my ladies ‘warm hug’, so went for the nutella cheesecake with Pistachio ice cream with a raspberry coulis. Wonderful combination it was as well. Fabulous and so delicious. I did have a couple of spoonfuls of the rice crumble dish, this was superb as well. The rice, so creamy, the crumble so tasty. Not a scrap left on any of hour plates on any of the courses. Magical experience and would thoroughly recommend.

On the Main Street of Uddingston (near train station). Interesting menu, 3 course £30 and 2 course £25. Party of four, had pate with brioche  and scallops with black pudding to start. The scallops had £6 surcharge, only two scallops but superb. For main we had a beef blade with roasted veg and baked cod (one cod made gluten free) with chowder.  Really nice. For dessert ice cream which was good and the cheese platen(£3 supplement). Two glasses pinot Grigio and two glass house Spanish rose. Both excellent. I knocked off a star for the cheese plate. Everything else was super, but the cheese was too cold and tasted like supermarket. No names given for what was served. It was disappointing. We should have had the desert.  A great meal and well worth a visit. £143 without tip, added 10 % Dietary restrictions: Excellent my parter said gluten free and chosen dish altered without fuss. Parking: It’s a busy street. We had blue badge passenger so parked outside. Very busy on street otherwise. Wheelchair accessibility: Parking outside for disabled (family member has badge) and easy in but toilet impossible. Family member waited to go at home.

For a spring theme we expected the dishes to have a fresh and light flavour. Instead, it was overly salty and one of the dishes was basically macaroni and cheese with bacon. How is that a spring flavour? I drank 4 glasses of water with the 10 dishes cause I was so dehydrated with how salty everything was. We really enjoyed 2 out of the 10 dishes. I would come back again to try a different menu, but really think the Spring one is not a success... Also, who serves a block of cheese as dish #8 when people are already stuffed? Could have definitely been presented better.

Wheelchair accessibility: Ramp/easily accessible for anyone with a wheelchair!

restaurant_name: Royal Oak Inn & Knife & Cork Restaurant
description: The review for the Royal Oak Inn, this place I travelled a little outmy  way, to try this place, as never been. Didn't know what to expect. There was plenty of parking and the place was clean. The waitress was very polite and asked all the right questions. Food service was ok coming from the kitchen, so no long waiting times. Menu was many choices all a little upper class from a standard pub. The food was good, and the scampi chips are my standard meal in all places as then  i can compare. This time, it's one of the best. Real chips and plenty of scampi, therefore no complaints. Overall, it was a nice place and good service . It was not a bad price as I took the option of two dishes and set price. Had to be done main mean and dessert 🍨. Just over £20 including drinks I had.

restaurant_name: Royal Oak Inn & Knife & Cork Restaurant
description: We were seated in the bar which was a bit noisy due to the sport although it wasn't a problem for me. The service although a bit slow was fine, there was only one lady on her own serving the tables (allowed for our main course to go down before we ordered desserts). Our party had beef Stroganoff, steak and ale pie and the trio of sausages. Although the sausages were fine (I ended up with one) my son didn't like them as they were Lincolnshire style sausages so too strong in flavour for him and maybe if it had indicated on the menu that they were Lincolnshire he would not have chosen this dish. For dessert we had sticky toffee pudding and the hanging oak dessert (like a kebab skewer with marshmallows, fudge pieces, waffle pieces, cookie dough and brownie pieces). This was REALLY nice. Not a cheap place to eat, probably would go again but might try to get seated in the restaurant part next time. Plenty of parking available.

This is a fabulous place to dine. The food is excellent. We came for a birthday meal and was not disappointed. This restaurant is a all you can eat venue. There is a good range of meats on the lunchtime menu, and in the evening, there is a further selection of meats added. All of these are freshly prepared, and staff come to your table and serve you from a tall skewer.  There is an excellent buffet for your sides, both hot and cold. Staff also come around with hot fries.  There is a small selection for the desert menu. However, the deserts are wonderful. This restaurant also caters for children with a smaller plate and a childrens desert. There is a good selection of drinks and cocktails, both alcoholic and non alcoholic. This restaurant is a little pricy but well worth it.

Went out for a quick lunch with a Portuguese friend. Being a native from Seville (Spain) myself, we thought a Brazilian restaurant would somehow hit home. And we were not wrong! 😃 Staff were incredibly welcoming, especially our very Spanish Mister J. Some of the themed colours used in table service were from the Portuguese flag, so it indeed felt very homely. The salads were full of flavour, and there was a choice of cold and hot starters. Although I couldn't eat that much, I would have happily indulged in every single dish. The variety of freshly grilled meat was nothing short of spectacular, very nicely seasoned, so compliments to the chef. The atmosphere felt so welcoming and chilled, that our "quick lunch" turned into a 4-hour catch-up. This being our first time in this restaurant, staff explained to us very politely how things worked. We were both pleasantly surprised with the simple, but intelligent approach to freshness and taste. It was a bit pricey, but worth every penny. Kudos to management for hiring staff of various backgrounds, thus ensuring a dynamic service. Staff seemed to know full well what they were selling, so training is visibly in place. Would highly recommend a visit. Vegetarian options: Hot and cold veg options. Parking: Parking is right beside the restaurant. Kid-friendliness: Saw large groups dining in, some bringing their kids.

First rate Indian restaurant with an extensive menu and excellent service.  We visited one Saturday evening and the atmosphere was good, a decent buzz but not too noisy.  Poppadoms and pickles as an appetiser were standard fare - nothing special but equally nothing negative.  Starters of a mixed grill and onion bhajis were excellent however, tasty and just the right amount of spice/heat in the grill.  Main courses comprised chicken tikka chilli mossala and a vegetable biryani, lemon rice, garlic and peshwari naan breads and a couple of sides: brinjal bhaji and tarka dall.  Superb! Very flavoursome and tasted fresh which is not always the case at Indian restaurants in my experience. With draft Cobra available and a decent wine list, I think this is a real find.  Add on great, friendly service and it's a winner.  We'll return if we want Indian in Yarmouth again.  Recommended.

Lovely food, can't fault it. Every dish was served piping hot and was all delicious. Our only issue was a small sentence on the receipt which says 'service not included'. In the UK, service IS included as all staff should be paid the UK minimum-wage. By putting 'service not included', you're trying to guilt people into leaving tips. Tips in this country are not expected as they do not form part of staff wages.

The effort you put in to make people feel welcome and special is unreal. The birthday music and the birthday song sang by all present added that extra special moment. We have eaten at your restaurant on many occasions now and we shall continue to visit to celebrate our special occasions. Colosseo’s is by far our favourite Italian restaurant. Thank you and your staff for continuing your hard work, delivering magnificent food in a warm, cosy friendly atmosphere. If I could give you more stars then I would. For those of you thinking of trying this restaurant for the first time, all I can say is it won’t be your last , you will not be disappointed and like me, I am sure it will become your favourite Italian dining experience.

Storico is a culinary haven that offers an exceptional dining experience. From the moment you step inside, the warm ambiance envelops you, setting the stage for an unforgettable meal. The attentive staff greets you with genuine smiles, eager to guide you through their delectable menu. The aroma of freshly baked pizzas wafts through the air, enticing your senses and whetting your appetite. The menu boasts an array of mouthwatering pizzas, crafted with the finest ingredients and a touch of culinary artistry. Each bite reveals a symphony of flavors, from the crispness of the thin crust to the harmonious blend of cheeses and toppings. Whether you're a fan of classic Margherita or crave the adventurous combinations of their specialty pizzas, Storico never disappoints. What truly sets Storico apart is their commitment to customer satisfaction. The friendly and knowledgeable servers effortlessly cater to your every need, ensuring a seamless dining experience. Their passion for pizza is contagious, and they take pride in creating personalized culinary delights that cater to diverse palates and dietary preferences. Beyond their exceptional pizzas, Storico offers a diverse selection of appetizers, salads, and desserts that elevate your meal to new heights. The vibrant flavors and impeccable presentation of each dish demonstrate their dedication to culinary excellence. From the moment you enter Storico to the final bite of their delectable desserts, you're enveloped in an atmosphere of culinary bliss. It's a place where great food, impeccable service, and a passion for pizza converge, leaving you with memories to savor long after the last slice is devoured.

Have been here twice now. The first time I came for a bottomless brunch to cheer my friend up after a recent break up. The service was exceptional. I had the shakshouka that day and again was very impressed so, when the other day my friend's birthday plans fell through, I recommended Jo & Co. They were able to fit him in and he also had a blast. I will definitely be back.

Rave reviews about the brunch here so had to give this place a go. Made a reservation given the popularity on New Year’s Day. On arrival we were met by what best could be described as a glare by the maître D followed by a look up and down. So odd. We told her we’d made a reservation but rather than take us to our table she promptly decided to clear a nearby table and take the plates away. Made to stand at the entrance for what seemed like an eternity although in fairness was probably 3-4 minutes. 3-4 minutes too long in my opinion. Perhaps the most unwelcome greeting I’ve had for a long while. Our actual waiter was however kindness and courtesy personified. Perhaps he should teach his female colleague a thing or two. Anyways to the libation and degustation. The drinks were sublime. A deep rich perfectly spiced Bloody Mary was a thing of beauty as was a fresh and gloriously vibrant green smoothie. Food I’m sad to say was decidedly average. The kiddies fish fingers and chips was basically a marriage made of Captain Birdseye and McCains. The Hollandaise for the eggs benny was radioactively yellow and runny. My spiced chicken burger and the deep fried calamari were perfectly acceptable but woefully under seasoned. I had to ask for the salt and I never usually add extra salt (I’m a cardiologist btw). The maître’D had a smile for every other customer that arrived after us. Perhaps we just weren’t the right fit for this establishment. This place certainly wasn’t the right fit for us.

Came here with my wife and 3 friends. For starters we had chilli wings, tandoori mixed grill, lamb momo and chicken momo. For mains we had Lamb madras, Karachi Prawn Masala and a bread basket. The chicken momo was the best dish, very flavoursome, followed by lamb momo. The chilli wings seemed like they were slightly undercooked. The tandoori mixed grill was a bit dry, but the accompanying sauces helped. All in all a decent start. The mains seemed quite basic, I would say maybe 5/6 pieces of lamb / prawn in each dish, and the curry wasn’t spectacular. The starters came quickly but the mains took awhile as the place started getting busier. I would come again and try different dishes! Vegetarian options: My vegan friend comes here all the time, it’s his go to.

Our first time eating from Takayama after hearing good things. Ordered takeaway through Uber Eats. Oh my GOODNESS this is some next level food. Firstly the presentation in the box is just absolutely gorgeous and completely unlike anything I’ve ever seen from a takeaway before. Not a single drop of anything had spilt despite having bubble tea and various sauces. The bubble tea is absolutely beautiful, with mine having little stars in it and even the straws being beautiful. The flavour is gorgeous. I had the Tako Karaage (fried octopus) which was beautifully cooked, flavour again was insane and it wasn’t too chewy which can be a real problem with octopus. I had the beef teriyaki and I have never tasted steak cooked so well, let alone the fact it was through a takeaway! The portion was huge, with the rice being served separately which meant it didn’t get soggy in the sauce. We also got some free fruit which was a really lovely touch. We will definitely be visiting the restaurant itself soon! My terrible photos really don’t do it justice.

For our honeymoon in Europe, we visited a Gordon Ramsay restaurant in our first city, London, to experience its fine dining. With high expectations given its Michelin 3-star rating, we found that while the interior wasn't large, it provided a cozy dining experience with moderate noise levels. We ordered the restaurant's signature menu Carte Blanche. However, while eating the seafood dish, I bit into shells twice and mentioned this to the staff. It was disappointing to see such a lack of preparation in a Michelin 3-star restaurant. The restaurant offered us complimentary wine to make up for it. But when we received the bill after our meal, we were charged for the supposedly free wine. If we hadn't checked the bill, we would have paid for the disappointing meal and an unordered wine. Whether it was a lack of communication among the staff or they were trying to take advantage of us, this restaurant seems undeserving of its Michelin 3-star title.

My wife and I traveled to the UK for our honeymoon and decided to make Restaurant Gordon Ramsay our celebratory dinner. As soon as you walk in you are greeted by their friendly and very helpful staff. We both ordered different things to taste a little bit of everything. My wife ordered the scallops for her starter while I ordered the ravioli. Both were delicious and set the expectations for the flavor profiles we were about to experience. For entrée, my wife ordered the cornish turbot and I had the Cumbrian blue gray. Her fish was so moist and flavorful. The blue gray was exquisite with the black garlic. The mushrooms alone on my plate could of been the highlight of any other meal. We did order and try the cheese before dessert but they were a bit too funky for our taste. For dessert we ordered the pecan praline and the strawberries and creme. Both were very good and not too sweet for my tastes (I don't really have a sweet tooth so it was right up my alley). The service was over the top with the staff constantly checking in and making sure everything was taken care of (they even go as far as to make sure you don't pour yourself your own water.... sorry about that haha). As we didn't have time during our wedding to finish our meals, thank you everyone who works there for making our celebratory wedding dinner one to remember forever.

We had booked the Inspiration table at this iconic restaurant and our experience was quite mixed. Starting with the positives, the food was outstanding and not one of the dishes fell short of expectations (which is very rare even at this level of restaurants). The young pastry chef who explained our dishes to us made our evening! Sorry we can’t remember your name - we dined here on March 22nd so hope that is enough to get you the credit you deserve! She explained every dish in a very professional but engaging manner and was a joy to chat to. On to the negatives, the table we had was not in the main dining room (I assume as we had a chef explaining the dishes to us?) but it meant we were the only diners in what looked like the ante-chamber and we felt a bit in the way of the staff. The other issue we had was the wine pairing. First of all the menu stated that the wine pairing would be personalised and that the sommelier would come talk to us to understand our preferences but nobody came to talk to us which is very disappointing when expectations were built up. When we got our wines we got only the briefest of descriptions - name of the wine and winemaker and despite us trying to engage and ask some questions we didn’t get much more engagement. It feels very disappointing given the price tag of the pairing. The wines themselves were really nice so no complaints there but given the reputation of the restaurant we were quite disappointed.

I've been waiting for visiting this place for a while now and I would say, the overall experience was good. They started with a few pre course appetizers which I would say were much better than the actual items on the menu. I liked how well they showcased the vegetables besides proteins and the complex flavors from each of the greens worked really well with the overall dishes. If I were to point out any faults it would be with the Lobster tail, which should have cut like butter as opposed to it being a bit on the chewier side. I liked the vegetarian course  which was the mushroom and ravioli, really different from what I've had before. The final main was the pork, and wow! The cook was perfect plus the sauces and citric tones worked beautifully with the protein. My favourite dish of the evening has to be the dessert - Millefeuille, the Mangoes tasted unreal...and that made the experience heavenly! Given the efforts they put into crafting each course, I'll give it a 5 star

description: A new find for us, a welcome one at that. Lovely setting in what I guess was the old ticket office of Hartlebury Station. Nice food at reasonable prices to go with a nice selection of local ales. It is a 20 minute drive from our house, but on the plus side it is only 20 minutes by train with stations seconds walk away at both ends. In a country pub it was also nice to see they had a couple of TV's with Sky Sports on.

Additionally, I had a park view table, but two large touristic buses parked in front of the window were quite disturbing and detracted from the full dining experience. Overall, it was a delightful evening that I would highly recommend.

Food & Drink: 8/10 (Dessert: 9/10) The Duck Season Menu had 8 dishes including dessert. There were several dishes I would recommend: Photo 1.	Duck Bone Broth – very tasty and pure duck taste as it was from the bone taste so it didn’t have any gamey flavour! Photo 2.	Choux Farci, Beetroot Glaze – A very balanced taste between mince and beetroot which, for me as a person who don’t normally like beetroot, also like it. Photo 3.	Jerusalem Artichoke & Chestnut – A very surprising dessert that ice cream with chestnut crisp on top, the best dish on the menu, I was shocked when I had the ice cream and chestnut crisp together that the strong flavour of chestnut was perfectly matched with Jerusalem artichoke. It would be better if the Duck Season Menu was a full ‘duck menu’ as the Pollock was not matched with other dishes, even though the taste was quite good! We ordered a red and an orange which were quite good, there were some other good wines on the list. Service: 7/10 Very friendly staff but it would be great if the staff could explain the dishes a bit better! Environment/Atmosphere: 7.5/10 Photo 4.	The restaurant was close to Old Street Station so it was not hard to find! I quite liked the idea of how they presented the menu in a small letter sealed by a wax stamp! Photo 5.	The open kitchen set near the entrance was a brilliant idea as well that caught my eyes when I walked into the restaurant. The score could have gone up to 8/10 if the reserved table was not arranged next to the column and the spacing between the tables increased! Price: 7/10 A set menu with a glass of wine x 2 cost £200+ which I believe was a decent price for this quality of food in Central London.

Restaurant Story was on my go-to places list when we planned our trip to London and we booked our table for 2 people for a Friday lunch. Reservation is a must and its not that easy to get a table for certain popular timeslots. It’s located in a corner of a park and is close to the signature landmark of London, Bridge Tower. The decor is classy and elegant with romantic ambiance & beautiful furniture. The staff was well-trained, friendly and served everything in etiquette. I was in my 7th month pregnancy and they were careful about my diet restrictions. We both had their 7-course tasting menu ($130) and it was one of the best & price worthy dining experiences we have ever had. There was no menu presented, even online, since they would make adjustment based on ingredients available so every dish was a surprise for us. From amuse small bite, appetizer, bread, entree to dessert, we were satisfied with both the visual and sense of taste. The food was overall delicious, delicate and various with texture. Our favorites were “Candle “, which is bread with butter, and “Duck”, which is grilled duck breast & leg. We could feel how Tom Seller cares about what they serve and love the stories behind each dish, which was also the reason how they named the restaurant.

Story is one of my favourite fine dining restaurant in London. They way they present every single dish were all well thought. It showed on each dish the effort and attention to details the chef had put into. This is the first time I went to Story after their renovation. So the menu itself was different from the pre-renovation time. I missed some of the dishes I enjoyed in the past. Good that the chef kept a few dishes or main elements of the dishes unchanged. The highlight for me is the lamb dish which was cooked to perfection. Flavours of all the dishes worked and complemented all the main ingredients. Although the price of their tasting menu has increased, if you divided into 10 courses, it’s really not expensive at all. It’s always a special dining experience at Story and I look forward to my next visit soon.

A very interesting tasting menu with many flavours of Mexico, definitely a change of pace from your standard modern European tasting menu. The mezcal and tequila cocktails were also masterfully crafted. Easily among the best service and atmosphere of the top fine dining restaurants in London without the prentiousness. I will say however, the norm in a lot of fine dining restaurants is to highlight and showcase the flavour of a specific ingredient, e.g. langoustine, wagyu. At times within this tasting menu it felt like this was not the case and some of the other (many!) flavours in the dish masked the full potential of another traditionally "highlight" ingredient. I don't know if this is Mexican cooking or if KOL does this on purpose, but just something to think about. I don't think this detracted at all from the experience due to the many other flavours, but if you're expecting this to be a direct style comparison to a European fine dining restaurant, I wouldn't say this is completely the case.

OMG! words simply can’t describe how good Ikoyi is, you just have to save the money and go for it. We have been to many Michelin star restaurants, have tried all the 3 stars in London, Ikoyi is simply on another level, I am certain they would have had the third star if Jeremy Chan is in the Michelin star inner circle. Flavor just simply exploded in your mouth layer after layer, we regretted that we didn’t come here sooner. I had tried African cuisine before but didn’t really enjoy it, but this is nothing like African cuisine, the use of spices are very subtle and everything is beautifully executed. If you are visiting London and want to treat yourself to a nice meal, look no more please, those overly hyped restaurants (e.g. most difficult to book) are not worth your money nor time. They serve a shorter lunch menu Tuesday to Thursday if you don’t want to break the bank.
