"Extraordinary culinary performance! Fine dining at its best. Jeremy Chan, head chef, leads the team through the performance of the open kitchen concept, channeling all positive tension into the restaurant itself. The interior is simple and serene, perfect for focusing on the eclectic gastronomic concept, a fusion of African-Asian cuisine with intense spice usage and unique ingredients that set this restaurant apart. A unique aspect is that the signature dishes aren't the 'strongest' ones, but two exceptional dishes preceding them (scallops and suya with creamed beans), offering a rhapsody of unexpected umami explosions. The service is exceptionally friendly. However, the atmosphere was disrupted by a table of overly loud guests, to the point where their noise drowned out the waiter's explanations of the dishes. This detracted from the overall impression as I couldn't hear information about the ingredients used in the dishes due to the noise. Since it's a blind tasting and the menu received at the end provides extremely limited information, unfortunately, the impression remains incomplete. Excellent cocktails."

I first visited Ikoyi in 2020. Back then, they were located in St James and it was a fairly “normal” restaurant in terms of decor, serving an a la carte menu which was reasonably priced. What was not normal though was the food. It was an outstanding meal and I knew it wouldn’t be my last visit. Fast forward 4 years and they’ve really grown up to become a serious fine dining destination in London, and one that can somehow get away with charging far more money than the likes of Core, The Ledbury, etc. The high prices definitely pushed it into special occasion territory for me, and ultimately we decided to visited when my wife was celebrating a milestone birthday. The current location is a bit random, but once you step inside it has been really nicely set up with dark, earthy tones and a fully open kitchen that faces the dining room. There are only 10 tables in the restaurant and we were lucky to get one of the 3 tables in the “front row”, giving us a great view of Jeremy and his team in the kitchen. No menu was presented until the end of the meal, but there were roughly 4 snacks, 4 starters, a main course and then 2 desserts plus the petit fours which turned out to be another individual dessert. The food was excellent, an almost entirely different menu versus my prior visit, but the unusual flavours and combinations had been maintained and there were some nice hits of spice in a few dishes, which we really enjoyed. Since I raised the topic of value for money, I now have to backtrack a bit as the quantity of food served was far higher than typical fine dining venues, perhaps even 50% more, which basically explains away the price differential. I have a big appetite and I was quite full up by the end of the meal. No bread was on offer, and it definitely wasn’t needed either! Service was another stand out aspect of the meal. Staff were so genuine and friendly, it made for a very relaxed experience. But best of all, we were served perhaps half of our courses by Jeremy Chan himself! He was such a lovely, down to earth guy and we really enjoyed our interactions with him. The bill for our meal was a punchy £986, which comprised the 2 tasting menus (£320 each), a single wine pairing (priced at £180), a couple of extra drinks and a coffee, plus service. No doubt a very expensive meal but as mentioned the portions were generous, and combining this with the differentiated menu, excellent service and comfortable setting, it did add up to be one of my favourite fine dining experiences in London, and I wouldn’t hesitate to recommend it to others.

Staff were so genuine and friendly, it made for a very relaxed experience. But best of all, we were served perhaps half of our courses by Jeremy Chan himself! He was such a lovely, down to earth guy and we really enjoyed our interactions with him. The bill for our meal was a punchy £986, which comprised the 2 tasting menus (£320 each), a single wine pairing (priced at £180), a couple of extra drinks and a coffee, plus service. No doubt a very expensive meal but as mentioned the portions were generous, and combining this with the differentiated menu, excellent service and comfortable setting, it did add up to be one of my favourite fine dining experiences in London, and I wouldn’t hesitate to recommend it to others.

I first visited Ikoyi in 2020. Back then, they were located in St James and it was a fairly “normal” restaurant in terms of decor, serving an a la carte menu which was reasonably priced. What was not normal though was the food. It was an outstanding meal and I knew it wouldn’t be my last visit. Fast forward 4 years and they’ve really grown up to become a serious fine dining destination in London, and one that can somehow get away with charging far more money than the likes of Core, The Ledbury, etc. The high prices definitely pushed it into special occasion territory for me, and ultimately we decided to visited when my wife was celebrating a milestone birthday. The current location is a bit random, but once you step inside it has been really nicely set up with dark, earthy tones and a fully open kitchen that faces the dining room. There are only 10 tables in the restaurant and we were lucky to get one of the 3 tables in the “front row”, giving us a great view of Jeremy and his team in the kitchen. No menu was presented until the end of the meal, but there were roughly 4 snacks, 4 starters, a main course and then 2 desserts plus the petit fours which turned out to be another individual dessert. The food was excellent, an almost entirely different menu versus my prior visit, but the unusual flavours and combinations had been maintained and there were some nice hits of spice in a few dishes, which we really enjoyed. Ikoyi had excellent food and a great ambience but at a decidedly steep price point. The tasting menu had some excellent dishes, especially when it came to the sauces and wringing flavour from vegetables in creative ways. Both the rib and the octopus were incredible. Unfortunately, especially the West African elements that Ikoyi likes to advertise, like the Jollof rice, underdeliver relative to everything else and relative to the fine dining expectations. I was pleasantly surprised by some of the innovative dessert dishes which often fall flat in fine dining. All that being said, I would not call the experience twice as good as the average 150£ 1-star restaurant. To make matters worse, when we went we ended up being overcharged by about 210£ due to waitstaff errors. The mistake ended up being resolved but left a bitter after-taste given that we were paying a premium for excellent and attentive service.

Honestly, this is one of my most memorable and amazing meals that I’ve had. A 3 star Michelin restaurant with a chef whom is consistently present with her staff and has the passion and empathy to say hi to her guests while making her menu financially accessible to more people considering the status of her food. It was a genuine pleasure to be serviced by the waiting staff and chefs. Clare Smyth is a major reason to visit, but her staff and their warmth and professionalism is on another level of service. Genuinely, it broke my mind the way we were treated. I ordered the classic menu while my date had the seasonal spring menu. We also ordered a bottle of wine! Overall, cannot say enough amazing things about my experience here.

Came here for lunch on Saturday. We chose the short tasting menu. I had to say all were excellent. I usually judge the restaurant by the bread and butter. I found bread was slightly tough. The butter was good but not outstanding. I also feel they should improve “the attention to detail of the whole dining experience”. Felt more like Michelin restaurant rather than world’s top 100. If you happen to experience in Tokyo or in Asia or Paris etc, you would understand. IFKYK

Intimate dining experience with front row seats looking into the kitchen. Service was impeccable with great attention to detail. I was touched by the handwritten card and personalised menu that was provided as a keepsake. We opted for the vegetarian tasting menu which consisted of 7 courses including a number of additional dishes to start. The food ate well with the crispy Shiso leaf being the highlight. I found  many of the dishes contained similar ingredients like cheese, mushrooms or asparagus and some of the courses were also prepared in a similar fashion leading to us having a number of granitas and sorbets throughout the meal. We also found the Beremeal pancakes a challenge to eat without the aid of cutlery, leaving our hands sticky. Whilst my Loquat sorbet was perfectly centred on the plate I noticed it was very much off centre on my partner’s dish. Overall a pleasant experience elevated by the service.

We went to the Clove Club to celebrate our wedding anniversary. From beginning to when you leave the staff is great. From the dining room you have front row seats to the open kitchen that works like clockwork. All dishes were nicely balanced and taste is impeccable. There were some unexpected combinations which all worked great together. Some reviews mention price, but it’s in line with other 2 michelin star restaurants we’ve been to. Maybe not fir people who love classic solid food, but if you like pure ingredients and unexpected combos this restaurant should be on you your list.

Such a disappointment. The food was ok but let down enormously by the terrible service. We chose the tasting menu with wine pairing. We had our lonely little sorbet and then the final wine pairing arrived 15 minutes later. At this point we were ready to leave, tired from the noisy kitchen and bustling floor. We’ve had better experiences at a much more reasonable price at our local curry houses. Don’t bother visiting.

We had high expectations for this 3 Michelin star restaurant, but unfortunately, our experience fell short. Starting from the interior that was lacking sophistication, and food been served directly on the wooden table without white cloth didn’t felt clean and elegant. The presentation of the dishes was ok but nowhere near 3*. The highest disappointment came from the food itself that didn't live up to the hype. Langoustine had strong garlic aftertaste, pea were tasting undercooked not in a tasty way, lobster was just a regular lobster without any distinct flavour, ox tongue was too fatty, cod literally has 0 taste, lamb was chewy etc. All the dishes were lacking balance and harmony in flavours. We went to many Michelin Star restaurants and this was not just a bad Michelin Star but generally bad food for a regular restaurant. I’m giving 2 stars just for the food presentation that is ok, but again not impressive to have 3*. Service was also a bit strange, waiters would gather for a mini meeting next to the table discussing notes from the tray, then 2 of them would serve it at the same time and 1 would pour the sauce to me and then go around the table to do it for my husband; while doing this they would be quite which made always awkward silence and then they would explain the dish. For the price and reputation, I expected more in terms of taste and atmosphere. Sadly, it was a disappointment. We are still wondering how this place has 3*, and wondering what is going on in a Michelin Stars world to have them keep these stars.

We went to many Michelin Star restaurants and this was not just a bad Michelin Star but generally bad food for a regular restaurant. I’m giving 2 stars just for the food presentation that is ok, but again not impressive to have 3*. Service was also a bit strange, waiters would gather for a mini meeting next to the table discussing notes from the tray, then 2 of them would serve it at the same time and 1 would pour the sauce to me and then go around the table to do it for my husband; while doing this they would be quite which made always awkward silence and then they would explain the dish. For the price and reputation, I expected more in terms of taste and atmosphere. Sadly, it was a disappointment. We are still wondering how this place has 3*, and wondering what is going on in a Michelin Stars world to have them keep these stars.

Fantastic food and for many sitting in the main dining area by the kitchen, a chance to watch a well-oiled machine at work making the food. How do they squeeze that many kitchen staff into such a tight space though?? It’s like a clown car with 6-8 staff shoulder to shoulder and back to back. The only minor drawback was that space is also tight for the customers in the main dining area. Clearly not too much of an impediment, however, with a constant wait list/queue. The burrata was creamy and fine and the bread delicious, but it was the main attraction that won the show. Such good pasta. And made fresh and then cooked to perfection in front of you. The tagliarini with dried chili, garlic and pangrattato had just the right hint of spiciness, nicely matched by the crunch of the pangrattato. The pici cacio et pepe was also fantastic. So much so, that the person who ate it might start a conflict or at least annoy a lot of Italians by stating that it was better than many enjoyed in Rome. And finally, the ravioli of Westcombe ricotta, peas, mint, Amalfi lemon and chili. Cooked expertly and presented with a nice little flourish of peas on the top. Delightful. The cocktails are good, but they’re not the star attraction. The same could be said for dessert. Tasty, but overshadowed by the pasta. An excellent meal.

One of my 11 year old boys has been pestering me for a while to eat at a Michelin Star Restaurant, so decided to take them to La Trompette where I’ve eaten many times as they have a good choice /selection of mains.  We had a lovely lunch on a Saturday and have to say it was really good as I was expecting.  James ordered the best starter on the menu in my view - cured bream, citrus  crème fraiche, kohlrabi, apple, lime and iced horseradish. It was fantastic, fresh and perfect delicate flavours. I had pork cheeks and Toulouse sausage, good but the bream was better.  The roast duck breast was very good, melted in your mouth.  The Lamb a la Nicoise was very good indeed and the olive mash to die for!!  Desserts also very good, banana soufflé and chocolate delice finished the meal off very well indeed.  Had a very good meal and will be back when finances allow as be good to bring my two girls and y wife.  A winner at Cheltenham covered our meal!!

Good higher end restaurant. I cannot say every dish was superb but the overall experience was pleasant. I’d love the portion sizes to be slightly bigger. The starters were just okay, nothing more. The portion of veal tartare was small, with asparagus being more massive taking the prevalence over the tartare itself. I could not taste the meat much because the mayo sauce overwhelmed everything. The rabbit raviolo had pretty basic taste but the onion velouté was nice and balanced the overall taste. The pancetta was too stiff in my opinion. Okay overall but not something I’d order again. The mains were pretty good. Aged beef rump cap had a right level of tenderness and the oxtail and bacon fondant was an amazing addition. The pork presa itself was nothing special as a meat cut, but the overall dish was offset by the crackling, nice sauces and pickled veggies - they played well together and left a pleasant impression. The desserts were definitely a highlight! Amazing passion fruit soufflé with ice cream - just melted in my mouth and the balance between sweet and sour was delightful. The salted caramel malt tart was one of the best desserts in my life - definitely a hit for the salted caramel lovers. The stout ice cream was a great addition although it melted quickly and became watery. The suggested wine pairings for the desserts were great. The staff was reasonably attentive with no major hiccups. One minor thing was that they were late to remove the amuse bouche plates but I did not mind at all. However, it definitely felt like some guests were more special than the others which I am not sure should be the case for a Michelin starred restaurants. The interior was very basic and had many aspects which would benefit from some maintenance - for example the water temperature and pressure in the bathroom or ceiling paint around the lamps.

Kubu in Peckham served up a dining experience that was equal parts impressive and mouthwatering. From the get-go, the menu had us intrigued, and boy, did it deliver! We kicked things off with the Kudu Bread, slathered in melted cultured butter and topped with house-cured bacon – talk about a flavor bomb! Then came the Smoked Prawn Eclair, a funky twist on a classic pastry that had us all nodding in approval. And let's not forget about the Beef Tartare, which was like a party in my mouth with its chicken liver parfait and smoked chilli. But the real stars of the show were the mains. The Cured Sea Bass was a delicate dance of flavors, with apple, pea, and horseradish stealing the spotlight. And the Rabbit Saddle? Oh boy, that confit leg was like heaven on a plate, and the asparagus and artichoke piccalilli were the perfect partners in crime. Now, about those African Carrots... While everything else was hitting all the right notes, these guys fell a bit flat. Sure, they were cooked perfectly, but the ras el hanout seasoning just didn't quite do it for me. They were a bit bland compared to the rest of the lineup. Overall, though, my night at Kubu was a hit. The Smoked Prawn Eclair and the Rabbit Saddle were definite highlights, and even though the carrots didn't quite hit the mark, I'd still be back in a heartbeat for another round of culinary delights.

It has been three years since we last time visit Margot. It was back in 2020 just after the first covid wave and we liked the food a lot. We decide to celebrate new year here again and are glad to be back here. The quality of the food remains the high level. The service is excellent and they are super nice to the baby. The pasta is just delicious and the side vegies are so good. The seafood risotto is slightly salty though. The beef cappacio is good as last time except they removed truffle. The veal slice appetiser is really tender and the sauce is amazing. It is definitely my top Italian restaurant in London.

I've had Gymkhana on my list of places to visit for a long time and after hearing about them being awarded their second Michelin star I had to get booked in. From start to finish my time here was amazing. The restaurant is cozy without feeling cramped and makes good use of the space. The staff are friendly and patient, taking time to ensure you understand everything about the menu. Never once did we feel rushed. The food is amazing, every single dish was an explosion of flavour and so delicately balanced allowing you to taste every element. Even the spicier dishes were beautiful with no overpowering elements. The same goes for the cocktails. Plus, unlike alot of high end restaurants, the portions are extremely generous! Be warned, you certainly won't leave hungry (we had some of the biggest lamb chops I've ever seen!). Our experience was so good we were on the website looking to book out next visit whilst sat at the table at the end of the meal. We will be back, even if it may take awhile given how busy they are now with bookings (fully deserved).

I've enjoyed quite a few excellent meals in my life. Probably not enough but more than a few. Having just enjoyed an excellent lunch at J Sheekey I now have a new entrant in the top ten. Maybe not number one but really all of my dining experiences at this level were fantastic. For starters the atmosphere at J Sheekey has that nice balance of being a bit special but also welcoming and friendly. The staff played a huge part in this and without exception they were all helpful, accommodating and on hand at all times. It took quite a while to pick our dishes, because the whole menu is uniformly attractive, but it was worth the wait. My starter scallops were large, juicy and perfectly cooked. Then came the Cornish fish stew which featured generous cuts of fish and just the right quantity of shellfish. Finally I went for the apple pie, because I'm an optimist, and the result was most excellent. Now lunchtime drinking is always hazardous but we went for the recommended Chablis and it was a fine choice. Robust and rich it paired nicely with all of our dishes. Really that's a good description for our whole dining experience and rarely have 2.5 hours passed so pleasingly.

Absolutely LOVED this spot! Almost purely fished based menu with a fair few options. All sounded great and after our meal we will be going back! In terms of atmosphere, it’s definitely an upper/higher class restaurant with a smart casual dressed crowd but I wasn’t too out of place in my large fleece. Service was impeccable throughout our server was attentive but not intrusive. It was the first time seeing my mother in years so it was so nice how much they allowed us to spend time chatting between courses and after. Now the food! Octopus with pepper and chorizo. So nicely cooked, octopus wasn’t rubbery and very easy to cut and eat with the salty chorizo was such a nice pairing. Fish pie. My mother’s dish looked and tasted amazing! It is one of Sheekey’s staples and didn’t disappoint. Creamy saucy with crisped mashed potatoes and flakes of fish throughout. Broccolini, tenderly cooked but not steamed and that gross steamed vegetable taste was no where to be found. Easy to cut but still firm. Fried Zucchini patties. These were also really nice and a nice accompaniment of Parmesan and a tangy tomato based sauce on the side. Scallops. Generously cooked in butter. And like the octopus was easy to cut and eat without any rubbery textures. Then our pudding we shared. What a masterpiece! Such a creamy base with sharp so very to help cut through all the yummy fish we’d had before! Overall Sheekeys was really amazing and the staff are truly a big highlight as well spent close to 30-45 minutes between our main and our dessert chatting and they couldn’t have been more accommodating! I’m going away again soon and I can see this being our go to for next catch up! Kid-friendliness: Super kid friendly! Our waitress also served a large group with 1 toddler and she was incredibly attentive to the toddler. Even dancing with them after the meal while the adult got coats and bills sorted. Kids menu also Wheelchair accessibility: Straight off the street, manageable lip into restaurant (not stairs) I would say the interior is a little tight but multiple rooms of dining and outdoor seating you’d definitely find a table!

3.5/4 - came as a high recommendation from a friend but overall disappointing for price : quality ratio. Nice courteous service and lovely location, pretty gorgeous. Split 4 dishes for lunch and was a good portion for two. 👍🏻 The aubergine mess was the best dish and had nice nuance to the flavours albeit sitting in a puddle of oil. 👎🏻 the baklava prawns were small and close to £30. Not a strong baklava taste, thought it would be more of a take on prawn toast, but are just grilled and battered prawns with some pistachio and sweetness (honey potentially). Quite disappointing given each prawn was £10 for a few morsels. The quality is not quite up to pay to expect fine dining prices for me. 👎🏻 The kebab dumplings were dry and hard, meat was not flavorful at all. Not juicy at all, clumpy even. 3 parcels for £23, and less flavourful than an Asian takeout place. Kind of tastes like nothing. The cauliflower was alright, tasted very same-y with the same labneh drowning every dish we ordered, which thankfully added a bit of moisture to the kebab dumplings. A la carte menu pricing is quite strange overall, brunch looks like it could be more promising but I'm not inclined to prioritize this restaurant again.

Daughter is 10 and they asked her age as we came in (can’t have 9 or younger after 7) so they do enforce that fwiw.

Have to visit the oldest restaurant in London if you visiting. It carries that historical feeling being there and appreciating the stories those walls have heard. The leg of rabbit and the steak and kidney pie were amazing. There was no room for appetizers during that visit. The rabbit was tender and had no gaminess at all. It was like a leg of tender chicken. The winner was the steak and kidney pie though. Excellent crust and flavor. Paired with some mustard for a kick is the way. The courgettes with tomatoes was a surprise hit and I encourage that to be included in any order. The cocktails were well done and I would visit again. The sticky toffee pudding was a bit burnt but not bad. The vanilla ice cream on the side helped. This was the first crumble I have had in London and it was pretty good. 2024.07.03

Dining at Chez Bruce was quite the experience, a mix of impeccable service and unexpectedly adventurous food. The staff were unfailingly polite and attentive, making us feel very well cared for throughout the evening. The culinary delights were another story. The sommelier was a standout. She recommended an excellent wine for £70, with a passionate explanation about rising prices in that French region. Intrigued, I did some research and managed to secure a box of the same wine for £20 a bottle that same night. Quite the markup! It seems even fine dining can't escape a bit of creative pricing. The menu boasted offerings for all tastes. I bravely ventured into the lobster ravioli, which turned out to be an unexpected workout for my jaw. Moving on to the main dishes, the fish was so salty that I barely touched it. I mentioned it to the server, who nodded sympathetically and then did absolutely nothing. The bread, aiming for rustic, instead hit the mark of soggy. The Chateaubriand steak was a rare bright spot, but the accompanying chips were hard and greasy, making me wonder just how difficult it is to get chips right. Is there a secret chip sabotage squad at work? Dessert was nice, no complains there. When it came time to pay, I was pleasantly surprised to find the fish discounted, but less thrilled by the accompanying lecture on timely feedback. Apparently, letting them know at the moment wasn't sufficient—perhaps I should have sent a smoke signal instead. It was my birthday, after all, and I was trying to enjoy my evening. I understand the challenges of keeping a restaurant's offerings fresh and exciting, but this experience left me feeling more than a little disappointed. It seems my quest for decent food in London continues. Chez Bruce has the potential for greatness, but I hope they work on smoothing out the rough edges for future diners.

If I could give the food zero stars I would. We decided to go to this restaurant due to its high ratings on Google and it being in the area where we live. We are all Indians and hence our opinion is based on our lived experience of eating Indian food. This restaurant might be going through the worlds supply of oil. You even feel it as you walk on the greasy floors. The staff is quite friendly so can’t complain about that. The concept of the restaurant is supposed to be Indian tapas but there’s nothing unique about it. All Indian food tends to be to share and there was no innovation in the menu. The food itself was so oily, the flavours were sub par. Spices almost tasted raw. It all tasted the same. The butter chicken was the worst I’ve had. The batter fried items were all dripping in oil and more soft and soggy than crispy. I wouldn’t write such a bad review as I genuinely like to support small businesses. But I’ve been kept up all night with a terrible stomach which even my friends were suffering. Also it was quite overpriced for the quality and portions.

I recently visited the oyster bar for lunch and, unfortunately, my experience was not very pleasant. While the food quality was acceptable given the price, it did not stand out. I wasn’t expecting much in terms of the food, so this was not a major issue for me. However, the most disappointing aspect was the quality of service. Although two of the staff members were friendly, one of the female staff who served our food was quite rude. She merely placed the dishes on the table without mentioning what they were or providing a simple introduction. There was no consideration for what the customers might need. Considering the restaurant charges a 15% service charge, I felt that the level of service provided was far below what one would expect. I did not feel that I received any good quality service during my visit. Overall, my experience was underwhelming and I hope they can improve their service in the future.

Ambience ruined by a three year old in a high chair either screeching out, laughing very loudly , saying words loudly or throwing napkins on the floor. Staff was very accommodating to the child but there should have a no very young child policy as this type of dining is not suited for that age. Located in what used to be a car garage the four. Level is converted into a brassiere and oyster bar and top a two michelin star restaurant. Lovely interior of Blue carpet, circular tables with white hugging table cloths.The kitchen is visible via the automatic sliding door and windows but not as visible as some other Michelin star restaurants. Beautiful light well with a dried flower arrangement, felt like summer. There is a map of Bordeaux on the far end of the glass and Two stain glass panels of the Michelin man. Three menus On offer  : taste of the season at £215, lunch 3 course menu at £145 and  market menu for £75 which I told had to be pre booked. Wine pairing is £189 for 6 wines  Or exceptional for £495 If you are planning to go for the market menu, best to call ahead and ask as I was refused it as they said they had run out and also it’s a sunrise menu and therefore you get what you’re given and the left over cuts from the other dishes to reduce waste. The first amouse bouche was the Miso Foam with rice crispy and rice a Ice cream. Combination of cold: Rice ice cream and hot :Miso foam Beautifully subtle and delicious dish as made rice ice cream taste amazing Second amouse was cheese with nuts and veg base with egg yolk. The Sourness of the dish was excessive with cheese crumbs at the top served in an 3/4 egg shell. The Bread and butter : standards sour dough with butter, love butter dish was it a Michelin man The first course of Scallop dish was beautiful, it looked like a sea of yellow roe with droplets of yellow  and red with three raw scallops wjth a scallop cracker which was very light and not overpowering some other seafood crackers. Very interesting- never had raw scallops and tasted fresh but neutral unlike grilled scallops. The mains of John Dory was beautiful, brushed with a black paste, it was fairly lightly cooked as the inside was The Green Ragu easily very fresh sweet green - kohlrabi and courgette. The asparagus brûlée was nice with small pieces  small asparagus, good dish as a whole. Palate cleanser was lemon sorbet with dill stands. Interesting dish to say the least as the dill strands were frozen and the lemon tasted similar verbena lemon. The rhubarb desert was somewhat disappointing as the cake was rather blend, the rhubarb syrup was more sour then sweet with pieces of sour rhubarb did not Lift the dish nor did the ice cream which was  sweet but tart. The beignet was soggy, the cream inside was too sweet and again disappointing. Service excellent provided Italian lady and I think her name is Genevieve. Unfortunately at the end, I was charged the dinner three course rather than the lunch so do check your bills as mistakes do happen!

Absolutely incredible dining experience. We came here for my boyfriends birthday and originally booked a table for 9.30, but were called prior to the booking by a member of the team who recommended that we come at 8.30 instead since the ambience would be more lively at that time. He offered to prepare our table early which was so sweet and made us feel so attended to before we even arrived. The service was immaculate from when we stepped into the building to the moment we left. The food was an entire experience all on its own, we both got the tasting menu and every dish was so well thought out and interesting. The bibendum egg was the highlight, an insane technical burst of flavours, we couldn’t stop talking about it (the hazelnut at the end?! Insane!). All in all, a really amazing night which was really made by the staff, they made my boyfriend feel so special, gave him a card for his birthday, took care to make sure we’d get the most out of the ambience, and were so knowledgeable on every aspect of the menu. Thank you so much to everyone and we’ll definitely be back again!

I arrived on a cloudy, wet Saturday afternoon but was warmly welcomed to what must be one of the nicest dining rooms in London. I had seen the £75 blind 'market' menu, which is only put together on the day based on seasonal ingredients. Based on Chef Bosi's reputation and the fact that this place has held 2* for a while, I thought this seemed reasonable. The staff were friendly and warm throughout; the place was surprisingly quiet when I arrived (not even half full) which meant there were enough waiters to home in on tiny issues within seconds (one would approach the table if I even tipped my head in their direction). The only minor thing was with the wine service. Despite using a filtering device, I noticed after a few seconds that my first glass had several tiny bits of cork floating around. I mentioned this and it was filtered again, but then I noticed a similar thing happened again with the glass of red I ordered after (I didn't bother mentioning it that time). The starter (pumpkin veloute with shaved black truffle and yoghurt with bacon brioche) was excellent, with the depth of flavour you'd expect of a solid 2* restaurant. The brioche was glazed slightly with honey and tasted very fresh. The main (chicken breast stuffed with foie gras, served with chicken jus, artichoke salad and some crispy potato things I didn't get the name of) was also delicious. The salad was slightly under seasoned to my taste but the jus was rich and packed full of flavour, the chicken cooked perfectly. The dessert sadly didn't live up to these previous courses, a white chocolate tart with vanilla pearls and lemon ice cream that was nice but a bit too sweet, given that the main base was made of white chocolate (I'd have preferred biscuit or pastry for this). The only other small negative for the food was that the bread came out tepid. Despite these minor issues, this was a solid visit and well worth the asking price, especially with the gougeres, 'Bibbendum egg' and petit fours added.  With all the decorations and small touches (my bill was presented in a 32-year-old Michelin guide) it felt almost as much a museum visit as a fine dining experience. I'd happily visit again and would recommend it to others, especially if they have any interest in the Michelin guide. 4.5/5, £126 all in (food, two glasses of wine, coffee, and service)

5* experience! It was super busy and atmospheric, this is a really popular place so book on weekends! There are tables outside with heaters though as well. Food was incredible, waitresses were very kind and service was really fast! One of the meals came slightly after the other so we got 2 free drinks which was super thoughtful and unexpected. The Thai tea is delicious, the lychee cooler was super sweet and refreshing and I also got the butterfly pea tea which changes colour and tastes incredible. For food we had the satay starter which was perfect and I had the vegan fish in red curry sauce with jasmine rice. My boyfriend had the vegan pork cracking with red curry paste and green beans which was so spicy, sweet and crunchy it was delicious!!! This place is seriously special, one of the best restaurants in London vegan or not. Also loads of gluten free options.

We lived in Putney for several years and heard a few positive feedbacks from friends about Tomoe; however, did not have much opportunity until last month. I had a chance to pop in for lunch; the restaurant was full; however, asked whether I could sit at the bar on the right-hand side next to the entrance; the staff are always very accommodating (went back again for exactly the same dishes – Prawn Tempura Bento. It was as nice as the first experience, the staff are very accommodating again because I was a bit late for their lunch service.  The quality of the foods stands out and the ambience does make me wonder whether it would be the same in Japan (one of the countries that I wish to visit). Therefore, if anyone lives near here, I would like to encourage all to try Tomoe.  I enjoy mine a lot and will go back for more soon. Just noticed, their opening hours are quite limited.  Check before you make a visit. Thanks, Tomoe, for making a simple lunch very enjoyable. Vegetarian options: no sure, i had Tempura

Went here after waiting to try it for a while. 6.40pm on a weekday afternoon. Was told it was fully booked even for 2 pax but if we could finish by 7.30pm then they could accommodate us. We were fine with it and went in to order as soon as possible. Good all came piping hot, such as our udon, agedashi tofu and tempura. Really enjoyed our spicy tuna sushi starter too and of course the yummy chutoro. I had a zaru soba and I felt like I was back in Japan. It’s so nice to have this just down the street from my home. The staff were friendly and had the traditional, typical Japanese hospitality and etiquette. The place is tiny but cosy and neat. Really reminds me of Japan. My husband kept complimenting the food as he ate. Can’t wait to visit again and try the other items and savour the experience whilst I wait for Japan to accept tourists once again! Book ahead to avoid disappointment!

Popped in for a snack around lunchtime on a Sunday. Warmly and politely received, seated within seconds. Due to the warm weather decided to sit in the garden. Plenty of seating, wasn't too busy for the time of day. After ordering drinks the service was slow. Felt forgotten at times with other tables arriving after served promptly, was a impromptu visit for me so no bother but some people may mind. I put it down to the seating position behind the centre piece tree because you're not in immediate view. Notwithstanding, the sushi was delicious and fresh, highly recommend and would order again plus more off the menu. Wish I  ordered some of the ice cream near the entrance to go as I was leaving. Only con for me was the toilet (there's two), it smelt awful but looked clean. Thankfully it's spacious inside so you don't feel choked up in a tiny cubicle. To each his own though as this is not a big deal for some.

I had a great time when I went to Oita on a Friday evening. We didn’t book in advance so they didn’t have any tables in the garden but the vibe and service was still amazing. We were given an option of where we wanted to sit in the main indoor area of the restaurant. Our server Monica was very accommodating asking if we had any dietary requirements and guiding us with our choices. When she was unsure whether the ramen broth was halal, she went to check with the head chef. I was very impressed with how well she knew not just the menu but the key ingredients within each dish. Food arrived in good time. Monica came to check if we were happy with our meals. She brought over extra dishes so we could share.  Overall, I was pleased with the freshness of the food and the service provided. I even had the chance to see the garden area which is absolutely stunning and relaxing. I would definitely reserve a garden table next time. The final bill price was also reasonable. Vegetarian options: Some dishes are for vegetarians. You can buy maki or rainbow sushi. Dietary restrictions: Some chicken dishes are suitable for halal customers. They also take precautions if you have allergies.

We visited for the early dinner set menu which if I am honest looked really appealing for a one star restaurant. Attentive service, informal but professional. One thing stood out, the "sommelier" or the person charged refill our wine glasses most probably forgot, so we had our starter with the first glass (we got a half a bottle carafe) and then almost finished our mains when she came around for the 2nd refill. It was particularly odd since there weren't many tables occupied. Now for the food I am sure that their actual tasting menu is great, with complex preperations and amazing ingredients, but this  review is based on an early dinner set menu, which is still their product. It was a very well cooked meal, rather simple but made with care. In my opinion It is not a great way to be introduced in fine dining, because didn't find anything to entice me to revisit for the full tasting menu experience which I think is the point of this exercise. Pleasant evening Out, nothing more.

I don’t often give 5 start however I feel this place deserves it. I loved my experience from beginning to end. Staff were extremely pleasant and accommodating. The restaurant is decorated beautifully I can imagine it to be lovely place to come in the summer as they have some outdoor seating. I visited to celebrate my nieces birthday with family. Everyone enjoyed the food, I tried things I would not normally go for and I was not disappointed. There is great options for non meat eaters which was appreciated with our party. I had a fabulous cocktail called “Zilli” it was so good that I would come back just for that cocktail. I also really enjoyed the asparagus salad which is not something I would normally go for but very impressive. I cannot end this review without mention the bread for the table, I believe it was complimentary however it was soo delicious and fresh! We also brought our own birthday cake which was not a problem, they bought it out with plates and napkins for us to serve ourselves. Overall great experience and I would 100% recommend and I also cannot wait to return. Wheelchair accessibility: I think on a busy evening it would be a struggle to get around with a wheel chair however not bad and there is a accessible toilet on the ground floor

restaurant_name: Mumbai Maska - Indian Restaurant and Takeaway in Chingford- London
description: Date Visited – 21st July 2024. First Impression: The Restaurant is perfectly situated and adorned with delightful decor. The entrance is immaculately tidy, and all tables are meticulously arranged with the necessary cutlery. The spotless tables and exceptional ambiance exceed expectations. The entire Restaurant is equipped with fans, a necessity in the sweltering heat outside. Service: From the moment we arrived, Qadeer extended a warm welcome and guided us to a table set for six. He thoughtfully asked if we had any questions about the drink menu before taking our orders. Qadeer's exemplary customer service was evident as he maintained eye contact and exhibited patience while we made our selections from the menu. Each dish we ordered was delivered with care, as Qadeer remembered who ordered what and ensured each plate was placed in front of the correct person. He made regular visits to our table to inquire if we needed anything else, promptly clearing empty dishes and cleaning the table before serving the main course. Food: The restaurant offers a splendid variety of food options, with choices available for both vegetarians and non-vegetarians. I highly recommend the Tandoori Mushroom. Additionally, we savoured Pav Bhaji, Dal Makhni, and Jeera Rice, all of which were served in ample portions and with impeccable quality. Last Impression: Faheem's outstanding service truly made a lasting impact on us. His engaging personality, sense of humour, and polite manners were exemplary. Faheem even made sure to wait for us to complete our payment, asked if we needed a receipt, and ended our interaction with a smile. Location: The Restaurant is on the popular High Street - Chingford, London. Parking – Parking is bit challenging mainly because of high street, however you can find some on side street. The parking on high street is free after 4 pm (Monday to Saturday). Price: We paid £107 for 5 people (starter, main and drink).

We really loved The Harwood Arms. It is such a pleasure to have exceptional food in a casual, relaxed setting. The dining room is rustic and cozy. And even though The Harwood Arms is a pub, the service is top notch. The food is classic British cooking with a focus on game and wild meat. My favorite dish was the venison scotch egg with Oxford sauce. It was beautiful with a runny golden yolk. My only complaint is that it came out with instead of ahead of my starter as requested. The thyme flavored sauce on the rabbit lasagne was phenomenal. The Berkshire Fallow Deer was perfectly cooked and served with mushrooms and onions. They had dessert special, a date custard tart, that we were lucky to get. I also enjoyed their gin list and tried three different English gins, each one delicious. I highly recommend it. Kid-friendliness: Kids are welcome and there is a small kids menu.

After that, I ordered a spicy margarita…that was actually spicy 😂 - it was delicious!! In total I had 3 spicy margaritas and one el Mexicano (tequila, melon and pineapple) cocktail! They brought a lovely dessert I didn’t quite get the name of and they all sung happy birthday to me! This was a wonderful surprise and the cake was amazing! 🍮 <— this is what it looked like!! Staff: The staff were amazing, great customer service! Incredibly polite, warm and welcoming! Our booking was fairly late and near closing time however we did not feel rushed one bit. The guys were constantly checking everything was ok and that we enjoyed our food and drinks! Some of the best customer service I’ve experienced in a while! so thank you to everyone at BiFe! ❤️

Visited for the Chef’s Table Experience for my birthday. I thought it was a solid and tasty menu but uninspiring, and the service lacked finesse. The standout was their “Tea & Cake” . The flavours were rich and scrumptious, setting high expectations. Another interesting element was the Ajo Blanco (“white gazpacho”) ice cream in the crab dish. The quality of the locally sourced ingredients was excellent, but I hoped for more memorable dishes. The service, although lovely, lacked the finesse expected at this price point. While the birthday card was a nice touch, adding a candle to one of the four desserts would have made it more special. Let's be honest, many restaurants at this calibre do this without requests. They gave us wrong cutlery for one of the courses. It was a bit embarrassing for them when we found the chocolate bonbons missing from a dessert box, and the staff had to quickly rectify it. Flavours were mostly classics, didn't get any wow factors. At £190pp, it was rather underwhelming. Perhaps their new projects would bring more excitement and thrill.

We decided to celebrate a special occasion at Medlar after reading the reviews. We booked well in advance and the manager tried to seat us right in front of the door on a chilli night when we arrived. We declined and he kindly took us to the back of the restaurant where he found a nice corner for us. The food was excellent, perfectly executed using top quality seasonal ingredients. The service staff generally are nice and quite attentive particularly those at junior level. However, it is clear those with seniority use their hierarchy positions to be opinionated and make inappropriate comments. The female sommelier was one of them, pushing to order making remarks, quickly opening our bottle of red wine whilst we were still enjoying a carafe of white. When we told her to stop she rolled her eyes and avoided eye contact from there on.Towards the end of the meal the manager came to our table and sarcastically told us he was going to “update our profile noting we didn’t like to seat in front of the door”. It was all a bit odd and made us feel uncomfortable. We left the restaurant in the middle of the busy dinner service and guess what…the tables in front of the door were still empty! So we weren’t the only ones refusing to sit in front of the draft. His remark was full of sarcasm and spoilt what had otherwise been a pleasant experience.

Located in southern Chelsea, Medlar offers a cozy atmosphere for fine dining without straining your budget. However, there is considerable room for improvement. The butter could be softer, and the fries need to be cooked more consistently. While the service is friendly, it lacks the sophistication expected from a fine dining establishment, with the pacing feeling uneven and somewhat chaotic at times. The portion sizes are satisfying, and the tarte tatin is great. However, the overall dining experience does not dazzle; it's mostly well-executed food. The wine pairing is good and complements the dishes nicely, though it isn't extraordinary. Had the bill been slightly higher, I might have rated it three stars. Nonetheless, it was a nice dining experience.

description: Saka Maka accepted the challenge of catering for 120 people at our village hall wedding in 2023. The quality of the food was absolutely outstanding and so many of our guests said it was the best wedding meal they had ever eaten. Everyone was talking about the panipuri!!! The food was average. It was not worth the money to be honest. The service was terrible! I will never go back to this place again and I have been to many michelin restaurants. The moment you enter the hosts are not welcoming. The sommelier is not experienced and asks you for your order prior to handing you the drinks menu. He gave us big cider glasses for red wine instead of the appropriate wine glass. The waitor was average and not very helpful with the menu explanations. The ambience is casual which can be nice at times but the furniture is a bit dated. The food did not leave us wanting more. The beef tartar which was a popular dish, tasted more like fish than it did meat. The fish was average and so was the lamb. Overall, never going back to this place. Not worth the money at all. The only thing nice was the plating but that could use improvement.

Service: the servers were extremely friendly and polite, however there is a clear distinction between this restaurant and its ability to gain another Michelin star. The servers could’ve done a better job at describing the dishes, the origins of the produce, and a wine list was left sitting on the table all night. The pacing was also a bit slow -2.5 hrs for 4 dishes is pushing it. Food: while perfectly acceptable, the food left me wanting more. No dish was perfect, always lacking in something (salt, acid, balance). The prawns were a bit bland, the sweetbreads overly claggy, and the caramel tart was salty (the miso icecream was extra salty). I wasn’t left with a “wow” feeling which is disappointing considering how lovely the staff and ambience were. Ambience: Beautiful, well presented and the staff are friendly and kind.

After a long time, I came across an Indian restaurant this packed in Wimbledon. I tried a couple of their dishes and was pleasantly surprised. I began with a lovely lychee-based cocktail, which was refreshing and delicious. For starters, I had the non-veg meat platter. The chicken tikka and salmon tikka in the platter were incredible – perfectly cooked and seasoned. Moving on to the mains, I tried the Nihari with peshwari naan. While the Nihari's texture was a bit too coarse for my liking, the naan was out-of-this-world wonderful. For dessert, I indulged in the rasmalai cake, which was absolutely delightful. The gajar ka halwa was nice too, though a bit more attention to presentation could have elevated it further. Overall, a wonderful dining experience with some standout dishes!

Cocktails 10/10, Starters 10/10, Main course / desert 7/10. The cocktails were outstanding and well presented. Same goes for the starters and they served them on a per person plate basis rather than to share which was also great. The mains (vegetarian choices) are okay with some dishes being better than others. The jackfruit biryani isn't anything memorable and honestly I've had better. The more south Indian orientated dishes such as the mango curry were definitely much more impressive so would recommend choosing those. Overall the service was good. The decor is more traditional inside and can at times feel a bit gloomy when it is quiet. However the main suggestion would be to have some background music or ambient sound as when we went it was not very busy and so felt awkwardly quiet to sit there in silence. Would recommend for the food and drink if you are looking for elevated south Indian food to Michelin standard. Decent choice for vegetarians too.

AFFORDABLE LUXURY Michelin-starred brunch YOU MUST TRY 🌟 Quilon: An Exceptional Gastronomic Experience 🌟 Located in the heart of London, Quilon is a true haven for Indian cuisine enthusiasts. I had the pleasure of trying their brunch, served every Saturday and Sunday and I was absolutely delighted. 🍽️ A Dream Brunch The Quilon brunch is a feast for the senses. Served at the table, it features an array of exceptional dishes created by their talented chefs. The cuisine is South-West coastal Indian, with a Michelin star to its name. 🍹 Cocktails and Delights The cocktails are a must-try: the Qojito with green chili-infused vodka and the Closer to the Edge with tequila and house-infused spices were my favourites. As for the food, I sampled both the vegetarian and non-vegetarian brunch menus. My highlights? The kosambari in a watermelon cup, herb-crusted seatrout, mini shrimp dosa, Malabar lamb curry, paneer, and tempered asparagus. I even asked for seconds of the best paratha I’ve ever tasted! For dessert, the almond and berries roulade stole the show. And let’s not forget the masala chai—the best I’ve ever had, even compared to my trips to India! 🌐 Ambiance and Service The service is impeccable: cheerful and well-prepared waitstaff make the experience even more enjoyable. The location itself is fantastic, setting the stage for an unforgettable culinary journey. In summary, Quilon is a culinary gem that deserves a visit. I can’t wait to go back! 🌟

If you are near Buckingham palace, this restaurant is a must visit. Yards away from Victoria station,  Try their weekend brunch which is available on Saturday and Sunday. It is a priced at £48 pp. For 5 very authentic and creative courses. Each course was beautifully presented and tasted amazing. We were very full at the end of it. Just the dessert could have had a choice we felt. It was still very good but another option would have made it even more memorable. Service was impeccable. Ambience was calming with subtle Indian instrumental music transporting you to the wonderful Kerala. There is adequate space between tables to enable you enough privacy. Service is efficient and attentive without intruding your personal space. There is no additional charge whatsoever added to the final bill, so no hidden costs like other restaurants. The icing on the cake was to see the celebrity head chef Mr. Sriram Aylur, whose over 20 years of hard work here has earned them a Michelin star. It is also ideal to celebrate a special occasion such as birthday or anniversary. It is now my favourite restaurant in London, I preferred it to Banaras and  Gymkhana. But is neck to neck with Jamavar. Go for it. It is owned by a highly prestigious five star Indian restaurant chain, Taj Hotels. They have a Taj hotel right next to it. This is Taj’s second restaurant in London, they also have Bombay Brasserie, which is also awesome. I don’t understand some poor reviews, if this is not for you, I don’t know what can please you! Highly recommended. Vegetarian options: Great veg selection. Try their jackfruit biryani. Mango Lassi.

description: Amazing experience from start to finish. They were able to accommodate gluten free for my husband and nut free for my daughter without sacrificing on quality, taste, or presentation. Food was fresh, seasonal, and delicious. Service was impeccable. Highly recommended!!

restaurant_name: Frog by Adam Handling Restaurant Covent Garden
description: My husband and I have been a little obsessed with Adam Handling, we've been to 2 of his other locations previously so we booked this for my sister and mother-in-law to indulge a little! As always the service was super attentive, and the food was fantastic (albeit a little much so I would advise eating nothing else for at least 24 hours, which is what we did). With the tasting menu, you will most certainly be rolling out of the beautiful restaurant but you'll be satisfied! The chicken butter which he is known for ( well by myself and my husband anyway ) has changed slightly, but still amazing and it's served with the most amazing bread you will ever have, you will most definitely have a heavenly moment. Most importantly, for myself and our family, they do a fully halal-friendly menu, which means you get to try things you would not be able to have in many other fine dining Michelin-starred restaurants! Ugly butterfly here we come because after being the photos online, we most certainly are adding it to our bucket list!

As always the service was super attentive, and the food was fantastic (albeit a little much so I would advise eating nothing else for at least 24 hours, which is what we did). With the tasting menu, you will most certainly be rolling out of the beautiful restaurant but you'll be satisfied! The chicken butter which he is known for ( well by myself and my husband anyway ) has changed slightly, but still amazing and it's served with the most amazing bread you will ever have, you will most definitely have a heavenly moment. Most importantly, for myself and our family, they do a fully halal-friendly menu, which means you get to try things you would not be able to have in many other fine dining Michelin-starred restaurants! Ugly butterfly here we come because after being the photos online, we most certainly are adding it to our bucket list!

restaurant_name: Frog by Adam Handling Restaurant Covent Garden
description: (Visited back in February) Food had a playful theatrical twist to it while maintaining a high level of service. The pacing did not feel rushed and the use of otherwise discarded waste ingredients was also very admirable. Some elements of dishes felt a little lacking or too strong in seasoning, though that may be personal preference, otherwise a good meal and experience that is most recommended.

Very cosy and intimate restaurant in the residential area of Angel. Staff were friendly and the food was delicious. We didn't have to wait long and I didn't realise my pizza had rocket, which I usually don't like. But even though there was a lot of it, the flavour was very subtle and worked so well with the Parma ham that I'm rethinking my aversion to rocket and what I've missed out on in life so far 😭 Tiramisu was filling and indulgent and didn't skimp on the brandy. I'm used to the cream being a bit thicker so this was lighter than I'd love but it was still delicious and if the cream was thicker, I probably wouldn't have been able to finish it. Definitely coming back to get the Saponara pizza as I tried a bit and it was amazing. Also the owner (I think) saw how my GF left her crusts and found it so funny he took a picture of it 😂

If you're looking for an authentic Italian place around Islington, this is the spot. "Just half of the menu card was real food, great presentation". Food was really great and reminded me of my travels in Italy and the local food quality. If you're able to get table here, you'll not regret the visit. If you love Italian food you need to try this genuine spot run by Italian people. Besides you can order food here, you are also able to buy some imported Italian products in here. Great concept, great restaurant. If I would be able, I would come every day.

Can’t believe I waited this long to visit Saponara, an islington local favourite for amazing Italian food. The place looks like and probably also serves as a deli with some indoor and outdoor tables, it’s casual, authentic but also well looked after. Tortellonis are to die for, with a great selection of different fillings and sauces. The pizza is so delicious too. They had run out of Tiramisu so will try that next time, but the affogato was a good compromise for the time being! Good Italian wine selection too. The prices are quite reasonable. Highly recommended for a nice meal!

Overall Pentolina looks like a nice restaurant has a very nice ambience but the food was very average. We had ordered the goats cheese with almond and honey as a starter, the dish was presented a bit strange (like a puddle) and was lacking a carb or other element. For mains we had ordered a steak medium well and their crab pasta, the pasta was cooked nicely but there was a lot of small shell pieces in the crab meat and not that much flavour, similarly the steak was lacking flavour and maybe needed a sauce plus the sides were too charred so they became a bit hard/dry. If you want somewhere relaxing to eat/drink where it's not too loud it's a nice place to go but the food definitely is just okay. We paid £64 for the three items which felt a bit pricey considering the meal we had.

Great little surprise in the Olympia- Hammersmith area. Off the main roads, in a really quiet little neighbourhood. The restaurant is cozy and welcoming. They have the ground floor and the basement floor. Lovely decorations. Lots of vintage pieces. The menu is simple but full of choices. They accommodate for vegans and gluten free. We ordered a starter and a main. Portions were pretty good and the dishes were cooked to perfection. Quick service and lovely staff. I recommend you book in advance if you have a date or the family to invite.

My partner and I had this restaurant on our lists for a while, but sadly (and surprisingly), we left disappointed. The inside of Pentolina is charming, and the staff were friendly. But the food was lacking in flavour. Firstly, I had the fennel salad — this was refreshing and delicate, but felt underwhelming and unseasoned, accompanied by a few small pieces of orange and finely sliced beetroot. I really think this is the best Sunday roast in London . Will definitely be back as soon as possible!

description: Authentic taste. Amazing food. Splendid service! Since I moved in the area, I have ordered food from Saka Maka multiple times (~50 times) . 3*Mich. I was disappointed as, to me, it lacked the magic of the Michelin star rating, the marketing and the wonderful glamorous surroundings within Dorchester Hotel. Only one dish was truly outstanding and memorable which is the scallops. It is a symphony of many different delicious flavours and textures. The remaining dishes were unremarkable. The Hugel Riesling wine is pleasant; I often have a glass of this exact same bottle in the French House Soho… hmm. The service set my teeth on edge announcing dishes far too rapidly and without engaging with us…the accent of one is so strong I could not understand what I was being told. Also I was uncomfortable with the manner of the waiting staff. I dined at Kerridge’s a few days later and both venues have enormously high ceilings; at both I found the feel/setting was unappealing and perhaps cold, compared to other venues. CH

We went for the tasting menu with paired wines. Having eaten at a few other Michelin restaurants (Core, Heston, Moor Hall, The Kitchin) we had some benchmarks to compare Alain Ducasse to.  The service is impeccable and the staff were very professional and friendly. The entire service took nearly 4.5 hours and there were long waits between courses so make sure to factor this in if you have a late reservation. The surprise was the food. Whilst some dishes (scallops, lobster) were exceptional with rich, incredible sauces we didn't have those wow moments with the other dishes that we experienced at other Michelin restaurants. I would highly recommend the caviar, the way they served it made it one of the stand-outs for us. We went for the Icons wine selection and the sommelier had done an incredible job. We didn't want to drink 7 full glasses of wine so they kindly split this so we had half a glass each per course. We got to meet Alberto (an absolute gent) and his team which was a lovely touch, and his kitchen is incredible. It's a huge restaurant and whilst the fibre optics are striking, when you're sat there you could almost see the room being used for a wedding/conference venue because of the style of wood panelling on the walls.

My partner and I recently visited Sanjugo in Shoreditch, and our experience was nothing short of exceptional. From the moment we walked in, we were warmly welcomed by the host, who was both friendly and incredibly helpful in guiding us through the menu. We decided to indulge in a variety of sushi rolls, including the Fried Soft Shell Crab Roll, Miso Prawn Maki, Spicy Tuna Roll, California Roll, and Duck Maki Roll. Each dish was meticulously prepared and bursting with flavor. Our standout favorites were the Duck Maki and the Soft Shell Crab Roll, both of which we would rate a perfect 10 out of 10. The richness of the duck paired beautifully with the freshness of the ingredients, and the fried crab roll offered a delightful crunch and savory taste that left us wanting more. As a starter, we opted for the Ebi Fry, which set the tone for the rest of the meal with its delightful flavours and perfect texture. My boyfriend also ordered the pear juice, which he praised as an excellent palate cleanser between the different sushi rolls, enhancing our overall dining experience. In summary, our visit to Sanjugo was a culinary delight. The atmosphere, the service, and most importantly, the food, were all top-notch. We left thoroughly satisfied and eager to return. Highly recommended for anyone looking to enjoy high-quality sushi in Shoreditch.

Recently dined at this vibrant restaurant, and the lively atmosphere immediately caught our attention. The place was bustling with people, creating a lively buzz. The owner, who was remarkably friendly, engaged us in a pleasant chat, adding a personal touch to our dining experience. Opting for the bottomless brunch, we were surprised to learn it doesn't happen on rugby days. Nonetheless, it gives us a perfect reason to return for another delightful experience. The food was a true highlight. We started with Papad basket which came with three delicious chutneys. Our starter Tandoori Phool was a burst of unique flavors, unlike anything I've tasted before. My other half savored the chicken biryani, expressing his delight. As a vegetarian, I tried the Artichoke- asparagus biryani, a dish I had never experienced before. To say it was extraordinarily delicious would be an understatement. The drinks complemented the meal perfectly (though my Mango turmeric tango cocktail lacked Mango flavour it was more turmericy) , rounding off a delightful dining experience. Despite the rugby day hiccup, the delicious food, friendly owner, and lively ambiance make it a place we're eager to revisit. Highly recommended for those seeking a combination of delectable cuisine and a warm, welcoming atmosphere. 🍽️🥂 #DiningDelight

The restaurant is set in a Victorian building and had a pleasant vibe, good food and service. Between the three of us, we shared the sourdough, burrata (great), asparagus (tasty but a very small portion), crab risotto (delicious and a favourite), mushroom tajarin (enjoyed the flavour but slighty salty), pici with sausage (good flavour but also a bit salty) and the radish as a side. We received a complimentary drink before our starters and another with the bill which was a nice touch. However, the waitress rushed us even though we hadn't finished our bottle of wine. We moved downstairs to the bar to finish it and also got to try their home made port-style wine. Emilia and Giuseppe took great care of us, being both knowledgeable and fun.

Wine list 🍷: intentionally didn’t post because you need to see it for yourself. Absolutely amazing list and you’re able to get a lot of very very nice wines by the glass. Staff: incredibly attentive. As soon as I dropped my knife and bent over to pick it up. The sommelier himself was already waiting with a new knife to switch out. Kudos to Guiseppe (sommelier) and Olivia our server. Our wines were served on time on the dot. Food was spaced out perfectly. Menus are changed on the daily. Hence no menu pics anywhere. Here is ours. Food: incredible! 🤩 Oysters    : amazingly fresh, juicy and meaty Asparagus    : they made this savoury cheese shortbread crust to go on top of the asparagus. You’ll love every bite. Sweet bread: best sweet bread of my life. A lot of the time jus can be over powering and way too heavy. Often it ruins the palate and appetite. This was not one of those. Highly recommend. Tajarin: delicious. It’s simplicity makes it bold and having you lick the plate clean. The mushrooms were done so well it had a nice bite without being watery. Highly recommend you ask for Parmesan to be added as garnish. T-bone: a fantastic steak that melts in your mouth. Hands down one of the best steaks in London. They come with absolutely exquisite potatoes and a chicory salad. Make no mistake these potatoes are dangerously addictive. Hard to do with potatoes that aren’t crunch but Doppo wins again. Tiramisu 🍰 : the mascarpone is next level of quality as is the coffee and Marsala.

As an Italian, finding a restaurant that truly captures the essence of our rich culinary heritage can be challenging. Doppo, however, exceeded all my expectations and delivered an authentic Italian dining experience that transported me back to Italy. From the moment I walked in, I was greeted with warm hospitality and an ambiance that beautifully combined rustic charm with modern elegance. The menu at Doppo is a testament to the richness of Italian cuisine, offering a diverse selection of dishes that highlight the best of the Tuscany region’s flavors. The pasta was freshly made and cooked to al dente perfection, while the ragù was rich, flavorful, and reminiscent of the home-cooked meals I grew up with. Each bite was a comforting reminder of the time-honored traditions that make Italian cuisine so beloved. The highlight of the meal was undoubtedly the tiramisu for dessert. Light, creamy, and with just the right amount of espresso kick, it was the perfect ending to an extraordinary meal. What truly sets Doppo apart is their commitment to quality and authenticity. Every ingredient tasted fresh and thoughtfully sourced, and the attention to detail in each dish was evident. The staff's knowledge and passion for Italian cuisine further enhanced the dining experience, making me feel like a valued guest in a family home. In conclusion, Doppo is a must-visit for anyone seeking genuine Italian flavors in an inviting and elegant setting. Whether you’re an Italian expatriate longing for a taste of home or a food enthusiast eager to explore the depth of Italy’s culinary offerings, Doppo promises a memorable and delightful dining experience. I can’t wait to return and savor more of their exquisite dishes.

Had the most wonderful evening here tasting the most flavorful food, amazing drinks and delicious desserts.  We ordered two entrees. The pappardelle had deep flavors and tender beef. The pici was cooked to perfection and I would go back for that entree alone. I loved the welcome drink, dessert wine and they also recommended the perfect wine pairing with our dinner. Leave room to try their amazing desserts. We tried the pavlova which was the perfect crisp and then we had a special “torretta” with the creamiest chocolate. Besides excellent food, the service and atmosphere make this place a standout for me. Be sure to make a reservation since it’s a small space and they fill up quickly.

Fantastic Experience at Asado Steak House I recently visited Asado Steak House and had a wonderful dining experience. I started with the empanadas, trying both the chicken and beef varieties at £3.50 each. They were delicious and filled generously, setting a great tone for the meal. For the main course, I ordered the rump steak for £22, cooked to perfection at medium. It's quite rare to find a steakhouse that gets the cooking just right, but Asado nailed it. The steak was juicy and flavorful, paired perfectly with a rich pepper sauce that added just the right amount of kick. We did have to buy the fries separately at £3.50 was also delicious! Despite the restaurant not being busy, the service was prompt and efficient, with very little wait time for our food. Additionally, it's worth mentioning that all the food is halal, which is a big plus for many diners. Overall, Asado Steak House offers excellent food, particularly for steak lovers, and provides a pleasant dining experience. My meal came up to £32 including starters and steak and 1 soft drink which is great. Highly recommended! Parking: Park on the fromt pay via ringo, or after 5.30 its free on single yellow.

I dined here last week and it was absolutely fantastic! The food was so delicious that I’m still thinking about it a week later and can’t wait to dine again! I got the ribeye steak and chips, coleslaw and button mushrooms, all of which were absolutely delightful. As a Asian woman travel alone in London, my recent solo dining experience at this restaurant was utterly unacceptable. Despite sitting alone, there were plates for two left on my table throughout the meal. While other tables were served right away, I asked the waiter for water. Furthermore,  unlike other guests, even water wasn’t  poured for me. Later, another server inquired if I was waiting for someone, which I wasn't. And only then did the waiter remove the extra plates from the table. Finally, upon leaving, I thanked the staff member at the door, but received no response. This experience was a stark disappointment, especially considering it was my first meal in London. It left me feeling unwelcome and disregarded as a customer. I was very upset and felt like I was being racially discriminated against by the stark difference in service compared to other customers. If you excuse that what I experienced was not racial discrimination, then everything I experienced must have happened to other ‘Western customers’ as well. Think about it one more time.

The dishes at this restaurant don't match the pictures, and the fish we saw on Google Maps isn't on the menu. So, friends planning to dine here, please take note. Additionally, their 'big plate' is overpriced and literally just a large plate with very little food. This restaurant offers poor value for money. Also, the lamb has a strong taste, so friends who dislike that flavor should avoid ordering it. I rarely write reviews after dining, but the service at this restaurant was exceptionally poor. A female server had a sour expression the whole time, as if I owed her two million pounds. Moreover, as soon as we finished eating, she rushed to clear the table, as if she wanted us gone. We've dined in Scotland a few days ago and at a Malaysian restaurant in London yesterday, and this restaurant has by far the worst service. So it really doesn’t deserve the 12% service fare. I don't understand how it has such high ratings.

*2nd visit* Dinner Came again to try their dinner menus. The caulifower and potatoes were probably the highlights for us. The flavours and textures were there compared to other dishes we had ordered that evening. Had high hopes for the zucchini but somehow didn’t enjoy it as much as other dishes. Also, the portions of the sharing plates were quite small in my opinion. In terms of service, many of the servers were friendly and approchable enough, but one stood out as unfriendly, bordering on arrogant/rude. It could just be a bad day for that particular staff but still, it was unpleasant for diners to interact with them. *1st visit* Brunch Recommended by a local to try out the dishes here, had high hopes but weren’t particularly impressed by the execution except for the french toast. Of course, it may be that the taste of these dishes just didn’t suit our fancy. All the savoury breakfast dishes were heavily seasoned for us (being the first thing you eat in the morning) other than the dish with the kale salad. That at least had the freshness and citrusy of the vegetable and dressing to cut through the richness and creaminess. We were thankful that we ordered the french toast as it really helped changed up the taste with the sweetness of the fruits and crunchiness of the toasted bread. Though its matcha latte needed much improvement but I understand that it’s not a Japanese restaurant so… Overall, I’d re visit to try other dishes but would hope for a more welcoming, more efficient hospitality next time.

Extremely fast and attentive service Olives and tomato dip on table in seconds of arriving. Olives, delicious, spicy, little too salty Tomato dip, delicious, sweet and juicy Basket of bread brought very shortly after. Fesh, soft and crispy but no doner kebab sauce on it(special Turkish secret). Still great when dipped in tomatoe dip. Mixed shish for main (Chicken & Lamb) Lamb, juicy, succulent, flavorful, soft, perfect Chicken, little dry (but very rarely very juicy anywhere) soft, charcoal flavour good Basmati rice a little basic but cooked right and soft, nice rice Salad lacked flavour, missing a nice dressing like pomegranate sauce. Yogurt on the side an unusual addition and not sure why/what exactly its meant to go with but nice, thick, rich and creamy Decor very chilled, dim lighting gives a relaxed and intimate vibe without being too romantic. Family friendly. Nice sofa style seating at some tables Plenty of pretty traditional hanging lights and plates on the walls setting the scene. Tea has sugar sachet not authentic cube. Pistachio ice cream, delicious, creamy, sweet but not too sweet with plenty of pistachio pieces. Baklava, warm, not cold like many places which is great! A little dry, maybe sitting a while but, not stale. Needed more honey on top. Pastry a little powdery/crumbly not soft and juicy. Not too sweet though like some baklava can be. The restaurant has a good authentic feel. Price at the higher end of mixed grills at £21.50 or £28 for mixed shish and kofté but not the most expensive and some others charging in the same range do not provide near the level of service or quality of food 4/5 Kid-friendliness: Families well catered to and staff friendly
