Anglo Our first visit to Anglo in October last year turned out to be one of the dining highlights of 2023. Well I can honestly say that our return visit on Saturday will take some beating in 2024. The imagination , creativity and skill of chef Anthony Raffo is nothing short of genius as he puts together some amazing dishes using the very best British produce. To match this you have manager / sommelier Marie Danzavilliers with her absolutely amazing friendly service and drinks pairings that complement each course perfectly. The restaurant is only a short walk from Farringdon Station on St. Cross Street. When you enter you will see that it’s a small restaurant seating between 14 -18 guests. This is why they can manage with a a very small team giving you friendly and personal service. You will also see an abundance of jars which are filled with all sorts of pickled ingredients. Their food style is from foraging and pride themselves on not wasting anything in order to create more fabulous dishes. Our return on saturday started with a lovely welcome from Marie before showing us to our table. We decided to have a drink while we looked at the menu and chose the Earth Ale Spicy Weiss beer and the Strawberries on Sea gose. The menu is Eleven Courses (including snacks and petit fours) priced at just £85 pounds and there is also a supplemented dish if you so wish. This I have to say is one of the best value for money Tasting Menu’s you will find anywhere. There is also a Drinks Pairing which is Five glasses for £49 pounds that believe me is well worth trying. There is a choice of a smaller tasting menu at lunchtime. We opted for the full tasting menu with the extra course and for myself I chose to have the drinks pairing. This began with our first snack of a drinkable White Cabbage , Hampshire breed pork , parsley and rapeseed. This was followed by the second snack of the Norfolk sand carrot which was very clever indeed. Now it was time for the bread which is the Anglo Sourdough with yeast and wild mushroom. This leads to the first course with a wine pairing and oh my god what an absolute delight it was to. The Yorkshire Leek with potato , ramson caper , tunworth and three-cornered leek. The depth of flavour was incredible and something you’ll find in every course. The pairing was a 2022 Skin Contact “Maria” Madeleine Angeline from the Renegade Winery in Bethnal Green , East London. This was followed by my personal highlight of the day. The Line Caught Cornish Cod , hay , cauliflower , hazelnut and sea purslane was quite simply stunning. The cod was matched perfectly with a 2022 Le Besson , Domaine Batard Langelier from Loire , France. Now it was time for the supplemented dish of Hampshire Trout , wild rocket , herring roe , purple sprouting broccoli , broad beans and goat’s curd. We then moved on to two Duck courses with the first being an incredible Devon Duck doughnut with a fabulous walnut purée. This was followed by the amazing Devon Duck , hogweed seed and swede. The wine pairing was unbelievable because on its own it was ok but with the duck it became soft and fruity. This was a 2020 Biografico , Uve de Vida from Castilla-La Mancha , Spain. Now it was time for the cheese course and it was very clever and delicious. The Somerset Montgomery Cheddar with Isle of Wight black garlic and walnut amazingly tasted like a savoury tiramisu. The pairing was a Pure Mead from the Loxwood Meadworks in West Sussex. Your palate was then refreshed with a Yorkshire Forced Rhubarb with gherkin , dill and oxalis. Now it was time to finish was an absolute genius of a dessert. It was a Jack Buck Farm Celeriac ice cream with a charred celeriac skin and a meringue. The pairing was equally fabulous in the form of a sweet apple Somerset Ice Cider. We then finished with a coffee and petit fours of Hay fudge and beetroot. This brought an end to an incredible dining experience where the food was outstanding and matched with fabulous drinks pairings. I really can’t recommend a visit to Anglo highly enough.

This is my favourite fine-dining restaurant in London. They use all UK-based ingredients, and half of the paring wines are also from the UK—the best place to introduce decent UK food to my visiting friend. The ambience is excellent. The staff is kind. She always explains the food and wines well with details of notes, colours, scents, tastes, etc. Those demonstrate to improve the experience because you would think what you expect. Until now, all of my friends I brought there told me it is the best restaurant they've tried in London. I think the price is also a strength of the restaurant, and I guess that is because of the location. If the restaurant was a bit west or east from the site, the price must be at least 50 pounds more expensive per person. The restaurant is firm with the sour flavour because they use fermented ingredients. Seafood lovers would like the place because they use seaweed flavour for the final touch. I like sour flavours and seafood, so it is the perfect place.

Zoilo has been on my shortlist for quite a while. Finally found an opportunity to have a business meal here. Upon walking in through what looks like a residential door, we were immediately struck by the fine balance this small restaurant has between casual bar in the centre and refined dining at the tables around the edges. Although we were having a business meal, there was a couple two tables down from us on a first date ("nice to meet you") confirming it is a good date venue as we suspected. Greeted by the maitre'd we were seated in a corner table under the speaker. A request to turn down the music slightly so we could hear each other was immediately actioned. Service was good. Prompt with the only area for improvement being timing of questions. Rather than wait for a pause in conversation, the different servers would approach us to ask and crowbar their question in. Seems quite common in restaurants but not the way high class service is. Hence four stars in this area. Everything else was to a very high standard. Onto the food: - In-house Charcuterie (salami, pancetta & pork shoulder), pickles & toast: absolutely outstanding and a great price considering the quality. In fact, if you go downstairs you see the fridge where it looks like they're curing the meat. I'll make sure to ask them next time. - Grilled Hand Dived Scallop, fennel, anchovies & apple, roe sabayon: sublime and as good as Gordon Ramsay's Petrus where a similar scallop dish has been on the menu for years as a favourite. - Bife Ancho | Rib Eye & our chimichurri sauce: could not be faulted. Cooked to perfection and the sauce was a fresh accompaniment with layers of flavour. - Bife Angosto | Glazed Sirloin, house chorizo, shallots & tarragon jus: again, fantastically prepared. Out of the two steaks, I preferred the chimchurri, but if you like a little bit of sweet tang to your sauce then get this dish. - Hand cut chips Provenzal: can't really go wrong with chips. Good to see they didn't here! - Dulce de leche Crème Brûlée & "banana split": this was the dish where I was a little disappointed. It was fine, but not standout. Although I'm not sure how you make creme brûlée standout. The serving of the dessert in the centre of the table and two spoons during a business meal without our request was a little....strange. Upon walking in through what looks like a residential door, we were immediately struck by the fine balance this small restaurant has between casual bar in the centre and refined dining at the tables around the edges. Although we were having a business meal, there was a couple two tables down from us on a first date ("nice to meet you") confirming it is a good date venue as we suspected. Greeted by the maitre'd we were seated in a corner table under the speaker. A request to turn down the music slightly so we could hear each other was immediately actioned. Service was good. Prompt with the only area for improvement being timing of questions. Rather than wait for a pause in conversation, the different servers would approach us to ask and crowbar their question in. Seems quite common in restaurants but not the way high class service is. Hence four stars in this area. Everything else was to a very high standard. Onto the food: - In-house Charcuterie (salami, pancetta & pork shoulder), pickles & toast: absolutely outstanding and a great price considering the quality. In fact, if you go downstairs you see the fridge where it looks like they're curing the meat. I'll make sure to ask them next time. - Grilled Hand Dived Scallop, fennel, anchovies & apple, roe sabayon: sublime and as good as Gordon Ramsay's Petrus where a similar scallop dish has been on the menu for years as a favourite. - Bife Ancho | Rib Eye & our chimichurri sauce: could not be faulted. Cooked to perfection and the sauce was a fresh accompaniment with layers of flavour. - Bife Angosto | Glazed Sirloin, house chorizo, shallots & tarragon jus: again, fantastically prepared. If I could give this place more than five stars I would. This restaurant is truly a hidden gem in Marble Arch. Upon arrival the staff were extremely friendly and welcoming and greeted us with hand sanitiser due to Covid. The menu is small but very interesting dishes (focusing on quality!). I was starters, mains and deserts were absolutely delicious! After every bite of every dish that we took, we just had to say “wow!”. Everything we ordered was extremely flavourful and cooked to perfection with quality in every detail taken. Service, the staff were so caring, funny, friendly and attentive. The food came out in a really good time and we were able to share everything which was nice! The rosemary spritz was so delicious and flavourful. The restaurant management and waiters were so friendly that they gave us a small complimentary jar of their famous sauce which is absolutely delicious and a celebration card as a gift! It was such a beautiful and thoughtful gesture. The restaurant is decorated very nicely, situated in a lovely area and it’s very cosy inside. A really nice feature was an additional side table that they put aside each table for additional space and drinks. Overall this is an amazing restaurant, with astonishingly delicious food, lovely atmosphere, immaculate customer service and pride in the quality of food and service. Highly recommended and will definitely be coming back.

We dined at Ormer on the first night of a 5 day trip to London in January 2024 and it was a great start. The staff were friendly, very helpful and happy to chat between courses about our thoughts on the food. Each course was delicious and packed with flavour. From the generous canapes, deconstructed Waldorf salad opener, stunningly light barley brioche, richly flavoured warm Iberico ham jelly, via the cured mackerel, impressive 2 dish pigeon followed by the brown butter and chocolate dessert, right down to the petit fours we enjoyed the lot! The flavours were all distinct yet blended well. At the end of the meal we were given another petit four to take away plus a small signed and dated copy of the menu to keep- a lovely extra touch and something which just added to the experience. We'll definitely return the next time we're in London!

Came here on a Sunday with a friend for lunch. I had made a reservation in advance seeing how many reviews this place has got so I assumed it would have been packed on a Sunday but it was literally empty apart from one table outside. We went with the cold mix mezze as a starter and it was fantastic. It came with 5 types of dips essentially and some seasoned pita bread on the side which was so so delicious. Bread was soft and fluffy and went well with the hummus, baba ghanoush, cacik, tabbouleh and braised aubergine. Then for mains, we went for the lamb skewers with rice and the chicken in yoghurt sauce with croutons. Again, both were super delicious and flavourful. Lamb was cooked to perfection, soft and tender and super well-marinated which went well with the rice. Chicken was juicy and tender also and the tomato and yoghurt sauce was so moreish I kept dipping the lamb into the sauce too. Interesting ingredient choice of croutons in the chicken dish which added more crunchy texture to the dish and made it fun to eat. Service was good but I won't say outstanding, staff were nice and friendly. I loved the interior design with the modern choice of pink chairs and glasses on wooden tables. It's very stylish yet it feels cosy at the same time. Can see it being a great date location too. Would be happy to come back soon!

This is one of my favourite places in London and I normally recommend it to my friends and people I know are big foodies. This restaurant has been a staple of my London life since 1992, the year I moved to Uk, and it has always been consistent, faultless, and just perfect. The ambience is still good, the food is still good, the lack of attention to detail and the rushed, careless service from our waiter ( a short, bald guy that was probably rushed off or simply too busy to cope with guests asking for guidance on wines, or desserts, leaving us meanwhile we were talking to him, mid-sentence), is simply unbelievable. If you are busy, I understand, but leaving us meanwhile we are deciding, or asking your opinion, is not ok, no matter how you want to look at it. It happened twice, when I was asking for advise on the wine, and then again when we were trying to order the desserts. I am ok with waiting, I am ok with receiving the starters before the wine we ordered, I am ok with leaving the langoustine shelves on the table for a long time and getting the wine at the wrong temperature, and not clearing a small table, not replacing the dirty plates and cutlery, and not bringing the new cutlery, but it is not ok to tell us in an angry way to move a very small iPhone so he could put the new food on the table without having cleared the dirty plates and cutlery which were there for a long time first. This was also a birthday dinner for my best friend, and this was specified in the reservation. Of course it was ignored and nothing was mentioned or even acknowledged during our dinner. Again, I am astonished by how badly things have gone in one of my favourite places on the service side. We ordered the smoked mackerel and the langoustines to start with, the pork chop with fennel and the hake with anchoiade, plus a very good Chassagne Montrachet, and a brownie with blackcurrant and creme fraiche, together with a meringue with pear and chocolate sauce . I am very sad to say I am not rushing to go back . Which is a shame, as I was very fond of this restaurant.

High quality, tasty food for great prices. I think this has to be one of the best restaurants in London for the quality to price ratio if you're looking for a nice place to eat on a date. We had two starters: the squid and the duck. Both were paired nicely wine by our water. They were fresh tasting with the crunchy veggies complimenting the textures of the meat. For mains, we took a fish and a meat dish - both delicious. For dessert, we had the cheesecake. It was pretty good, but I think you can find a better Basque cheesecake elsewhere.

First time family visit to this restaurant, we were greeted with ample smiles as we arrived and were taken to our table to get settled, the space itself was simple, comfortable and authentic, our server Fabiano was very friendly and had a good knowledge of the menu, he was attentive throughout the course of the evening, always in hand nearby if needed. We ordered multiple dishes from the menu including starters, small & large plates consisting of a variety of meats and veggies which were all beautifully cooked and presented, and to be fair they all tasted very good, the family favourite was the beef shin curry or " Gaeng gatti " , the beef was soft and tender and the curry was well made, tasty with a nice little kick, all in all we had a great time with the family and would definitely go back !

One of my favorite Greek restaurants in London, this place offers an amazing take on Greek cuisine. The menu is complemented by a wide selection of wines at great prices, enhancing the overall dining experience. must-try tarama and spicy feta, both great. The calamari is perfectly crispy and light, while the octopus is simply phenomenal. The aubergine, broccoli, and salads are all great and well executed. The ribeye, accompanied by fantastic au jus, is a highlight, cooked to perfection and deeply satisfying. The orzo dish was disappointing. Initially, it was excessively salty, and when we requested a replacement, it returned completely flavorless. I’ll avoid this dish in the future. Desserts are generally excellent, though the vanilla ice cream is a bit bland and the baklava dessert a touch overpowering. Overall, this restaurant offers great food, a wonderful atmosphere, and impeccable service, topped off by an amazing sommelier.

It was the second Michelin starred restaurant we tried. We went there for lunch, we were a party of 5 for the bar express menu. Keep in mind they only have tables for 4, so we split our reservation into a group of 3 and 2 of us stayed at the bar, the groups of 2 are always seated at the bar. But we kind of enjoyed this vibe. The drinks are very good and nicely presented. We paired a negroni and a spritz with the parmesan fries which are really interesting. We took the 3 course menu. The appetizer with the jersualem artichoke was to die for, an explosion of tastes left you speechless for a couple of seconds while you tried to figure out what is it exactly you ate. For the mains both of them were very nice, the 3 fishes came with a nice bouillabaisse, a bit almondy for my taste but still it paired nicely. The beef was really tasty and tender for a cut of beef that was not ribeye or fillet. The tiramisu was perfectly executed but the star of dessert was the Panna Cotta with rhubarb. Would gladly return here to try the full tasting menu

Even though it was a Michelin starred restaurant, we went there without any expectation as we were opting for the more “quick and budget-friendly” lunch option. The quality of the food was superb considering the price of the 3-course meal (£30). The fried Jerusalem artichoke dish was so flavourful and imo the best dish we had that day. The main was slightly underwhelming considering both the starters were great. Bavette steak was quick chewy but I would assume it’s due to the choice of cut as meat was cooked to the perfect medium rare temperature as seen in picture. Service was good - the staff were attentive. Overall, it was an enjoyable dining experience  at Luca.

Pleasant enough place - very comfy atmosphere with nice decor. Staff were very nice and friendly. We had the shared starter made of halloumi, chicken wings, fried brie, and goat's cheese crostini. Crostini was nice, the others lacking a little quality imho. Mains were chicken mozzarella which was very nice, and baked sea bass - which looked great but lacked much taste- slightly watery fish. 3 stars is harsh but for me, not up to a 4 I'm afraid. It's ok there- nice surroundings, and probably better than other local places.

description: We had one starter and two mains. The bread / cheese (Kachuri I think) was good but slightly salty. description: A lovely surprise! This beautiful, traditional restaurant was quiet when we arrived, but soon filled up after the England/Switzerland match. Service was excellent and the food quite different and very tasty - portions are generous, especially the honey cake which we shared between the two of us. A lovely selection of soft drinks - we had fejoa flavoured lemonade which was absolutely delicious, but impossible to describe (see photo). Would definitely return when I'm next in London 😊

restaurant_name: Kartuli - Georgian Restaurant in East Dulwich- London
description: What a lovely surprise walking around Dulwich and discovered this great gem. Beautiful decor in an old Victorian building probably used as butcher or game shop. Fantastic atmosphere specially this evening as Georgia was playing the Euro Cup. It was very lively. We sat outside, it was much quieter and have a delicious rose wine and a mezze. Absolutely delicious food and the wine was superb. Our waiter was super friendly and knowledgeable (Misho) and we were great by the lady owner which made us feel very welcome. Old fashion hospitality as it should be. Thank you both for such a great evening. Definitely a place to return soon and try more tasty food and other wines.

This place is not somewhere you would stumble upon by accident, but I seriously urge you to seek it out. The food is sensational, especially the seafood. We went for the 6 course tasting menu as we like to try a broad sample of dishes, and were really glad we did. The spiced chickpea chaat with yoghurt is one of the best dishes I’ve eaten all year - crunchy on the inside, creamy in the outside, and bursting with flavour. The Malabar prawn is one of the best prawns I’ve ever eaten. The scallop was delicious. We also had an off-menu pre-starter that the kitchen sent which was delightful, while the meat dishes (chargrilled chicken, and lamb chops) were both tender and tasty. We had great service from every single member of staff, especially Akeel. And the whole meal was rounded off by a fabulous chocolate delight (my wife had ice cream due to allergies) and some interesting drinks, including a sparkling Jasmine tea which I’d never seen before. Kahani doesn’t shout about how good it is, it lets the food do the talking, and that is more than enough. There were lots of other dishes on the menu (such as some of the tandoori ones) that sounded amazing so hopefully I’ll try them next time. One of my favourite Indian restaurants in London and certainly one of the tastiest.

Went here Monday 27/05. We’ve reserved a booking at 12:00. Staff at the reception was really friendly at went straight to showing us our table. Not just the staff from the reception who was approachable and friendly but all their staff were friendly, knowledgeable and it made our lunch pleasant and comfortable. After sorting out everything, we had a quick talk with Taki explaining the restaurant and that they have a published book for their recipes in the restaurant. I took the opportunity to ask how to cook the garlic mushroom(side) I had ordered. I didn’t find it in the book but Carolina kindly sent it to us via e-mail and I’m really thankful for that. Paul was kind enough to be in our service. We ordered drinks first, and then ordered starters and mains since we were starving. For the drinks, I ordered the non-alcoholic one, which was the Shirley Temple. ( I loved it, especially with the cherries on top) I had to ask Paul if I could top up the cherries after I finished the first batch. For starters, we ordered Hawksmoor Smoked Salmon and Bone Marrow with Onions. I was not able to taste the salmon though. But one thing I can say about the Bone Marrow was it was tasty and has a very unique combination. It was so full, and the onions compliment the bone marrow. It has a bit of sweetness (from the onion) and saltiness which is the perfect balance. I was already full from my starters. Had to adjust my stomach so it can fit more food. For the Main, we ordered the T-bone medium rare 650g. When it was served I was so excited. They have explained each side of the T-bone. Sirloin and fillet. It was cooked beautifully and you can definitely appreciate the pinkness and tenderness of the meat. I preferred the sirloin part since it has a bit of fat compared to the fillet but it was really melting in the mouth and you can’t really resist having more from it. You don’t need a sauce from it as well. Good for sharing as well (2person). For the sides, we ordered Beef dipping fries and garlic mushrooms. The fries were cooked well and it was crispy with their intended taste. For the Garlic Mushroom, I can say never miss ordering this side. It was delectable. It has some buttery salt taste, with other unique combination of ingredients in it. I was really loving it and if I wasn’t full enough, I would have ordered a second batch of the Garlic Mushroom. For dessert, we ordered their Sticky Toffee Pudding. I have been always a fan of sticky toffee puddings. It’s always my first choice of dessert when eating out. The sauce was sweet, balanced with the pudding and topped with cream. Loved it all the way. The ambience and the vibe of the interior were elegant. The bar was separated from the dining area. It was a comfortable experience with no pressure. Because every staff was really capable and approachable.

description: Due to my previous experience with delivery, where I found the food very delicious, I decided to visit the nearby restaurant for a takeaway this time. Initially, the service was very friendly. Although they only accepted cash, they offered the option to pay via bank transfer. However, when I was having a picnic in the park, I found a piece of wire in the fried chicken, which was shocking. After returning to the restaurant to inform the staff and explain that my gums were bleeding because of it, the staff did not apologize at all. Instead, they took the wire to the kitchen, came back with a mocking attitude, refunded the cash, and I left. During the whole process, there were 3-4 staff members present, but none of them apologized. It seemed as if this was a common occurrence!

restaurant_name: Dotori Korean and Japanese -Walk in system-
description: Having been recommended this place by our host we decided to give it a try.  The sheer busyness convinced us it was going to be amazing. Walking in we were doubtful we would get a table but a kind waiter beckoned us to a seat. Once settled  we perused through the Korean/ Japanese menu. I was very thirsty too so ordered sake, water , plum soda and a beer. To eat we shared breadcrumb scallops,  miso,  vegetable croquette, eel with donburi and yakisoba. As mentioned it was busy and we were asked if a couple could sit next to us. We agreed but instantly regretted it. They were very loud and did not consider us who are more gently spoken. So all we could do was just stare at each other. Anyway, the starters were of good size and very hot temperature-wise.  My eel was plentiful but was difficult to eat with the tough skin attached and being In such large pieces. It only came with three sliced pickles as well. My partners' yakisoba was very greasy and not the best of flavours. Looking at other dishes being served like the pork and tempura prawns these looked immense so think it's luck out the draw ..overall food was okay, service great but hated the atmosphere

restaurant_name: Dotori Korean and Japanese -Walk in system-
description: I really like this Japanese and Korean restaurant. It’s very close to Finsbury Park tube station, just walk for about a minute or two and it's said to be run by a family for about ten years now. Initially, they only had four tables, but now they have two and a half floors, with quirky anime-themed decorations. Here are some of their standout dishes that I ordered and quite like: SCALLOP KATSU: Breaded and fried scallops served with tasty Japanese sauce. Crispy outside, tender inside, it's a fun taste experience. DEOJI BULGOGGI: Spicy pork belly marinated in honey, Korean chilli sauce, and soy sauce. It's a mix of sweet and oily flavours that's hard not to love. YUKHOE BIBIMBAP: Thinly sliced raw beef (or shredded beef) and raw egg yolk mixed with rice in a stone pot. It looks a bit like French dish Steak Tartare but the beef is partially cooked by the hot pot. It tastes really good.The sushi platter is beautifully arranged, with fresh salmon, tuna, sweet shrimp, seaweed, and octopus slices. The sushi is made by the chef with great care, it's a pleasure to watch them being prepared. Their matcha ice cream is a generous portion and has a nice matcha flavour, it's delicious. In terms of London's Japanese-Korean cuisine, personally, it feels quite affordable. £30 per person can get you a pretty good meal.

This is a case of not enough stars, should be 10 stars for this place. A fantastic experience, service was superb, we had a few questions which were answered with no trouble, the older waitresses are so lovely, like aunties serving your food. And the food, it is absolutely delicious, maybe went a bit overboard (pun intended) but the menu all looks amazing. So we went for the chefs selection nigiri sushi, it was amazing, tuna, salmon, octopus, seabass, bonito etc, not a fan of roe but I think they would replace if you asked before ordering. The tempura and salmon teriyaki were great but the skewers were unreal, and the king prawn was massive and juicy, you can see them being cooked to perfection behind the counter on the hibachi grill. It's all very straightforward but skills at the highest level. It is expensive, but it is worth it, other than my green tea sour was not sour enough, and they didn't have any konomono starter left, but other than that, an absolute stupefying pleasure. Super recommended, and can't wait to go back. Arigato gozaimasu!

I approved both the service and atmosphere of this beautiful Japanese style restaurant, but the food there was really really disappointing. The sushi roll - i didn’t take pictures of this but the rice is warm… and it definitely doesnt taste better than even Wasabi to be priced at that. 3. Skewers - these are good! Indeed! But this is the only one good dish among all we’ve ordered 4. Soba - I understand we ordered cold soba but this is way beyond cold, it is FREEZING! The noodles themselves also dont look nor taste fresh. It’s like they’ve cooked it for very long and stored them in iced water… and the sauce is tasteless also… 5. And be ware of the sake tasting menu, it actually costs you more than ordering each sake shot on the tasting menu individually. One of the sake was run out and they replaced it with an even cheaper one, feels like scam but we made the choice, who’s there to blame. So we paid £40 per person ended up craving for some more KFC. (Again, skewers were worth it, but that’s all)

The sushi roll - i didn’t take pictures of this but the rice is warm… and it definitely doesnt taste better than even Wasabi to be priced at that. 3. Skewers - these are good! Indeed! But this is the only one good dish among all we’ve ordered 4. Soba - I understand we ordered cold soba but this is way beyond cold, it is FREEZING! The noodles themselves also dont look nor taste fresh. It’s like they’ve cooked it for very long and stored them in iced water… and the sauce is tasteless also… 5. And be ware of the sake tasting menu, it actually costs you more than ordering each sake shot on the tasting menu individually. One of the sake was run out and they replaced it with an even cheaper one, feels like scam but we made the choice, who’s there to blame. So we paid £40 per person ended up craving for some more KFC. (Again, skewers were worth it, but that’s all)

Place came highly recommend from a friend. We decided to try it out because another restaurant we originally wanted to go was closed. The staff are extremely friendly and take the time to give recommendations and offer their opinions when asked. The restaurant itself has a beautiful atmosphere that leaves patrons very comfortable and at ease. For the appetizers we got the Pacific tempura shrimp and chicken wings. The teriyaki chicken wings were perfectly sauced, although they weren't very crispy they were still enjoyable. The pacific shrimp tempura was perfect in every way. Amazing sauces, perfectly crispy with the best shrimp I've had in a while. We ordered two virgin cocktails, I got the passion fruit mojito, and I swear I could bring a whole gallon without getting tired of the taste. We ordered a thick cut prime rib, which was the most tender piece of meat I've ever tasted. It had all the flavour that naturally comes with the prime rib, with the perfect amount of chew. They have perfected their steaks. We also order the Wagyu burger. It looked amazing, very soft and tender, unfortunately from a flavour standpoint it didn't wow me like the rest of the dishes. Overall this place, although a tad pricey ( £100 for two) is definitely worth going to once in a while for a fancy evening. Finally with the bill, I wanted to give an additional tip because of the fantastic service, only to notice that it was already included. It's a shame because I would have given them more than what was included in the bill.

Celebrating our 30th wedding anniversary at Hannah. Pressure was on to find a memorable venue, being 'foodies' there is always a risk of one tasting menu meal blending into another. Not so at Hannah! I'd worked in Japan many years ago and Kaiseki meals are always an event. I've looked out for this style menu in London ever since. Hannah had been on my radar since it opened, but the price was daunting given it hadn't received Michelin notice. Recently Andy Hayler visited and having read his reviews (visiting twice in short order) I knew I had to go. It's not a restaurant with wow factor in terms of Instagram decor (yes, the toilets are an adventure) but that isn't the point. The menu and the genuine enthusiasm displayed by the servers and the chefs is what makes this restaurant shine. It is a meal we will remember for years to come, even if we can't afford to experience the full menu on a regular basis. I won't try and describe the dishes, would recommend reading Andy Haylers reviews as he does the food far more credit than I could, but it was an exquisite meal. The ingredients were first class, the serveware was beautiful and the sake sommelier knew her stuff, and was very respectful, addressing my wife directly regularly rather than focusing on the 'alpha male' as is usually the case in these situations. I was also able to request a pescatarian menu for my wife when arranging the booking. Will return for the lunch menus each season change, and the full 12 courses as funds permit.

This is interesting given that the restaurant seems to only cater to tourist and is extremely overpriced (these prices are what would be expected at an upscale fine dining restaurant not this place).

This was my third visit to The Delaunay and it remains absolutely outstanding. Two of us had the chicken schnitzel with lingonberry compote and a side of fries, which were excellent, while my mum thoroughly enjoyed the wild mushroom stroganoff with herb-buttered spätzle. We did also order the broccoli side dish, which was a bit underwhelming and didn't feel worth the price at all. For dessert, we ordered the Kaiserschmarrn and apple strudel to share, and staff wonderfully brought out a slice of Sachertorte with a Happy Birthday slice of marzipan for my mum, which was a lovely touch and most appreciated. The trio of desserts were all *extremely* rich! Service was outstanding (apologies as I didn't get the name of the team who served us) and we'll definitely be back. Vegetarian options: The mushroom stroganoff was superb.

My darling friend  took me for a post birthday meal/girlie catchup. May is birth month and, I am celebrating everyday!   🎉✌🏾   We dined at Filika, a Mediterranean restaurant on Wanstead High Street. To start we enjoyed complimentary humus and bread then I proceeded to order a lychee martini which was exquisite. For my main I decided to try their herb crusted salmon fillet served with sautéed spinach, mash Potato, pomegranate and a side of garlic lemon butter cream sauce. It was the best piece of salmon I have ever eaten. Whilst my friend had Steamed mussels,cooked with wine & onions with a choice of cream sauce served with chips. Finally, for desserts I had an apple tart tatin and my friend opted for a tiramisu torte it was decadent and creamy. The food was divine 10 out of 10. The cocktails were strong, you could taste that they used premium ingredients. They were all very cordial and the service was quick.

We were a party of eight people who went here for dinner. Our hosts highly recommended this restaurant, and they were right. The restaurant looks like an English pub from the outside, but inside, it's a very posh and luxurious setting that is perfect for an entertaining night out in central London. The place is quite large, multileveled, and with separate bar- and dining areas. The staff are discreet and polite, and they will cater to your every need. Food: This is high-end, authentic South Indian cuisine, so expect hot spices, chillies, savoury sauces, and many small plates and dishes on the table. All your traditional expected dishes are on the menu, and you should order three or four dishes per person (or share) to have a filling experience. The food is expensive. There are no condiments or sides, so you'll be spending more than you normally do on Indian food. But the food is worth it. It's delicious and satisfying. Vegetarian options: Many indian dishes are natively vegetarian, and they have most selections Dietary restrictions: True indian dishes with true indian spices, means HEAT and savoury sauces. Fingerlicking good ;-) Parking: Its central London, so get a taxi Kid-friendliness: Nope. Adults night out Wheelchair accessibility: Nope. Multi-levelled, toilets in the basement

Sanskruti is Vegetarian/Vegan restaurant in Liverpool City centre. It is just a few minutes walk from Liverpool One, so relatively easy to get to. The menu is vast and has lots to choose from, our server kindly gave us some strong suggestions which we loved! We had the Daal Makhani which used black lentils with a smokey creamy base, it was delicious. Next we tried the Channa Masala, which had perfectly cooked chickpeas with a flavourful sauce. We also had the Vegan Chick'n curry which honestly might have been my favourite dish! The vegan chick'n was cooked tandoori style which really took it to the next level. The base was just delicious sweet, spicy and tangy absolutely perfect. Then we had Aloo Gobi which was a very close second, everything was cooked perfectly and was just really delicious. On the side we also had a Peshwari Naan which was fantastic. For dessert we tried the Chocolate Heaven which was delicious. The sizzling chocolate sauce worked really well and the ice cream cooled it down to get the perfect temperature. Overall this was my favourite plant-based Indian food I have tried. It is extremely well balanced and there is a distinct lack of oil or butter which means the spices and flavour is the focus. Excellent service and great food, I would advise anyone to come and see how good the food is! 😁

I’ll definitely come back for the grills at Sufi as they were top! Their grills are absolutely delicious and very well-made, the whole grill platter was amazing and I’d highly recommend it. We ordered the Sufi platter for 2 to share and tried the chicken skewers, the kebabs and kofta and all were top! Kofta is a bit fatty (as it should be) so I personally wouldn’t order it as a dish on its own, but among a sharing platter is great. The grills also each come with a side of rice and salad which is very filling. The main downside on the food was the starter platters. We ordered the Naz Khatoun and Hummus Classic with the bread. The starters were a bit underwhelming, including the bread. I’d recommend if you go to go to skip those starters and head directly to the grills section which was amazing. The special traditional plates with lamb shank also looked great but we haven’t tried it ourselves. The service was lovely and the place itself is really nice and cozy. Baklava for dessert is super good! Not a fan of the saffron ice cream as it was condensed with rose water but the baklava on its own was lovely. They had vegetarian options as well for the mains and starters which is great!

This is a wonderful independent restaurant in the centre of Epsom. We were visiting Epsom for The Derby and wanted somewhere to eat afterwards. Our friends booked in here because they had been before. The restaurant were incredibly accommodating and let us pull our reservation forward by half an hour at very short notice. We were welcomed warmly and offered a choice of several tables, opting for mine outside. We had a variety of starters, including Hummus, Bruschetta, Turkish Sausage in filo pastry and Basque Sausage with Hummus. They were all incredible. The Hummus was so good I got some to take away. Main courses were mixed grill, Penne Arrabiatta and Sea Bass..Again all delicious, and generous portions. Service was very attentive, we really got the impression that the owners and staff would do all they could to ensure we had a great meal and experience. Wine was great, and the loos were clean! Highly recommend. This really was a little jewel and a great example of why we should support our independent restaurants. We wish we lived nearby.

I was REALLY looking forward to eating here. We took a 10min taxi from the city and it's quite an unassuming entrance from the street in a nice Georgian architectural area of the city. A warm, friendly welcome and pleasant enough surroundings. Excellent to offer an a la carte menu as well as tasting (my bestie isn't very adventurous beyond steak and chicken 🙄).  We chose from the ALC which was £89 for 3 courses, with a £5 supplement for sirloin steak main. The 3 amuse bouche, as is customary, from the kitchen were just ok. The bread was equally just ok. The two seeded rolls were dry bordering stale, not warm and certainly not baked fresh that day (or had been under a hot lamp). Scallop starter was ok, one King sliced into three with  few queens in a bisque sauce that didn't really taste as punchy as it could have. The sirloin was a total disappointment! Especially given the supplement. My slices had sinew, and it really was a very ordinary plate of food. The desserts were good, light flaky mille-feuille. The decaf coffee was delicious and I probably enjoyed that the most. The atmosphere was nice enough but the music was a bit dated. All the staff were very friendly and helpful, I was quite surprised when the bread crumbs were cleared that they were swept onto the carpet, and not onto a receptacle/hand. I left feeling disappointed and I wouldn't come again. When I'm lucky enough to eat at fine dining places I want to close my eyes and really taste all the flavours and textures dancing around. I only wanted to close my eyes for bed after this. My score was bordering 3.5/4.  Sorry!

The mussels are very fresh, but not as good as the one I ate at Southport last time, but for 10£. a large size of fresh mussels is pretty good. There are many types of seafood in the seafood pasta. In short, I think this restaurant is very good as a seafood restaurant and the price is not expensive. It deserves to be on my must-eat list in Liverpool. 2022: It was our first time going here and we didn't know what to expect, but honestly it's was mouthwateringly delicious. It seems Nepalese food likes to use mint a lot, which I very much love. It's similar to Indian food in a way, if I had to choose what it was closest too, but it's way nicer. The spice levels do range but each dish tells you whether it's mild, medium or hot and you can ask for it to not be spicy if you prefer. The price was actually well worth it, it wasn't expensive, for how fancy the restaurant and the food presentation was I expected it to be more, but actually it's not. The starters ranged between about £3-£8 depending what you got and whether you had the meat/fish starters. Mains on average were between £10-£15 and sides, such as the ghurka potatoes, bread and rice, which we had, were around £3. And on top of that you get free poppadoms and dips, amazing! The service was excellent and the servers were kind, caring and very prompt. Definitely one of my favourite restaurants, we'll be going back there soon for sure. Also to explain my pictures; one is of the side dishes, the ghurka bread, the ghurka potatoes, the ghurka rice, the last two both came with their own bowl of curry like dip. Another is my main, the lamb and chicken grill, it comes with what tastes like sweet pickled beetroot, carrot and cabbage in the middle. The last one is a picture of our starters, Nepalese dumplings (called momo) on the long black plater, they come with a curry sauce on top. Poleko chicken, which was so tasty I wish I had it as a main. Then finally tarkari or tarkeri, I'm not sure how to spell it but they were divine (also on our plates in the photo). They sort of tasted like a mix between an onion bhaji and a pakora but so much nicer and with veggies in the middle. I definitely recommend them but they are a little bit spicy, but in a nice way. Update 2023: We went back a year later and it's still just as amazing, the food was exceptional and as last time, the staff were so accommodating and friendly. Definitely would recommend trying here if you haven't! For the extra pictures; the orange sauce in the bowl with cream swirled in it was called lamb nauni gedi, I believe. It had lamb chunks which fell apart so easily and the sauce/curry was delicious. The next one kebab and chicken on the grill, with it's sauce. Then Gurkha bread. Then Rambache chicken, which is a starter. It was hot, but not too hot, and tasted to me like satay chicken minus the peanuts. It was gorgeous. The four crispy balls on the slate is called Tarkari Ghiu, something we got last time. They're mixed veg with spices in balls. And lastly, the picture of Poleko chicken on a black hot plate. Another repeat from last time.

restaurant_name: PUNJABI HEAVEN Restaurant - Indian Street Food
description: Update: we ordered a takeaway from here a few months after the below visit. It was delivered without the breads we'd ordered so we complained. It's good that the restaurant then eventually delivered the missing breads AND offered to supply new curries as well, which they did. My gripe, however, was the very high prices, for the naan and especially the roti (which is a glorified Chapatti - see photo) - yes, we paid slightly more for the order via Uber (an high £3.50 for the roti - see photo) but even the restaurant menu has exorbitant breads & rice prices. The curries were, to be honest, nothing special - and very oily (see photo where we tried to spoon off some of the oil or ghee), but the takeaway cost was nearly £50 for 2 curries, 1 rice, some okra, a roti and a smallish naan (inc slightly higher Uber prices + Uber fee). Won't be ordering again. Too expensive and nothing special. Sorry. Previous comment: We celebrated a double birthday on a quiet night. First of all, each dish was around £2 more expensive than the online menu so that needs updating! The food was excellent and the service responsive and quick. But the atmosphere was kind of weird? Staff standing around looking miserable and bored which I couldn't help noticing. I know it was a quiet night so not great for revenue, I suppose, but I couldn't help feeling that we weren't welcome? Not sure I'd return because of that - and the price hikes.

Amazing Seafood. My girlfriend and I visited Aquapod as a special treat and to celebrate a special occasion. We shared their mixed seafood platter which contained Lobster, crab, a whole sea bass, king prawns, mussels, clams, vegetables, potato wedges, and garlic bread. There was plenty to share and we really enjoyed it. A word of caution is that, as expected with eating shellfish like this, it does get messy and if you want the platter get a big table! The size of the platter also meant it cooled down quickly so some of it was only warm when we go to eating it. Not sure how that would be rectified however. Also, be careful of the crab legs. The method of cooking meant the hairy spines on the legs become very hard and sharp and stuck into our fingers. This was a minor issue (but worth pointing out to others). The restaurant was well presented and looked good, especially with the massive fish tank as a front window. We can’t comment about the atmosphere in their as we were the only people in the for the entirety of our visit (a quiet Tuesday lunchtime). But this was fine a we wanted it to be special for just us so probably worked in our favour. I feel that we will return and will try out some of the other dishes on the menu. Definitely a place to go if you like seafood. Parking: Paid multi-storey car park nearby. Very handy for here and the shops. (ParkBee Liverpool Central)

Our recent lunch at Aquapod Seafood Restaurant was an enchanting experience, blending the delightful nuances of exceptional seafood, an inviting atmosphere, and the charm of a lovely staff. From the moment we walked in, we were embraced by an ambiance that radiated warmth and sophistication. The decor, a perfect blend of coastal elegance and modern chic, set the tone for an unforgettable midday meal. The gentle hum of conversation, the clinking of glasses, and the soft melodies playing in the background created an atmosphere that was both lively and intimate. The seafood was nothing short of divine. Each dish was a testament to the chef’s mastery, bringing forth flavors that were both bold and delicate. The oysters were fresh and briny, the lobster succulent and sweet, and the scallops seared to perfection, melting in the mouth with an exquisite richness. Every bite was a celebration of the ocean’s bounty, prepared with a creativity and finesse that left us in awe. However, what truly elevated our experience was the impeccable service. The staff at Aquapod Seafood Restaurant were not only attentive and knowledgeable but also genuinely passionate about their craft. They guided us through the menu with enthusiasm, offering recommendations that never missed the mark. Their warm smiles and gracious demeanor made us feel like cherished guests, adding a personal touch that was deeply appreciated. In conclusion, our lunch at Aquapod Seafood Restaurant was a symphony of sensory delights. The stellar seafood, captivating atmosphere, and the wonderful staff created a dining experience that was both magical and memorable. We can’t wait to return and indulge in this oceanic paradise once again!

Booked this restaurant for Mother's Day and I'm so glad I did. The whole family really enjoyed the food, atmosphere, and the authenticity of the venue. . Located towards the to of Bold Street, near the church, the venue is in an excellent location and is competing with several other excellent restaurants that make Bold Street a real treat for foodies. There really is something for everyone and in my opinion it's one of the best streets in Liverpool. . On entering the restaurant we were greeted and seated and I immediately got the impression that the staff are professional restauranteurs with a passion for good hospitality. . The menu is vast but nothing complicated and the staff seemed very knowledgeable about the dishes and the cooking methods. Bring a meat house, steak is of course a big feature of the menu, however, there were plenty of alternatives to choose from too. . The beer on tap was great and the wine list catered for all tastes and budgets. . My youngest dined from the kids menu which was exceptionally reasonable and almost as large as an adult portion. Totally suited to older children as well as little ones. My meal was super and I really enjoyed the chicken and lamb kebab. It was perfectly cooked and really tasty. My wife and son both had steaks and loved them - had my kebab not been so tasty I would have been pretty envious. . In summary, I will definitely return and hope this is not in the distant future. One tip - we booked and I think this is essential. The restaurant was very quickly at full capacity and I can understand why.

The waiting time was extremely long. We ordered all at once, the starter took 35 minutes to arrive. We finished it (quite scarce for two) in a few minutes and then the meat took an extra 20 minutes. Waiting times are very long. The quality of the meat is not bad but nothing exceptional, for the price the restaurant has there are much better options in Liverpool. We were brought the bill and when we asked them to please remove the service charge as we found the meat extremely peppery (barely any meat flavour) and the long waiting time they became extremely rude with us and took quite a long time in bringing our bill again. Quite disappointed

My brother and his daughter who love everything Asian were equally impressed as this was their first time at a Korean BBQ restaurant. The host was great and very helpful so was the waiter very attentive too. The food was cooked perfectly squid very crisp without grease and the meats were great and easy to cook under the guidance of the host. She made sure everything was cooked properly and knew when to approach the table watching from the background. We will definitely be going back to taste more dishes next holidays. Also parking is easy if you park in the shopping centre car park and walk 5 mins to the restaurant.

I had came to little Tokyo because the owner from another drink company had requested me to try it out, so I did after so long. We was served really quickly, several customers inside the food wait wasn’t too long which is a good thing. Duck à la carte Pineapple no taste drench in water pulling all the natural pineapple juices Sweet and sour sauce is more like a Chinese plum sauce, mixed with dark soy sauce but it’s added extra extra sugar to it. Must eat with the rice Maki - Sushi rice itself not seasoned not even a little. You can taste the sushi rice was just boiled, could added some seasoning even a little compared to the sushi’s I’ve had in Leicester. Set A - curry was bland, I could make Japanese curry from the pre-made packets from the Asian supermarket store. It’s  tasteless curry sauce. Lots of veggies in it tho but a random large mushroom that should have been sliced preferably which is deep fried, and mushrooms shouldn’t be deep fried as it’s a sponge. Both the soy sauce for the box menus are very very little. It was like the chef was on a budget I had to dip from my other sushi’s that came with the dip Set C - The chicken was really small it reminded me of a smaller size of the Lidls chicken thigh that was fried and sliced. Overall, the portion size isn’t great for the price, if it tasted really good the portion size and the price wouldn’t matter. However, the price of alcohol is great nice and nice selection and the waiting time to the customer service was great no issues just the food itself. Vegetarian options: Lots of variety for vegetarian options.

restaurant_name: PUNJABI HEAVEN Restaurant - Indian Street Food
description: Visited on a Sunday evening, it is an Indian street style restaurant, it was busy which is always a good sign. The restaurant itself is quite small which is in keeping with the street kitchen feel. There's a good selection of dishes on offer. The onion bhajis were really nice and tasty. The Keema curry was served with peas which is the more traditional way of making, I do prefer with potatoes but still had a good level of flavour and nicely spiced. I would definitely return to try some other Indian cuisine.

Kayal Restaurant in Leicester is renowned for its authentic South Indian cuisine, particularly its specialties from the coastal regions of Kerala. Here are some key highlights of the restaurant: Cuisine: Kayal is celebrated for its traditional South Indian dishes, including dosas, idlis, seafood, and various vegetarian options. The menu features a wide range of dishes that highlight the unique flavors and spices of Kerala. Atmosphere: The restaurant's decor reflects the coastal theme of Kerala, creating a warm and inviting ambiance. The setting is designed to offer a comfortable and culturally immersive dining experience. A few things that need improvement or suggested changes . Please replace Chilli Paneer ( it was a tad too sweet - definitely not indo Chinese as suggested by the steward - a pretty sad preparation of what seemed like North Indian flavours in a shoddily prepared dish ) with an authentic Paneer 65 . The Papaddam platter was pretty sad - definitely not freshly fried - smell of reused oil. The South Indian Vadas also had a smell of used oil . The preparation of the cocktails needs improvement largely - though the choices on the menu are lovely but not the preparation. The wow factor was majorly in the starter grilled fish, the appams and the vegetable stew Vegetarian options: Nice options - loved the vegetable stew Parking: Parking is available in a lot just behind the restaurant - take the lane down

This was my very first visit to Chez Jerome, I visited with a friend and we were made very welcome. We sat at table no 1 in the window, which looked very Christmasy. We had a extensive menu to choose from. We both chose the festive 3 course menu.   I had smoked kipper for starter, my friend chose melon and prawn cocktail. Both were absolutely delicious. We were also served fresh baked small baguette type slices So tasty we finished the lot off! For our mains I chose salmon with seasonal vegetables, my friend chose duck also with seasonal vegetables.  The size of the meal was deceiving, there was plenty and we both struggled to get through it, again both were cooked to perfection. Dessert was an amaretto espresso coffee dessert followed by a lovely liquor coffee,I had TIA Maria and my friends had baileys. We also had a glass of water and I had a glass of rosé wine and my friend had a soft drink.  The price of the whole meal was very reasonable for what we had. We both thoroughly enjoyed it. My experience here for the first time was really good, I thoroughly enjoyed the atmosphere and we were made very welcomed. Thank you to the chef and owners of Chez Jerome and waitress for a great experience.

This place was fantastic! The food was great. There was good variety and everything was full over flavour. They used great ingredients particularly in the tomato and yellow bean sides. The spätzle was great, we had never tried it before but it was light and it held the sauce well. The bolognaise sauce was the best we’ve had in the UK, nice and rich. The Russian dumplings were also fantastic, small, crispy and would be ideal for snacking. We also ordered a second focaccia because the first one was so good and gone too quickly. The service was impeccable. The food is brought in waves with staff recommending which two dishes to bring at a time. It was a great way of eating because it meant the table wasn’t cluttered with lots of dishes and you could appreciate each dish on its own. We were served at various times by 6 different staff members but it wasn’t chaotic, the service just flowed perfectly with staff there when you needed and not bothering you while you were eating. All the staff were really warm and friendly too. The atmosphere in the restaurant was great. Despite the high ceiling it felt intimate but still vibrant. The price was very reasonable too. Overall it was just a perfect meal out.

It was a nice experience as a one off but we wouldn’t go back. The service was quite substandard. We waited almost 2 1/2 hours for five dishes and by the time the next one came, we were still hungry. I only one of the waiters and waitresses seemed happy. The rest didn’t seem that bothered. The asparagus special was amazing and one the best dishes I’ve had. That may be because we were really hungry and it was the first one we had though. It was also £18, which seemed very steep for five pieces. The dumplings were fine. Very fresh but the Dip with it didn’t do anything for it. Was nice to try the spatzle but for the prices, I wouldn’t be getting it again. The dessert was also very lack lustre and a nothingness. For £90 The atmosphere was fine. I didn’t like being able to look in the kitchen in the way that they framed it. It was all a bit too industrial. It seemed too much like a pop-up stall than a restaurant. The quality of the food was great and you could really tell a difference Compared to a normal restaurant standard. For £96 though which included one alcoholic drink, I think there’s probably better value elsewhere. I would recommend everybody try it at least once though and form their own opinion

When you have people who are plant based/vegan eaters in your party it's not often you can find a pizza place to satisfy, let alone a pizza place that is good....Purezza does both with its completely vegan menu aimed squarely at the pizza lover. Nestled on a corner in  the Northern Quarter, the airy interior gives a window onto the vibrant street life, a stones through from the Arndale Centre. We stopped by later lunch on a Saturday and we're seated straight away, quickly checking out the menu safe in the knowledge that everything on it was vegan. The pizzas were delicious and we ordered dips to enjoy every last bit of the crusts. We didn't have to wait long for our food, great to be able to watch the pizzas being made and fired in the pizza oven. Staff were friendly and courteous, will definitely be revisiting again. Vegetarian options: Menu is all vegan.

Wow ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ One of the best pizza places I’ve ever been to that beats places like Italy, New York - USA. The venue just on Main Street - Rothwell. Has a excellent car park only 1/2 mins away. It’s kept the building original features and is very cosy, however the tables are well spread out and not on top of each other. There’s a really good atmosphere and vibe in the place as soon as you walk in. Mind your head going upstairs (top tip). Service was excellent, swift order for food & drinks. Which was served probably about 10-12 mins later. Even though the team were a member down you wouldn’t of notice. The food (the important bit) you get the wow factor when your food arrives. Seriously filled the table! I had a Neapolitan pizza, wife calzone and daughter child’s pizza. We had to take a box home as we were very full. The quality of the pizza was fantastic, the wood burning oven makes the difference and the ingredients and dough are up there as the best you’ll get. It also does gluten free dough/pizza’s The menu is small, however this isnt a bad thing as there is plenty of choices including starters etc. Excellent beer choices too. We will be back ! The Blackburn family

You know you’re in for a treat when you enter the restaurant and see the amazing decor and know it will only get better when you take your place on a comfy seat at your table. First impressions are very important and the waiting staff at l’aquila do not disappoint, instantly getting to work to make sure your experience is a good one. And what an experience it is, from the barman presenting the wine bottle like we are royalty to the perfect presentation of the food! We shared a half and half garlic bread and the special prawn starter which were both immaculately presented and mouth-wateringly good. The ingredients were obviously fresh and if high quality as the taste exploded in your mouth. For mains we both chose a pasta dish and again both were such a delight! I took a gamble in trying the steak pasta as I’m not a huge steak fan but the strips of stake in my pasta were so tender flavourful I would recommend it to everyone! My husband went for a salmon and baby prawn pasta, which I took a little bite of, and what a ride of flavours! Each item in the dish had its own unique taste rather than blending into one which can happen with seafood dishes. Fresh and beautiful. Although we were certainly full by now it was so good that we couldn’t pass the opportunity to try the desserts, after a short break to settle the mains. Again, immaculate presentation of a rich but not sickly sticky toffee pudding and a beautiful, light crème brûlée. We ended the night with a special cocktail each, both with such unique flavours but gorgeous none the less. All in all it was a wonderful experience and I highly recommend l’aquila. I will certainly be going back!

A Gastronomic Delight at Black Friar Salford If you find yourself in Manchester with a craving for an unforgettable dining experience, Black Friar Salford must be at the top of your list. From the moment we walked in, the atmosphere was inviting, enhanced by the warm and friendly greetings from both the staff and host. The menu boasted a diverse selection, ensuring there was something tantalizing for every palate. The service was impeccable. The waiting staff were not only knowledgeable but also eager to share their recommendations, making our choices much easier and more informed. The highlight was meeting the chef a friendly and personable individual whose passion for his craft was evident. His brief interaction added a personal touch that was much appreciated. We indulged in a three course meal, sharing several starters and desserts among us. Every dish was a masterpiece of presentation and taste. The whipped smoked cod roe crumpet starter was particularly memorable, its unique flavor and excellent execution make it a must try. For the main course, I had the pleasure of tasting Black Friar's famous pie arguably the best pie I've ever had, with perfectly textured pastry packed with a generous filling. My partner’s beef fillet and oyster mushroom cannellini were equally impressive, cooked to perfection and bursting with flavors. The side dishes, including truffle fries and peas a la francaise, were well executed with just the right amount of crunch. Dessert was another high point, with both the Salted Caramel Tart and the blueberry cheesecake leaving us delighted, though the tart was my personal favorite. The ambiance of the venue matched the quality of the food. The beautifully designed restaurant features an open kitchen and a terrace that transitions into a covered area, offering an intimate setting that caters to all preferences. The staff were consistently attentive, frequently checking in to ensure our experience was nothing short of perfect. Their friendliness and professionalism contributed greatly to our enjoyable vist. Overall, Black Friar Salford is a gem that deserves all the praise it can get. Whether you're a local or just passing through, this place guarantees an exceptional dining experience. I highly recommended!

description: So eaten at the Istanbul Grill for the Third time yesterday and we always give our honest experience of the restaurant, Cleanliness, food, drink, service etc. I have over 23,000,000 views and we honestly love Istanbul Grill in Radcliffe, We turned up on Sunday 24th March at 12Noon as the restaurant opened. We were warmly greeted and placed into a lovely booth, My Fiancee ordered a large glass of Red Wine 🍷 and I went for a pint of San Miguel(£6), My Fiancee really enjoyed her Full Bodied Red Wine, My pint of San Miguel was ice cold, Crisp and a really good pint. For Food we ordered 2x Lots of Three Plates of Tapas(£12 for 3 Dishes), We ordered the Mussels in a Tomato and garlic sauce(Also available in a cream White Wine sauce), Meatballs, Calamari(deep fried squid), Spicy Turkish sausage, Spicy chicken rolls, Garlic Mushrooms in a lovely garlic creamy sauce, We ordered some warm Turkish bread and steak cut chips. The Mussels were extremely fresh, Extremely tasty and the sauce was beautiful, The Meatballs weren't massive but they were so succulent and tasty, It was my first time trying Calamari but again the Calamari were extremely tasty, fresh, The Spicy Turkish sausage was juicy, meaty and slightly Spicy and very flavoursome, The Spicy chicken rolls were lovely, Crunchy roll with the chicken was another delicious dish, My Fiancee had the Garlic Mushrooms in the garlic and white wine sauce which she really, really enjoyed, The Warm Turkish bread was fresh, soft and came with Some lovely dips and the chips were very tasty, slight cajun spices which were again really nice. description: Visited for a big family meal, about 20 of us. The staff did amazingly well really attentive to us all. All the food came out on time and it was PERFECT. Thank you so much for looking after us all and making us feel special. 10/10 👍

I wish I could give the woman I talked to tonight 0 stars. I go to this place for roast beef sandwiches all the time. Tonight I ordered a pick up order with two sandwiches for my boyfriend and I and when we got them they were so rare to the point where I actually felt sick trying to eat them. I called to ask for a refund for only the two sandwiches and nothing else that I got and the woman who answered (claiming to be the owner which I do not believe) was so rude about it. Refused to give me any money back. She started by saying I can have 15% of my money back and then changed it to 10% so clearly it wasn’t a policy they were following. She said that I have to drive and “give her back her food” if I want a full refund. I said that was ridiculous to make a consistent customer especially drive all the way back 25 minutes just to get money back for what THEY messed up. We said they can definitely send the delivery driver which she said she can’t. Being in the restaurant industry I was genuinely so confused and shocked at how she handled the situation. So In reality  they could’ve given me like 16 dollars back for their disgusting rare food they gave me and I would’ve 100% gone back but instead they lost consistent business. Absolutely appalled.

I'm a self confessed curry-holic,  see my reviews from around the world. Firstly I ordered my food to be cooked with a reduced amount of ghee. My starter, chicken tikka with a bag of salad and pot of raita, the chicken was sitting in a pool of oil in the container! After careful decanting and patting with kitchen paper the food was moist and tasty. Main course of Chicken Pathia and a Keema naan with garlic and coriander. The ghee was leaking out of the lid, again upon removal I was presented with another accumulation of ghee on the surface. After more kitchen paper the food was very good, tasty and a depth of flavour, mild amount of heat and delicately balanced by coriander. Only one piece of chicken in the dish was hard, but still edible (the rest was nice and moist). The base of the naan bread was slightly over but still that's better than being under. Overall very friendly staff and reasonable prices for good tasty food. Go and enjoy yourself!

I've eaten here a couple of times now. The first time was pretty decent, but this most recent experience has left me feeling squeamish. Walking in with a friend, we were promptly seated and asked if we wanted some poppadoms for starters.  Nodding enthusiastically, these were delivered promptly with dips.  The usual spicy tomato dip was possessed no spice and literally tasted of passata,  the yoghurt dip didn't taste right either, like cheese as if it had gone off. Amongst my poppadoms, I also found a dark beard? Hair. My friend had  had a rough day, so I didn't say anything as she seemed to be enjoying herself, so I pushed these things aside. Next, I ordered crab claws and tilapia for the main. The crab meat was tasty with dashes of mint, and the main fish was cooked well and a decent portion. My friend had ordered a fish curry , and the fish tasted fried and added in latterly to the sauce. Overall this most recent experience would not have me rushing back.

We came here by chance as we had reservations elsewhere but the fire alarm was going off for 30mins and we were starving. We did have to wait outside for 10minutes and then also move tables when a bigger group came in as it was a busy Saturday night but honestly we didn't mind as they seated us last minute. We are SO glad we came here instead - the food was out of this world, the chef was so welcoming and helpful, we are both vegans and they have a dedicated vegan/veggie menu and honestly it was some of the best food I've ever eaten. He even took our orders personally because the wait staff were so busy, so we never waited too long for a drink or our food. The Vegan Chicken Pepper Fried starter is made with the chef's own Seitan and I can't recommend enough - if you like good food, great Indian food, amazing vegan food or just the best onion Bhajis you've ever had, hit this place up. The ONLY criticism is that it took 15/20 minutes to pay because they were so busy, but that's such a small thing it was barely worth mentioning. Dietary restrictions: Vegan Menu (on website)

I come here quite regularly to order take-outs and not gonna lie the food is always amazing. For a Vietnamese restaurant they surely do well on the basics - Pho, chargrilled meat, spring rolls etc but what surprises me is the super delicious noodles with fish/ fish cake and the fried ice cream that I've never found anywhere else in the UK. Oh and the Bo luc lac (shakeing beef) is probably one of the best beef dishes I've ever had. Price is very reasonable, only less than £13 for a main dish that can already fill you up. Also very quick with take outs (I often wait for like 5 - 10 mins). Nothing to complain really.

I recently visited a Vietnamese restaurant that had a really homely feel to it, and I have to say, the food was absolutely amazing. One dish that stood out to me was the rice noodles with grilled pork. The meat was well-marinated and had an amazing taste, and the sweet and sour sauce really complemented the pork and noodles. It was a dish that left me feeling satisfied and wanting more at the same time. Another standout dish was the coconut sizzling hot plate beef. The beef was tender and cooked to perfection, and the sauce had just the right amount of coconut to give it a unique and delicious flavor. It was a dish that really hit the spot and left me feeling extremely satisfied. I also tried the rare beef pho, which had an amazing soup base that was heart-warming and comforting. The beef was cooked just right and added to the overall deliciousness of the dish. Finally, I have to mention the salt and pepper chicken wings. These were perfectly marinated and fried, leaving me wanting more even after I had finished my meal. The flavor was amazing and the texture was just right. Overall, this Vietnamese restaurant exceeded my expectations and I highly recommend it to anyone looking for some amazing Asian cuisine. The homely feel of the place, combined with the amazing food, made it a memorable experience that I won't soon forget.

So eaten at Campo Blanco Today for the Second time in the last few years and honestly the standards are even better than they were before. So we booked last minute and luckily Campo Blanco had space to accommodate the 4 of us so we were warmly greeted by the waitress and seated in the restaurant. We were given a few minutes before the waitress took our drink orders, My Fiancee ordered a large glass of Rioja, I ordered a cold crisp pint of Cruz Campo, Our daughter ordered a half pint of Cruz Campo and our other daughter ordered a pint of coke with ice. A few minutes later the waitress came back and we were ready to order Food so we decided on Mixed olives to start with a selection of bread with olive olive, Balsamic vinegar and garlic alioli then for mains we ordered several plates of Tapas we ordered Fish Tacos, 2x Chorizo in red wine, Salt aged Pork, 2x Chilli king prawns, Mussels in wine wine sauce, Sweet potato and halloumi, Chilli chicken, Slow cooked Lamb Harissa, meatballs etc. Food was absolutely fantastic, Great selection of Tapas, Fantastic tasting mixing meat with spices etc it all went together really well and portion sizes were generous, as busy as the restaurant was the service was fantastic, Attentive staff. The pint of Cruz Campo was crisp and ice cold, The wine really complimented the food and the whole experience was fantastic. Bill Total for 4 of us with starters, Drinks and countless portions of Tapas with Tip was £134 We like to support local businesses and we can't recommend Campo Blanco highly enough. There is a small car park round the back. 5☆

The lamb was incredibly tender, and the sauce was rich and flavorful. Although I would have preferred it a bit spicier, it was still exceptionally delicious. It seems that her earlier aversion was simply due to not knowing what to order. This restaurant has certainly changed her perception, and she is now eager to explore more Indian dishes. Overall, the consistent quality and flavors of this place have made it a favorite of mine

restaurant_name: Bardez - Indian Street Food and Grill- Rusholme
description: This restaurant deserves a lot of credit! Hats off to the Owner, Markus, for creating and running such a fantastic establishment on Wilmslow Road. “The Curry Mile” is running out of decent Curry restaurants but I’m glad that Bardez exists. It is 100% a must try. The restaurant atmoshpere was great with good music in the background. We ordered Pani Puri Shots, Seekh Kebab and Chicken Manchurian for starters. They did not disappoint! Great portion sizes for the price! They were a little bit spicy for the Mrs but, it meant there was more for me. For mains, we ordered the Lamb Dum Biryani. A good Biryani is hard to come by these days, they use lamb and not Mutton like some local competitors and it was sublime. The meat was tender and the rice was very flavourful. We also ordered Chicken Handi with tandoori roti (a chicken curry) which again tasted amazing. Only critiques were that it was a little bit spicy for the Mrs again (she can handle moderate heat) it may be worth the waitresses asking what spice we would prefer, if this is an option. Aditionally we would have loved a few more pieces of chicken in there as it tasted so good, we wanted it to last a little longer! Nonetheless we enjoyed every single bite. We spent roughly £50 and we would 1000000% would return again, and may even try their restaurant in Didsbury. The owner, Markus, was extremely friendly and personable when we got to talking with him. Truly another hidden gem on Wilmslow road.

restaurant_name: Bardez - Indian Street Food and Grill- Rusholme
description: Followed the Google reviews and few other recommended lists to here for some food Sunday lunch time. Quite quiet so difficult to fully judge the atmosphere (hence the 4 stars) but friendly and attentive service with great food to accompany. Witnessed them at the pass prior to serving customers  ensuring the food was well presented, cutlery was replaced between courses and everything was done with a smile. We had a couple of versions of chaat to share for starters the individual mains, sticking down the Indian route even though they offer an indo-chinese fusion (or menu options). Had to go with the biryani as this seems a reoccurring theme in the reviews, chose the dum lamb option - it was both amazingly tasty and substantial. Thought there was way I'd be finishing it but kept wanting more, even forgot to take a picture til it was nearly all gone. Added to the list of places to revisit.

We had a good time ordering our meals and chatting and we realized the kitchen is still visible from the restaurant, which is very nice. So we were just watching how the chefs made our food as we were the only customers at that moment, I was certain it was for us. Everything went well until it was time to make sushi. One chopping board, for everything. Vegetables, raw fish and meat! And no gloves, no hand washing in between. I will give some more stars for trying to improve hygiene and cleanliness!
