🍽️ Just dropped by Vesuvius Restaurant and here's the lowdown: - 🇮🇹 Ambiance: Stepping into Vesuvius is like a time travel to old-school Italy. Everything has a really vintage touch. It’s not exactly my cup of tea as I lean towards more modern settings, but it's got character! - 🤔 Service: Had a bit of an odd experience. The waitress seemed a tad unsure, not even asking for our booking name. Made me wonder why we booked in the first place. - 🍞 Food: The garlic breadsticks came in a packet, which was unexpected. I reckon serving them out of the packet might add a touch of freshness! The menu choices and the dishes themselves were a bit basic for my taste. However, the roast potatoes were a hit - not sure how Italian they are, but delicious nonetheless! Tried a bit of the carbonara and found it a bit bland. - 🍴 Overall Vibe: The place was buzzing for a Friday night, which was nice to see. Rating: 4/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐ It didn't quite hit the spot for me, and while I might not head back on my own initiative, I'm open to giving it another go if someone else is keen.

What a discovery - authentic Italian food here in Maidstone! Our first visit to Vesuvius and it certainly won't be our last. Thank you to Alessandro, his partner and team, who have created something unique in Maidstone. Having enjoyed traveling in Italy, we love Italian food. Vesuvius doesn't only serve fantastic food but the atmosphere inside feels like a little bit of Naples right here on our doorstep. Our food choices included aubergine, seafood, and steak, which were delicious. With the steak, the recommended wine was Gragnano, a sparkling red served chilled, imported from a spot close to the foot of Mt Vesuvius itself. It paired perfectly with the steak - an enjoyable surprise! The dessert menu was another thing too - my wife is a bit of a tiramisu expert, having tried many throughout Italy, and was delighted. For me, the hot dark chocolate pudding with white chocolate inside... Safe to say, we're looking forward to our next visit! ... updated a few visits later and I have one word to add: panettone!!

With the steak, the recommended wine was Gragnano, a sparkling red served chilled, imported from a spot close to the foot of Mt Vesuvius itself. The food here is 5 star. As a table of 7 we sampled a variety of what was on the menu. 4 of us had Pho, and we're all in agreement that it was some of the best Pho we had ever had. In terms of starters, one of the group got through a sharing platter for 3 on their own. It was busy when we went, and despite having pre-booked, it was quite evident that a different group of 6 had been recently seated at our table, as there was only a table for 6 remaining for us (and a separate table for 2). We were moved to a table to accommodate all of us before the food arrived, but it spoiled the start of the meal. Due to the confusion, staff were also slow to take a drinks order. The staff were friendly, and I am sure that if you go when it is less busy the service would be fine. But, in this instance the service nudged the overall experience to a 4 star, rather than a 5 star review that the food really deserves.

If you're like me and don't rate the chain PHO, come here to get your Pho fix. We wanted to order the BBQ grilled quail, but they ran out, so instead we shared the prawn summer roll starter (£6.80), very fresh and refreshing. I had the Bún cá cay (Spicy fish noodle soup, £13.80). Unfortunately they ran out of fish cake, so replaced this ingredient with prawns. The flavour was decent and amount of noodles given was plentiful, would've preferred if there was more seabass and of course fish cakes. Tofu was fried to good ol crisp level. Fiancé had the Bún bò giò heo (Traditional homemade pig trotters Bun Hue, £12.80). Very flavourful, right level of spice, a lot of meat and very filling. Lemon Grass Tea and Peach Ice Tea (£4.00 ea) again were really refreshing, tasted freshly made rather than poured from a can or bottle.

The service, ambience and rooms are very very good. However, the food, whilst beautifully presented, did not hit all the high points for my palate. Some really excellent dishes, "from the embers" was outstanding along with the "wagyu peppercorns". But for me, the beautiful smoked eel was totally overpowered by the truffle sauce and both of us found the salmon wrapped in seaweed left an odd taste in the mouth. It was lovely to retire outside into the beautiful wooden hut after the meal and indulge in lovely chocolate and coffee. Breakfast the following morning was superb. You have to admire the work and techniques involved in presenting a unique foodie experience.

I was excited to be Invited to what only can be described as the best culinary experience I'd ever had & tasted.. Nottingham based 2* Michelin Sat Bains Restaurant.. from the moment you pulled up on the gravel drive, greeted most hospitably at the door, served fine chianti wine 🍷 then led to your table, beautifully set & and well-dressed, attired waitresses & waiters. The food served, looking like pieces of art & the incredible passionate work making it. Fully described by our hosts, the ingredients, the inspiration & locally sourced products, some coming from their own garden too, made this 10 course menu more special. The difference in taste & texture, the taste buds fireing on all cylinders, the explosions of white ice cream that melted instantly as you snapped on the honeycomb wafer. The lamb that was pink yet braised with crispy potatoes & light garden leaves & garlic roasted with an AuJus that brought everything together. Bursting with flavour, texture & crunch. The work gone into tonight's treat was pure heaven. Thanks to all at Restaurant Sat Bains, a truly wonderful experience & one to be treasured for sure. Highly recommended folks. 😋👍🍷✨️

No on site parking g and most of the streets around have permit parking so it is a little tricky but there are some spaces to be had not far from the front door.

His knowledge of the menu and thoughtful recommendations ensured that our meal was both memorable and satisfying. Chak Dhoom is undoubtedly one of the best Indian restaurants I’ve visited in the UK, and I highly recommend it to anyone seeking a genuine Indian dining experience. This restaurant is a true gem in Newcastle, and I look forward to returning soon.

I tried the lamb mandi and the lamb mixed grill. The standout feature of both dishes was the quality of the meat. The lamb in the mandi was particularly impressive, with a generous portion size, especially for such an affordable price. In the mixed grill, I especially enjoyed the lamb ribs and cubes. On my next visit, I’ll definitely be ordering the lamb ribs again. To finish off the meal, I treated myself to Kunafa, which was very tasty. The ice cream on top complemented it perfectly. Overall, it was a nice experience, and I look forward to returning.

What an amazing restaurant! The family are so warm and welcoming,the restaurant is beautifully decorated and the food is out of this world! With typical Lebanese hospitality and affinity with food, the portions are  enormous and everything cooked to perfection. The menu is vast so  it took some time for me to decide what to have; I opted for the Maklooba Aubergine Chicken as it was something new to me. Oh my, it was so good! It arrived on a serving dish in a huge upturned bowl so that when this was removed the food was eye catching - a mini mountain of chicken, aubergines and other vegetables on rice, accompanied by  yoghurt and cucumber dressing and a spicy sauce. The meal was rounded off with a cup of sweet tea and sweet treat, complimentary. I don’t visit Newcastle very often but I shall certainly be going back to this restaurant the next time that I do! As a lone diner I felt very comfortable eating there. Highly recommended!

What an amazing restaurant! The family are so warm and welcoming,the restaurant is beautifully decorated and the food is out of this world! With typical Lebanese hospitality and affinity with food, the portions are  enormous and everything cooked to perfection. The menu is vast so  it took some time for me to decide what to have; I opted for the Maklooba Aubergine Chicken as it was something new to me. Oh my, it was so good! My only criticism would be that maybe the green walls could be decorated more because otherwise they're quite bland. Expensive but not too expensive, and besting in quality some other places in Norwich (haven't tried Shiki yet). I've seen that they offer lunch menu for a decent price; definitely worth having it if you're in town between 12:00 and 14:30. Vegetarian options: Vegetarian sushi and other dishes with vegetables instead of fish; cucumber and avocado for example, or omelette.

Absolutely loved this place. A real hidden gem in the centre of Norwich. Feeling spontaneous on a Friday evening. I called half an hour before to see if they could accommodate my wife and I for dinner. The staff were very helpful and friendly and they managed to squeeze us in at the last minute. The food is absolutely amazing and very reasonably priced. We opted to share a mix of various small plates and everything was delicious, well presented and served promptly. The drinks offering is decent so my wife opted to try a glass of the Plum wine while I stuck with the familiar Sapporo. We were so blown away by the plum wine we decided to share a bottle. It is the perfect drink to have whilst savouring the delicate flavours of the food, a wonderful balance of dry, sweet, tangy and fresh. The staff were exceptionally friendly and efficient. We will be returning again in the very near future.

It has been a couple of years since we last dined here, so when our friends invited us along to celebrate a birthday we jumped at the chance. We opted for the full taster menu with the wine pairings, and boy did we have a superb meal! From the amuse bouche to the final dessert, everything was absolutely delicious.  Particular standouts were the sherry mousse (always a favourite), the Gressingham duck and the megrim sole. Service was impeccable as always, the staff here really know their stuff and are happy to answer any questions on the dishes or wine.  It is just nice to enjoy food to this high standard in a restaurant that doesn’t require you to be overly formal. Thank you Team Benedicts!  Hopefully it won’t be so long before we’re back again.

A couple in our hotel described Benedicts as "expensive". I'd argue it isn't, for what it has to offer. First, 61GBP for a 6 course set menu is pretty standard. They are also very accommodating. We aren't big drinkers, so we asked to split accompanying wines in two, to try them out, but not to drink too much. And we did the same with cheeses. We wanted to try everything, but to be frank, their main dish was quite big, compared to other restaurants with set menus, where sometimes you get a single piece of meat. All in all, very friendly service, not a single dish I would consider to be weak, and a very reasonable price for that.

We took our parents here every time they visited Norwich. Even I tried to bring them to different new places over the years, Jorge’s still remains as their most favourite restaurant. This place sometimes got very busy, sometimes a bit more relaxed, but either way the quality of food and service are always at such a high standard and consistency, not even once we were let down. This is just amazing. Seafood and fish Cataplana is our all time favourite. Simple and delicious, very heart warming in the winter. The new black bean rice on the menu (served along side with pork) is also very nice which added a more diverse flavour profile to the meal mainly consists of seafood and meat grill. They are expanding their desserts menu too. Pao of cheese with cheese ice cream is a must try, very nice balanced sweet and savoury from the smooth ice cream and fluffy cake. Selection of wines is nice. Vibrant and joyful. Just like their services. We just feel happy every time we see the staff. Thank you for bringing such great experiences to us!

This place deserves all 5 stars for everything! We wanted something special for our Anniversary and they certainly didn't disappoint. We were made to feel welcome as soon as we walked through the doors. They took our jackets, while we sat in the bar area for a drink. The mojito, was beautifully presented, with a little vanilla bubble, and coconut dry ice! We chose black pudding and belly pork, and beetroot and goats cheese for starters, these were amazing. Seafood linguine and chicken for main courses, again perfectly cooked, and very tasty. Desserts, sticky toffee pudding and the mango cheesecake were delicious. The restaurant was cosy, clean, and we requested a table under the "tree". The staff were lovely, attentive, pleasant and the little extras were rather special too. Thank you to all the Banches team for making a night to remember, highly recommended for a special meal out. Hope to see you again soon.

Second time visiting Namaste. The place is entirely vegetarian so don't be misled by the "chicken" and "prawn" on the menu. They're plant based alternatives. The chicken is really nice and the prawns are king prawn shaped and have the same texture although they don't have a lot of taste. That doesn't matter though 'cos all the flavours come from the curry they're in which is great. If you like a bit of spice, choose a dish that's one down from the "Indian hot" (I haven't been brave enough to go for one of those yet 😁). The milder dishes were just too mild for me. The menu clearly states any allergens and the servers ask about any specific dietary requirements. Decent portions, very friendly staff. No parking on site but there's the Queen's road pay and display car park directly opposite. I didn't see a wheelchair accessible entrance, there are a couple of steps into the building. Will definitely go again. They also do takeaway.

Popped in for lunch, we were the only people in, but its midweek in January so not massively unexpected. The food was great! Really really tasty, hot, fragrant and fresh, if I'm honest, I felt it was a touch on the pricey side, but I understand the rising food and utilities costs are starting to trickle down to the customer now, they're definitely not over priced, but it's not a cheap lunch. We had a curry, a rice, a selection of breads and a Dosa, the Dosa wasn't very hot, temperature wise, not sure if this is how it's meant to be served or not. My only gripe about the meal is that they add a 12.5% service charge on to the bill, I feel this is a bit of a liberty, especially when it's a party of 2 and we were the only guests, I was happy to tip as the service was fine, but to automatically add it to a bill leaves a bit of a sour taste.

First time going to a Japanese restaurant and it was amazing! The food I had were: - Dumplings (first time having them and they were very nice). -Fried squid (surprisingly chewy but tasty). -Chicken Ramen : The soup was like chicken soup mixed with a hige amalgamation of herbs and spices. The noodles were very fine, tender and addicting to eat. The chicken itself was full of flavour and cooked very well. For someone who is not that much of a fan of big, steamed veg - this dish made me want to eat all my onions and sweet peppers. -I had a little sake, and it honestly tastes like if someone made Lambrini stronger and with a hint of wheat (which someone makes sense since it is a "rice alcoholic beverage". On top of that : -Beautiful paintings -a beautiful restaurant with japanses ornaments -very good staff -beautiful Japanese-style cutlery and plates... ... All add up to one MAGNIFICENT restaurant for either yourself, or a little group to go to.

The primary goal of any restaurant that claims to be a higher end eatery in the middle of a city centre should be the quality of its food, but sadly, that's where the calcutta club fails. First of all, the portions are tiny, and I mean, tiny. They come in either very large size dishes with a minute amount of food or a tiny bowl that's filled to the brim that wouldn't even fill a growing  child. We were a hungry group of 4 and ordered the following: Starters Chicken platter Vegetarian platter Amrtodari fish Mains Chicken Rogan Josh Punjabj Karahi chicken Lamb biryani Paneer karahi Sides Garlic naan Peshawar naan Tandoori roti Plain naan Pilau rice Desserts Gulab jamun with pistachio kulfi One Indian tea The starters were piping hot, juicy and flavoursome with spice and garnished well. So expectations were high. The mains were spiced well but not enough to share, let alone fill a stomach. The meat and chicken has all been pre-boiled and then thrown into masala to disguise it's damp, limp-wristed flavour. The rice was not long-grain basmati, which for ANY Indian restaurant owner or frequentir will tell you, should be a punishable offence. Then there's the prices. The average main here costs around 15 pounds and sundries like naan and rice cost £4 to £5 EACH! The Desserts cane and I couldn't bring myself to even try it. I sipped on the authentic tea which... wasn't. The service was good. The manager greeted us on entry, took our coats and we were promptly shown to a table.The service team themselves were polite, professional and knowledgeable and seemed to know the menu. £155 for 4. That's about £39 each for what was  spectacularly average fayre disguised in authentic settings. If this is what passes for a decent curry house.here in the East Midlands, well let me tell you Nottingham, you have MUCH to learn and see.

I recently had the pleasure of dining at The Calcutta Club, a charming curry house nestled in the heart of Nottingham, From the moment I walked through the door, I was greeted with warm hospitality by the owner and an inviting ambiance that set the tone for a delightful culinary experience. The menu at The Calcutta Club is a testament to the rich diversity of Indian cuisine. It features an extensive selection of dishes that cater to both traditional tastes and modern palates. I started with the classic Chicken Tikka, which was perfectly marinated and grilled to succulent perfection. The spices were balanced beautifully, providing a hint of heat without overwhelming the palate. For the main course, I opted for the Lamb Rogan Josh, a dish that truly showcased the chef's expertise. The lamb was tender and infused with aromatic spices, simmered to create a rich, flavorful sauce. Paired with fluffy basmati rice and freshly baked naan, it was a meal that was both satisfying and memorable. Vegetarian options are also abundant and equally impressive. The use of fresh ingredients and traditional cooking techniques was evident in every bite. The Calcutta Club also offers a variety of beverages, including refreshing lassis and a well-curated selection of wines and beers that complement the spicy dishes perfectly. The lassi, in particular, was a delightful treat, providing a sweet and tangy contrast to the savory mains. Service at The Calcutta Club was impeccable. The staff were knowledgeable and attentive, ensuring that each dish was served promptly and at the perfect temperature. They were also more than happy to provide recommendations and accommodate any dietary preferences or spice level adjustments. In terms of ambiance, The Calcutta Club strikes the perfect balance between cozy and elegant. The decor is tastefully done, with traditional Indian motifs and modern touches that create a welcoming environment. Soft lighting and comfortable seating make it an ideal spot for both casual dinners and special occasions. Overall, The Calcutta Club offers an exceptional dining experience that goes beyond just great food. It's a place where flavors come alive, and every meal is a celebration of Indian culinary heritage. Whether you're a curry enthusiast or new to Indian cuisine, The Calcutta Club is sure to impress with its authentic dishes, superb service, and inviting atmosphere. I would definitely highly recommend this Curry house

First, authentic Indian cuisine is my absolute most favorite food! Wherever I go in the world I seek it out. Having partially grown up in Wales and visiting it again now, I truly miss the Indian restaurants that were here 20-30+ years ago. Those were the restaurants where you had fresh chicken and lamb, sauces where you could taste and see whole spices like bay leaf, cinnamon, cumin, green chilis, cloves and cardamoms. This restaurant has none of that authenticity of true Indian cuisine. We ordered chicken tikka masala(very thick fruity red sauce) and chicken bhunna. We wanted a lamb bhunna but they said we couldn’t as the only lamb dish was lamb tikka.  The chicken bhunna was frozen chicken, no fresh Indian spices, and oily and sweet. The chicken tikka masala was super thick, very red, no detectable spices, and frozen chicken. The Naan bread was more like an over cooked cracker and hard. The pilau rice was very colorful but lacked any aromatic qualities and no spice at all. the lamb samosas were frozen packets of fried meat. I was underwhelmed and very disappointed. You have to buy the poppadoms and chutneys. Lastly, they do not serve any alcoholic beverages but you can BYOB.

I had a bit of a wait for my train at Newport station so went to find something to eat. Looking on Google maps, Taste of Asia was only a five minute walk away and slightly out of the town centre but was well worth a visit! I told them I had a train to catch and they got the food out to me in good time which was very good of them. I went for onion bhaji which were lovely, crisp, not at all oily and with a nice drawing and a fresh side salad . Lamb Dansak is my go to but they only served chicken or beef so went for the latter which was very good. It was to the spicier end of the Dansak scale but manageable and full of flavour. They don’t have a license so you would need to take your own beer etc. they die red my to a local convenience store and happily opened the bottle and provided a glass. The kitchen is open to the restaurant which is always good to see the chef at work, the staff were friendly and the look of the restaurant is very nice, contemporary but with some classic touches with the wood paneling. It was quite early when I went so was quite empty but there was a regular flow of take aways being collected which is always a good sign I think. Overall, The Taste of Asia was a very happy find and would happily go again next time I’m in the area!

I have read decent reviews about this restaurant and so we decided to give it a try for wifey's birthday. We pre-booked a table for a Saturday night and when we arrived there was a choice of 3 tables for two to choose from. We sat down and were handed the drinks menu. The first thing we noticed was the price. Very expensive, so we decided on small glasses of wine each. We ordered a garlic bread as a starter to share, which didn't taste of garlic, only the really cheap tasting cheese. Not pleasant at all. For mains I ordered the Penne con salsiccia affumicata e funghi, which was penne pasta with smoked Italian pork sausage, mushrooms, fresh peppers, onion & garlic in a homemade tomato sauce. My wife had the Spaghetti alla Carbonara, spaghetti with Italian pancetta & rich Italian cream sauce, finished with egg yolk & parmesan. Both were quite tasty, albeit on the very small side. The dessert menu is extremely limited with just three choices, so we had the tiramisu and a lemon cheesecake. Both were quite dry so my wife asked for some cream or ice cream, which was met with extreme confusion by the waitress and eventually she brought out a small jug of cream "that we use for cooking". Overall, the venue is very small, much like the menu choice and portions. It was all extremely expensive, with the bill for two coming to a few pence under £100. I have to say I am not sure why this venue has such great reviews.

So confused why this place is rated so highly? Food is bland, pasta didn’t taste fresh & all over-priced. The chef/owner came up and asked us at the end how it all was and asked if we’d come back again. I can’t lie so I said “no”. Fair play he was open to the feedback conversation, but it felt more like him justifying. He did own up to not putting a lot of cheese in a 4 cheese pasta dish - probably because Gorgonzola is expensive and cutting costs? Instead of fixing the bill there and then, he said “when you come back next time you’ll get free drinks”. How about you fix it now, if you’re going to offer? Food itself: 1/ 4 cheese penne - didn’t taste of cheese at all, more like a bland creamy sauce. 2/ seafood spaghetti - tomato sauce barely had any flavour. The chefs excuse was the sauce is meant to be simple. OK, but then it should be done perfectly? 3/ side dish of potatoes - super oily and again barely any seasoning 4/ garlic bread - no taste of garlic insight and no idea what cheese was used on it. 5/ veal tagliatelle - this was actually nice, probably because the veal helped release some salt & flavouring. Had to ask for salt & pepper, but that couldn’t save it. Service: unwelcoming/unfriendly waitresses. We realised we weren’t even told the specials after we paid the bill. Total for 4 people: £114, only had soft drinks. Very overpriced for what you get. We went and had dessert elsewhere 👌 — In their defence, they did ask if everything was ok during the meal. However, everything was so mediocre (except the veal) we’d have had to ask them to re-do it all if it came down to that conversation.

I had the pleasure of visiting La Terraza Tapas Bar in Upton with my kids, and I must say, it was a delightful experience. The ambiance was incredibly cozy and inviting, creating the perfect setting for a family outing. The friendly staff added to the welcoming atmosphere, making us feel right at home. The highlight of the meal was undoubtedly the tapas selection. The steak with chimichurri sauce was a burst of flavors that left us craving for more, and the Tempura prawns were simply delectable. It's clear that the chefs here take pride in their creations, as every dish we tried was a delightful journey for the taste buds. As a first-time visitor, I was thoroughly impressed by the overall experience, and I can confidently say it won't be our last visit. While the prices leaned slightly towards the expensive side, the quality of the food and the cozy ambiance more than made up for it. La Terraza Tapas Bar strikes the perfect balance between a gourmet dining experience and a comfortable family outing. I also appreciated the cleanliness of the restaurant, which is always an important factor for me when choosing a place to dine. All in all, La Terraza Tapas Bar offers a fantastic option for a memorable lunch with family or friends. If you're looking for a place that combines delicious food, a warm atmosphere, and a touch of elegance, this is definitely a spot worth considering. Dietary restrictions: Has gluten free bread

The “pan-Asian” restaurants of the UK are a crazy phenomenon that should be studied. I usually love when British Asian food is unabashedly inauthentic and my gripe with pan-Asian places is their dedication to the bit  of “authenticity” but then the food is just bland. AND YET Pan Pan pulled through. We just got a bunch of appetizers- the Korean fried chicken, crispy dump, aubergine, roti, Thai wings, ttobeoki (sp?) and they all slapped. Was the KFC as good as a Korean place in London? No. Did it hit The Spot? Yes.  Very yum and loved the variety. Wish they made the restaurant like 50% more bright in terms of lighting tho.

I had my lunch which was Indonesian Satay with beef and Oolong tea. The food was excellent,  exactly original Indonesian taste brought in a big portion together with a bowl of steam rice and a very fresh and tasty salad. Prices rather small according to the quality and quantityof food and great service 10+for the Chef. The server , Julia was extremely kind, helpful, professional,  smiling all the time. 10+ Inside is a nice music , not very loud, but exactly how it should be in a small cozy Asian food place. Very peaceful and relaxing. However,  it was the first time when I came to eat in this place. I walked inside, but I walked outside immediately to check the Korean pub on the opposite side of the road. Why? Because Pan Pan it doesn't look so great decorated from outside and I didn't trust it so much. I ve lived in Thailand and traveled in whole indochina for 20 years. I wanted an authentic taste of Asian food. So, I came back 3 min later because the other Korean pub was closed, so I didn't have a choice. And I didn't regret any second ! I felt absolutely great in Pan Pan! I recommend from whole my heart 💯 ❤❤❤❤❤ I ll come back at Pan Pan for sure. Pan Pan is not only a fake advertising, but for sure" The real taste of Asian Far East". Thank you, Chef, Julita and all Pan Pan staff for your brilliant work❤❤❤

Was staying in Oswestry for a couple of nights so I looked to see if there was an Indian in the town, & boy was I glad I did as the place is just amazing. There are plenty of tables but it was quite busy for a Wednesday night so it will definitely be busy on a Friday & Saturday so best to book. They have a great choice on the menu, plenty of speciality meals, starters, the usual meals like Kormas, masalas etc & a selection of rice's & naan breads. My husband had the tandoori chicken to start & that was delicious with good chunks of chicken. For our main we ordered a chicken curry, (sorry the name escapes me) with garlic rice and it really was soo good. The poppadoms were excellent too as not greasy but crispy & came with onions, mango, lime pickle & a spicy red one 😋 I have to say it was one of the best Indian meals I've ever had, I really couldn't fault it at all, I wish I lived local to it 👌 The staff are wonderful & extremely helpful, they have been in business for 45 years which says everything 😍

We recently visited Pompette to celebrate my husband's birthday and had a truly lovely experience. The sommelier and waiter were superb. We ordered the steak frites, which was quite good value. The steak was perfectly cooked and very flavorful. Our waiter was exceptionally attentive, always checking on us to see if we needed anything. Since we chose to sit outdoors, we appreciated the cozy blankets provided – exactly what I needed to stay comfortable. Overall, it was a wonderful dining experience, and we look forward to returning.

Wife and kids brought me here on my birthday after I said I wanted desi food with minimal fuss. This turned out to be the right place. At first, we walked in to the pub side by mistake, and I was massively disappointed thinking the place was a dive, but luckily we were guided to the restaurant side which was much nicer! It was very quiet when we were seated, we were the only diners there, but shortly a much larger and louder group came in, also celebrating a birthday by the looks of it. We were served by a young lady, (sorry, didn't catch her name). She was great, very friendly and talkative, and got everything right when we asked for specific things like asking to take the wings out of the mixed grill. She even came back to check and make sure the chef had done as she'd asked. The food was much better than I had expected, as I don't really hear about this place a lot these days. The mixed grill had a spicy kick to it which is just how I like it. We ordered a lot so we had to get it packed up, but we did finish it at home because it was so good. The only bad thing to say is that one of our plates had chips/cracks and one had a little stain on it, but we didn't make a thing out of it. Overall the experience was worthy of 5 stars. Vegetarian options: Plenty of options to satisfy my family who are all vegetarian. Dietary restrictions: We asked if their meat was halal or kosher when we booked, as I'm not permitted to eat these. We were told it isn't. Parking: They have a car park which is substantial, but it would be easy to park on a side road if it got too busy. Kid-friendliness: Had my 2 children with me and they were well catered for, and they enjoyed the place.

Easter Bank Holiday where to go. As most places closed. Which was good luck. In my job role I cover 35 - 50 pubs Hotels & restaurants per week. Algraves of Southsea Portsmouth.  Absolutely Glorious. Excellent service friendly staff from Manager to waitress to even the Chef coming out & asking about how was your food. Trust me alot of places could learn a lesson from the whole experience here at Algraves. Starters were great hot & Excellent size portions. Biggest chicken wings apart from being abroad I've ever had. The main? Well Algraves Special Paella.  This was enough for four people. Mussels / crevettes/ chicken/ half a lobster / chirozo in exceptionally tasty typical rice saffron flavours. Second main , Half a lobster again & steak cooked perfectly. Desserts as if there was room . A classic take on Banoffee pie. Large waffle ice cream caramel syrup & cooked Bananas. Then the classic Portuguese Chocolate cake.  Full of flavour.  Then on the house two lovely shots of Portuguese port. From the Staff. My only complaint is to staff. Food is priced too cheap. Compared to what I see at other places. I would highly recommend Coming here. Three components covered. Excellent hospitality Excellent  food Excellent prices. You must take a visit here.

To say this is an excellent restaurant is an understatement. It's one of the best restaurants in terms of food and atmosphere I've been in. The food is of such high quality and in turn taste produced to a high standard time after time. For me it's our go to place to eat when we really need a good slap up meal. The owner and his staff are very friendly and helpful. They offer some authentic Portuguese dishes alongside an extensive menu containing a dish for all tastes. The portions are large without being off-putting. We tend to share main meals between our party as to get a real taste of the menu. I would definitely recommend this but please call ahead and book before your visit, even mid week! *Edited review June 2021, original posted 2 years ago* *Edited review to add photos April 2024, review still stands*

I took my wife here for her birthday after stumbling across the menu online. We were not disappointed. I had tempura pork belly to start which was fatty heaven, really amazing and came with apple sauce and a sweet chilli dip. My wife had the crispy shredded lamb with houmous for starter and the Brazilian fish stew for main. Both were again excellent. I had the octopus for main and whilst it was very tasty, by the end of the meal I was a bit tentacled out. The tips were crispy and delicious and the thicker end was fairly soft but the middle was slightly chewy and with such a large portion, I couldn't finish it. I also don't think the sweet potato added much. I think crispy fries would have been a nice contrast. That said, I'd probably order it again in future but we'll be returning to try loads of other dishes first. For 2 x starters, 2 x mains, a beer, large glass of rose, a very nice bottle of Portuguese red and 2 x double Courvoisier's to finish, our bill came to £125 including a service charge. I was more than pleased with that. Service was very friendly and the atmosphere really nice and relaxed. It was quite busy by the time we left but not at all noisy as the background music was nice and low. I did give some feedback to one of the owners before we left and he seemed genuinely delighted to hear it. A future favourite and we can't wait to come back.

I had the octopus for main and whilst it was very tasty, by the end of the meal I was a bit tentacled out. The tips were crispy and delicious and the thicker end was fairly soft but the middle was slightly chewy and with such a large portion, I couldn't finish it. I also don't think the sweet potato added much. I think crispy fries would have been a nice contrast. That said, I'd probably order it again in future but we'll be returning to try loads of other dishes first. For 2 x starters, 2 x mains, a beer, large glass of rose, a very nice bottle of Portuguese red and 2 x double Courvoisier's to finish, our bill came to £125 including a service charge. I was more than pleased with that. Service was very friendly and the atmosphere really nice and relaxed. It was quite busy by the time we left but not at all noisy as the background music was nice and low. I did give some feedback to one of the owners before we left and he seemed genuinely delighted to hear it. A future favourite and we can't wait to come back.

The best Japanese Food I've had outside of Japan!! Took myself out here as a little self indulgent self date, and decided to engulge a bit and try some things I've not had before. I ordered the Miso Soup & Beef Yakitori as appetiser, with Fried Vegetables and Tofu as my main (would recommend having this with rice, as Japanese cuisine combines these. You have your carbohydrates as the rice essentially- I just wanted to have some space for more food since I've enjoyed, and do enjoy, expanding my pallette.) For pudding I enjoyed the Fried Green Tea Ice Cream with Fruit Salad, a truly interesting dish that I found myself enjoying. :) For drinks I had the Cherry Blossom Cocktail & Warmed/Hot Koshino Happo Sake. Very pleasant restaurant, and I strongly recommend it to anyone within the area. The staff are incredibly attentive and caring to your needs & the restaurant is comfortably sized- I'm surprised that it isn't that popular (I went on a Friday Night.) The only drawback I would say is it isn't particularly budget friendly- but if you have the money, or budget accordingly with what you can afford, it is an absolutely lovely dining experience with impeccable food.
